functions.funcDef: Provide propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (PRP §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans provide thrust for all phases of flight (§5.1.1).

functions.funcDef: Provide propulsive thrust for all phases of flight (PRP §5.1.1).
functions.subDef: Thrust reversers on the two inboard engines, inhibited in flight by WoW and radio-altimeter agreement (§5.1.2).

functions.funcDef: Deliver fuel to the four engines and APU at required pressure and flow, and manage fuel mass distribution (FUE §5.2.1).
functions.subDef: Store and deliver fuel to the four engines and the APU at the pressure and flow the engines require (§5.2.1).

functions.funcDef: Deliver fuel to the four engines and APU at required pressure and flow, and manage fuel mass distribution (FUE §5.2.1).
functions.subDef: Schedule transfer and cross-feed to hold centre of gravity and wing bending within limits (§5.2.1, §5.2.6).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers position for roll control (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: All-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators positions for pitch control (§5.3.2).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Split rudder in upper and lower segments, each with own actuation and hydraulic supply, sizes the engine-out directional case (§5.3.2, §5.3.3).

functions.funcDef: Position aerodynamic surfaces to provide control authority across the envelope including engine-out and blade-loaded cases (FCS §5.3.1).
functions.subDef: Double-slotted Fowler flaps in four sections and full-span leading-edge slats, driven by two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes (§5.3.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subName: Support aircraft and absorb ground loads
functions.subDef: Nose unit and six main bogies support the aircraft and absorb landing and taxi loads, spreading footprint pressure for semi-prepared surfaces (§5.6.1, §5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic retraction/extension on system A with free-fall alternate; uplocks/downlocks mechanically held, hydraulically released (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normally system B with system A alternate and accumulator-supported emergency braking; anti-skid per wheel pair (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Support and control aircraft on the ground
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on the ground, absorb landing/taxi loads, provide braking and ground directional control on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces (LDG §5.6.1).
functions.subDef: Hydraulic nose-wheel steering commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with mechanical disconnect for towing (§5.6.2).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Upward-hinging visor opened/closed hydraulically from system A with electric backup drive; cannot be operated in flight (§5.7.2, §5.7.6).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches on a common torque shaft plus eight locking pins on a separate supply; pressure interlock in series with unlock (§5.7.2).

functions.funcName: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in nose access to the hold and, when closed, form part of the pressure boundary (NZD §5.7.1). Structural load-path role of the door is treated as structure, not function (§5.7.3).
functions.subDef: Two dissimilar independently routed circuits sense lock; status displayed on flight deck and fed to take-off configuration monitor (§5.7.2, §5.7.4).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (CRG §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points are structure, not function (§5.8.3).
functions.subDef: Longitudinal restraint by two tension straps per saddle, tensioned by electric winches and locked mechanically; lateral/vertical by saddle geometry (§5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade and maintain restraint through all flight and ground load cases (CRG §5.8.1). Hold floor hard points are structure, not function (§5.8.3).
functions.subDef: Single instrumented tension loop; loss of tension on any strap annunciated in flight, two adjacent stations flagged as restraint condition (§5.8.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (ECS §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two air cycle packs on cross-bleed condition and distribute air to two separate zones, flight deck and hold (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold, and control fuselage pressure differential (ECS §5.9.1).
functions.subDef: Two digital controllers driving two outflow valves with pneumatic backup; independent positive/negative mechanical relief protects the structure (§5.9.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect aerodynamic surfaces and inlets from ice
functions.subDef: Hot bleed air protects wing leading edges and engine inlet cowls; stabiliser leading edges electrically heated in six independent zones (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subName: Protect probes and windshields from ice
functions.subDef: Probes, static ports, windshields and two ice detectors electrically heated and monitored individually (§5.10.2).

functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes for flight in the icing envelope (IPS §5.10.1).
functions.subDef: Two ice detectors of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage provide advisory detection and automatic activation (§5.10.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Four display units and two head-up displays driven by three display processors on dual networks; any unit can present any format (§5.11.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subName: Provide air data and inertial reference
functions.subDef: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data, two on main buses and one on DC essential (§5.11.2).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Independent integrated standby instrument on DC essential bus, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays (§5.11.2, §5.11.3).

functions.funcName: Provide flight-crew information and control interface
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting (AVI §5.11.1).
functions.subDef: Alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with procedures, on two independent channels (§5.11.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (FPR §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU, overheat detection on bleed duct runs and main gear bays, hold smoke detection at nine stations (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them (FPR §5.12.1).
functions.subDef: Two extinguisher bottles per engine pair cross-plumbed, independent APU bottle; hold has detection but deliberately no suppression (§5.12.2).

functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the following descent and diversion (OXY §5.13.1).
functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders on a common manifold with crossover feed four quick-donning full-face demand masks; sized for four occupants for the diversion time (§5.13.2).

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Loss of thrust from all four engines; aircraft cannot sustain flight and hull loss follows with no recovery credited by crew action.
fha.effCrew: Fatalities or incapacitation — crew aboard, outcome not recoverable.
fha.effPax: Aircraft is a freighter with flight crew only and unoccupied hold; multiple fatalities (crew).
fha.judgementNote: The SDD gives the one-engine-inop dispatch case and a mature-engine IFSD rate but does not state the all-four-engine loss outcome; I credited hull loss as not recoverable. A demonstrated glide/restart capability or an independent thrust source would move this — confirm against the propulsion architecture.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. The SDD gives the one-engine-inop dispatch case and a mature-engine IFSD rate but does not state the all-four-engine loss outcome; I credited hull loss as not recoverable. A demonstrated glide/restart capability or an independent thrust source would move this — confirm against the propulsion architecture. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust from all four engines cannot be recovered by crew action and results in hull loss. "A failure condition that would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — symmetric
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust available symmetrically; climb gradient and performance margins reduced but flight is sustainable with remaining engines and no asymmetry to control. Significant reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload managing degraded performance, diversion planning and thrust management.
fha.effPax: Freighter, flight crew only; no occupant injury expected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Symmetric partial thrust loss reduces performance margins without loss of control; the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of one engine. "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded change in thrust (increase or decrease) not matching crew command; if asymmetric, introduces a yawing moment the crew must arrest. Reduction in functional capabilities and control margins depending on which engine and magnitude.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to detect and counter the uncommanded thrust and re-establish the intended flight path.
fha.effPax: Freighter, flight crew only; no occupant injury expected in the credited outcome.
fha.judgementNote: Class turns on whether the uncommanded change is on a single engine (asymmetric, directional-control event) or affects thrust symmetrically, and whether FADEC protection bounds the magnitude; the SDD credits FADEC overspeed/overtemp protection but does not bound an uncommanded thrust excursion at the outboard moment arm. A large single-engine excursion at V1 could be more severe — confirm the credited magnitude and asymmetry.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Class turns on whether the uncommanded change is on a single engine (asymmetric, directional-control event) or affects thrust symmetrically, and whether FADEC protection bounds the magnitude; the SDD credits FADEC overspeed/overtemp protection but does not bound an uncommanded thrust excursion at the outboard moment arm. A large single-engine excursion at V1 could be more severe — confirm the credited magnitude and asymmetry. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded thrust change is detectable via engine parameter display and counterable; credited outcome is a significant reduction in capability with increased workload, arrested by the crew. "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of forward thrust — asymmetric
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Asymmetric thrust loss (one engine, notably an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm) produces a yawing/rolling moment; directional control must be maintained by rudder. This is the directional-control sizing case and the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome. Significant reduction in functional capabilities and margins.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to maintain directional control, manage the asymmetry and plan a diversion.
fha.effPax: Freighter, flight crew only; no occupant injury expected in the credited outcome.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Single-engine asymmetric loss is the design directional-control case with sufficient rudder authority retained and continued flight to a suitable aerodrome; credited outcome is a significant reduction in margins with increased workload. "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Engine responds erroneously to the crew thrust command (wrong magnitude or direction of thrust relative to command); if it produces asymmetry it is a directional-control event, otherwise a performance/handling degradation. Reduction in functional capabilities depending on which engine and the error.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to recognise the mismatch between command and response and to re-establish the intended thrust and flight path.
fha.effPax: Freighter, flight crew only; no occupant injury expected in the credited outcome.
fha.judgementNote: Class turns on whether the erroneous response is asymmetric (single outboard engine, directional-control event) and how large the error is versus command; the SDD does not bound the FADEC command-error case. A large single-engine erroneous response near V1 could raise the class toward Hazardous — confirm the credited magnitude, asymmetry and FADEC command-integrity protection.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Class turns on whether the erroneous response is asymmetric (single outboard engine, directional-control event) and how large the error is versus command; the SDD does not bound the FADEC command-error case. A large single-engine erroneous response near V1 could raise the class toward Hazardous — confirm the credited magnitude, asymmetry and FADEC command-integrity protection. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous thrust response is annunciated by the command/response mismatch on engine parameter display and counterable by the crew; credited outcome is a significant reduction in capability with increased workload. "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: No thrust reverser assistance during the landing roll; ground deceleration reverts to wheel braking, which is the primary means. Against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement with ~1,080 m predicted rollout, this is a slight reduction in functional capabilities on a normal-length surface but consumes stopping margin on a contaminated/short surface.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in workload — crew manages the landing roll on wheel braking alone and monitors remaining distance.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew only aboard.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the 1,800 m/~1,080 m margin and available wheel braking hold on the semi-prepared/contaminated surface such that loss of reverse thrust stays within stopping margin; if landing-distance analysis shows reverse thrust is credited to meet the 1,800 m requirement on a wet/contaminated strip, this rises toward Major. Confirm from LDG braking-degradation and performance analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes the 1,800 m/~1,080 m margin and available wheel braking hold on the semi-prepared/contaminated surface such that loss of reverse thrust stays within stopping margin; if landing-distance analysis shows reverse thrust is credited to meet the 1,800 m requirement on a wet/contaminated strip, this rises toward Major. Confirm from LDG braking-degradation and performance analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reverse thrust is a supplementary decelerating means; wheel braking (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) is the primary and remains available, and predicted rollout (~1,080 m) sits well inside the 1,800 m requirement. Effects amount to a "slight reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2). Other phases: reverse thrust is not used, and in-flight deployment is inhibited, so loss of the function has no effect outside landing (NSE); this row carries the landing effect. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of reverse thrust — asymmetric
fha.phases: Landing
fha.effAc: Reverse thrust available on one inboard engine only; asymmetric reverse produces a yawing moment during the landing roll. Nose-wheel steering and differential braking are available to counter it; net a slight reduction in functional capabilities with some directional demand.
fha.effCrew: Slight-to-significant increase in workload — crew arrests the asymmetric yaw with rudder/steering and differential braking during rollout and may elect to stow reverse.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect. Crew only aboard.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes crew can arrest the asymmetric-reverse yaw with available steering/differential braking on the semi-prepared surface, holding this to a workload increase rather than a directional-control excursion. If directional-control analysis shows one-side reverse at the inboard 0.18-semi-span moment produces an unrecoverable excursion on a low-friction strip, this rises toward Hazardous. Confirm from FCS/LDG directional-control analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes crew can arrest the asymmetric-reverse yaw with available steering/differential braking on the semi-prepared surface, holding this to a workload increase rather than a directional-control excursion. If directional-control analysis shows one-side reverse at the inboard 0.18-semi-span moment produces an unrecoverable excursion on a low-friction strip, this rises toward Hazardous. Confirm from FCS/LDG directional-control analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Asymmetric reverse introduces a directional-control demand during the ground roll on a semi-prepared surface, giving a "significant increase in flightcrew workload" to maintain the runway centreline (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3). Ground steering and differential braking remain; effect is bounded below Hazardous. Reverse is not used in other phases and in-flight deployment is inhibited, so this row carries the landing effect only. [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (crew axis governs). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fuel delivery — single engine
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One engine loses fuel delivery and its thrust; with dual boost pumps per collector, a gravity feed path below FL150 and a cross-feed gallery permitting any tank to feed any engine, the affected engine can normally be restored or the aircraft continues three-engine — a significant reduction in functional capabilities, not a safety-of-flight loss, given the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in crew workload: crew detect the loss via engine parameters and low-pressure/imbalance discretes, select manual cross-feed or accept three-engine operation, and manage a diversion.
fha.effPax: None — hold is unoccupied in flight; no passengers aboard.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether cross-feed/collector reserve or three-engine continuation is credited for the affected engine; SDD states dual boost pumps, gravity path and cross-feed gallery but not restoration timing. Assumed restoration or safe three-engine continuation. A demonstrated single-engine restore/continuation case would confirm Major; if the affected engine cannot be restored and directional/performance margins are eroded near the ground, the class could rise.

fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload as the crew counter an unexpected and possibly opposite yaw response; on the sized engine-out/low-speed case the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to recover consistently.
fha.effPax: Crew only aboard; hold unoccupied.
fha.judgementNote: Whether an erroneous yaw command in the worst phase (takeoff/landing, low speed, engine-out) is recoverable versus catastrophic turns on the magnitude/rate of the erroneous surface deflection and the FCS command-monitoring that limits it, which the SDD does not quantify; if a full-authority erroneous rudder deflection is credible and unrecoverable near the ground this row becomes Catastrophic. Confirm from FCS command-monitor and rudder authority limiting analysis.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of yaw control authority — outside MAC
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Remaining yaw authority insufficient outside the maneuvering envelope — against the sized outboard-engine-out at the 28 m moment arm, directional control margin is largely eroded; a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Excessive workload to maintain directional control at the limit; the flightcrew may not be relied upon to hold the aircraft against the full engine-out/crosswind demand.
fha.effPax: Crew only aboard; hold unoccupied.
fha.judgementNote: Whether outside-MAC partial loss remains Hazardous rather than Catastrophic depends on how much authority remains against the sized outboard-engine-out demand and whether that residual is controllable; the SDD sizes rudder to the engine-out case but does not state the residual after a partial loss. Confirm from FCS directional-control sizing and controllability analysis.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded yaw/sideslip imposes an unplanned directional excursion at the 28 m outboard moment arm reference; a large reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins results unless the crew arrests it promptly with rudder and roll.
fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload to identify and counter the uncommanded yaw, particularly near the ground; recovery is credited but demanding.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; ground/handling consequences downstream of aircraft path deviation.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the crew being able to detect and arrest the uncommanded yaw before departure, especially in the takeoff/landing phases; the SDD credits split-rudder authority sized for engine-out but does not state the recovery margin for an uncommanded (not thrust-driven) yaw. Handling-qualities analysis or simulation would confirm whether recovery is reliable (Hazardous) or the condition escalates to Catastrophic.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command — undetected
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: An erroneous yaw response the crew does not detect corrupts directional control against pilot intent; with no crew correction credited the excursion develops toward loss of directional control and hull loss.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; no corrective action is taken and the developing excursion is not arrested — fatalities or incapacitation follow the loss of control.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; multiple fatalities on hull loss.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether an erroneous yaw response can go genuinely undetected long enough to become unrecoverable — the SDD gives three dissimilar flight-control computers voting and asymmetry/jam discretes but does not state coverage against an erroneous (as opposed to lost) yaw command. If monitoring reliably annunciates the error, the credited condition reverts to the aware case (Hazardous); FCS monitor-coverage analysis would settle it.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Complete loss of high lift raises stall and approach speeds and lengthens takeoff and landing distance; against a 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement with ~1,080 m predicted rollout the margin is eroded — a significant to large reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in workload to fly a flapless/slatless profile and re-plan the landing to the available surface; distress if the field length cannot be met.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; consequence downstream of degraded landing performance.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether a flapless/slatless landing remains achievable within the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement at max landing weight — the SDD gives the requirement and a ~1,080 m normal rollout but no flapless landing distance. If flapless distance still fits with margin the class is Major; if it exceeds available surface (no diversion at the semi-prepared strip) it approaches Catastrophic. Landing-performance analysis would settle effPaxLevel and the class.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Rolling moment from asymmetric flap/slat deployment; asymmetry brakes at each section arrest the split, but a significant reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities results before arrest during the high-workload takeoff and landing phases.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to counter the roll and manage the configuration; asymmetry annunciated.
fha.effPax: None aboard the hold; flight crew only.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the asymmetry brake arresting the split before roll authority is exceeded near the ground; SDD credits asymmetry brakes at each section but gives no arrest angle or roll-margin data. If the arrested asymmetry still exceeds recoverable roll authority at low speed the class rises to Hazardous. Confirm with FCS asymmetry limits and handling analysis.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded flap/slat extension or retraction changes the lift/drag state and stall margin; a significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities results, most acute if retraction occurs at low speed on approach/takeoff or extension occurs above placard speed in cruise.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to re-establish the correct configuration and respect speed limits; condition annunciated.
fha.effPax: None aboard the hold; flight crew only.

fha.effAc: Asymmetric deployment develops without annunciation; the crew do not command a correction and the rolling moment builds during a low-speed high-workload phase, giving a large reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities before the asymmetry brakes act or the crew recognise it by aircraft response.
fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload once the asymmetry is recognised only by aircraft behaviour, such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to counter it in time near the ground.
fha.effPax: None aboard the hold; flight crew only.

If the asymmetry brake arrests the split fast enough to keep the aircraft controllable regardless of crew action, the class falls to Major. Confirm with FCS asymmetry-brake response and detection coverage.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground load support
fha.phases: Takeoff, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Total inability to support the aircraft and absorb ground loads results in gear collapse / fuselage contact during touchdown or ground roll; the aircraft is not recoverable by crew action once support is lost under weight, giving loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities / crew incapacitation credited jointly with hull loss.
fha.effPax: None aboard the hold; flight crew only — fatalities or incapacitation credited jointly with hull loss.
fha.judgementNote: SF-009 is stated as a function ("support aircraft and absorb ground loads") but complete loss borders on structural integrity, which is normally substantiated by structural analysis and PRA rather than functional FHA. Classified as the functional end effect; confirm the boundary between this FHA row and the structural substantiation, and whether the gear/floor structure single-load-path items belong to PRA.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground load support
fha.phases: Takeoff, Landing, Taxi
fha.effAc: Partial loss of ground load support (e.g. a bogie or leg not carrying its share) unbalances the footprint and reduces flotation and load-spreading capability on the semi-prepared surface; a significant reduction in functional capabilities results, with potential for a further leg to overload.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to manage the landing/rollout and directional control with degraded support.
fha.effPax: None aboard the hold; flight crew only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Cannot be grounded from the provided functions: the class turns on how much of the ground support is lost and whether the remaining legs/bogies carry the redistributed load within limits on the semi-prepared surface. SF-009 has no malfunction/partial breakdown data in the FCIM beyond the phrase, and the SDD notes gear leg and bogie count are preliminary and not frozen — the residual load path after a partial loss is unquantified. Provide the bogie/leg redundancy and residual-strength case before classifying. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Normal gear extension unavailable; free-fall alternate extension is the credited means to achieve a locked-down configuration for landing (per SDD §5.6.2). If the alternate succeeds, a normal landing follows with significant reduction in functional capabilities during the reconfiguration.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the failure to extend, action the alternate free-fall extension from a separate handle, and verify downlock — a significant increase in crew workload during approach.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the free-fall alternate extension is independent of the normal hydraulic system-A path and is credited as the second means; if the alternate shares the failure that caused loss of normal extension, the credited outcome is a gear-up or partial-gear landing and the class rises. Confirm alternate independence in the PSSA.

fha.phases: Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One or more bogies fail to extend and lock while the remainder are down; landing on a reduced gear set with reduced flotation on a semi-prepared surface, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities and increased risk of a gear-collapse or excursion on rollout.
fha.effCrew: Crew detect the asymmetric/incomplete configuration, attempt alternate extension, and manage a degraded-gear landing — a significant increase in crew workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes a partial-gear landing on the semi-prepared strip remains controllable (arrested excursion, no hull loss); the number of legs lost and their position is not specified and the leg/bogie count is preliminary per §1.2. If the residual footprint cannot carry the landing on the unpaved surface the outcome escalates. Confirm against flotation and landing-performance analysis.

fha.phases: Taxi, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded retraction with weight on wheels collapses the aircraft onto the ground, causing structural damage and loss of ground control; a large reduction in functional capabilities and potential for fire from ground contact of engines/structure.
fha.effCrew: Sudden collapse gives the crew no effective recovery action on the ground; excessive and abrupt workload with limited ability to arrest the event.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew. Ground personnel may be exposed during ground phases.
fha.judgementNote: Ground-collapse severity turns on whether uplock/downlock design and weight-on-wheels interlock (SDD notes downlocks mechanically held, hydraulically released, dual proximity sensing) actually prevent retraction on the ground; the SDD does not state a WoW inhibit on retraction. Assumed a credible uncommanded-retraction path on the ground with severe consequence. Confirm the retraction inhibit logic in the SFHA/PSSA.

fha.phases: Taxi
fha.effAc: No braking available on the ground; the 1,800 m landing distance requirement cannot be met against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout on a semi-prepared strip, exhausting the deceleration margin and giving a large reduction in functional capabilities leading to a runway/strip overrun.
fha.effCrew: Crew apply all available deceleration means (reverse on the two inboard engines, aerodynamic drag) but cannot arrest the aircraft within the available surface; excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to prevent the overrun.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; injury exposure is to the two-to-four flight crew in the overrun.
fha.judgementNote: The SDD gives the 1,800 m requirement vs ~1,080 m predicted rollout but not the overrun terrain, the ground speed at which the margin is exhausted with all braking lost, or whether reverse thrust plus drag keeps the excursion survivable; classified Hazardous crediting residual deceleration means. fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of door latching and locking
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: The door is the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed; a complete loss of latching and locking that is NOT annunciated allows the visor to depart in flight, with loss of the pressure boundary and the forward structural load path — normally with hull loss.
fha.effCrew: With the loss undetected the crew take no action; on boundary departure the outcome is not recoverable by crew action — multiple fatalities / incapacitation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied, but hull loss is a joint catastrophic outcome for the crew aboard.
fha.comments: ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Take-off, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An undetected complete loss of a door that is both pressure boundary and forward structural load path permits in-flight departure: "A failure condition that would result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5). The undetected (dual-sensing-defeated) case removes the crew alleviation the aware case relies on. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of lock status indication
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Both dissimilar lock-sensing paths (proximity harness and mechanical indicator) fail to present status; the door itself may be correctly locked, but the crew and the take-off configuration monitor lose the means to confirm lock integrity. Loss of this annunciation is itself a failure condition, and combined with a latent lock failure the door boundary/structural role is unverified.
fha.effCrew: Crew cannot verify lock status pre-flight or in flight; the take-off configuration check cannot be completed, giving a significant increase in flightcrew workload and dispatch impact.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect from the indication loss alone.
fha.comments: ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Taxi-out, Take-off, Taxi-in, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of annunciation is a failure condition in itself and is "classified as major unless the applicant can show otherwise" (AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2); its combination with an actual lock failure must meet the objective of the un-annunciated effect (the Catastrophic SF-014-TL2). As an indication loss alone it is Major. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of lock status indication
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One of the two dissimilar and independently routed lock-sensing paths is lost while the other continues to present status; lock integrity remains verifiable through the surviving path, with a slight reduction in the redundancy of the indication function.
fha.effCrew: Crew retains a means to confirm lock status via the remaining path; slight increase in workload to note the degraded indication and manage dispatch of the affected channel.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Credits the surviving sensing path (proximity harness OR mechanical indicator) as fully sufficient to confirm lock status and complete the config check. If the config monitor requires both channels, or a partial loss is itself latent, the class rises to Major per the annunciation-loss rule. Confirm the config-monitor logic against single-channel indication.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Nose-door lock status is presented incorrectly to the flight deck and to the take-off configuration monitor; because the erroneous indication is present and available for cross-check against the dissimilar mechanical indicator (§5.7.2), a significant reduction in functional capability of the lock-status integrity chain results, not a loss of the physical door which cannot be operated in flight.
fha.effCrew: Crew must resolve a disagreement between the proximity indication and the mechanical visual indicator and revert to the independent path; a significant increase in flightcrew workload to establish true lock state.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the second dissimilar indicator remains valid so the erroneous indication is caught; if both indications can be corrupted or the take-off config monitor accepts the erroneous state undetected, the condition escalates. FCS/config-monitor architecture and the config-check logic would confirm or overturn.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous lock status indication — undetected
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Lock status is erroneous and the error is not detected, so the flight deck and the take-off configuration monitor accept an incorrect lock state; the door forms part of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage load path when closed (§5.7.1), so an undetected wrong indication removes the crew's assurance that the boundary is secured, a large reduction in safety margins if it masks an unlocked or partially locked door.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties normally taking no action against the condition; no workload increase because the error is undetected — the hazard is precisely the absence of the cue to act.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the undetected erroneous indication can coincide with an actually-unsecured door and that no other independent boundary/structural cue catches it before pressurisation load; if the door state is independently confirmed (e.g. pressure interlock, structural indication) the class reduces to Major. The dissimilar sensing independence and config-monitor logic would confirm or overturn — depends on SF-014 door-latch state coupling.

fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted by the tension monitoring loop and manage the condition per the immediate-attention annunciation with no in-flight adjustment available (§5.8.6); a significant increase in flightcrew workload to assess and constrain the flight envelope.
fha.effPax: None; hold unoccupied in flight.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of blade restraint — undetected
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One or more restraint straps degraded at a saddle station with the tension monitor not annunciating; load is carried by neighbouring straps per the design load-sharing but the degradation is undetected, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities as restraint margin erodes without crew knowledge.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties unaware; no procedure triggered because the monitoring does not annunciate the degraded station, so a significant increase in workload arises only if a subsequent stated restraint condition (adjacent-station loss) is reached and must be managed without warning of the pre-existing degradation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect from the degraded restraint alone.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed a single-station undetected strap loss is carried by neighbours without progressing to blade shift within one flight (SDD: 'loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours'). If an undetected partial loss can propagate to a multi-station / blade-shift condition before the next inspection, the class rises toward Hazardous/Catastrophic — substantiate with restraint load-path and progression analysis.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded release of restraint on the single 72.6 t blade occupying the full 108 m hold length, undetected by the crew; the blade is free to shift longitudinally under flight and manoeuvre loads, producing a large centre-of-gravity excursion on a payload that is a large fraction of operating weight, with no in-flight means to arrest or correct it — assessed as loss of the aircraft.
fha.effCrew: Fatalities or incapacitation — crew aboard, restraint release undetected and un-correctable in flight (indication only, no in-flight restraint adjustment), so no crew action can recover the resulting CG excursion.
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — occupants of the flight deck aboard at hull loss.
fha.judgementNote: Assumed a fully released 72.6 t blade shifts far enough to drive the CG outside the recoverable envelope before any crew response, and that no in-flight means exists to arrest it (SDD: 'In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint'). If blade travel is mechanically limited by saddle geometry to a recoverable excursion, the class may reduce — substantiate with blade-shift dynamics and CG-envelope analysis.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of restraint tension monitoring
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Total loss of the function that instruments strap tension along the hold; no annunciation of a restraint condition is available, removing the crew's only in-flight means of detecting a developing restraint problem — a significant reduction in the safety margin against an undetected restraint failure.
fha.effCrew: Loss of the annunciation the crew rely on to detect a restraint degradation; the crew have no in-flight visibility of strap tension and must dispatch/continue on the assumption restraint remains intact — a significant increase in the difficulty of managing any restraint contingency.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.

[anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of restraint tension monitoring
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Loss of tension monitoring over part of the hold length (the loop is a single instrumented run); restraint conditions on the unmonitored stations would not be annunciated, giving a significant reduction in the safety margin against an undetected restraint failure in the affected region.
fha.effCrew: Crew retain annunciation over the monitored stations but have no coverage over the affected stations; managing a restraint contingency is harder because coverage is partial and its extent may not be evident — a significant increase in crew workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.

fha.effCrew: Misleading tension indication drives inappropriate crew assessment: a false-normal masks a developing restraint problem (no action when action may be warranted), a false-alert prompts an unnecessary restraint-condition response — a significant increase in crew workload and reduced ability to correctly assess restraint state.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of restraint tension monitoring
fha.effAc: Blade restraint remains physically intact (saddles and straps unaffected); the aircraft loses its only means to detect a slackening or migrating strap, so a developing restraint degradation could progress undetected toward a payload-shift or CG condition — a significant reduction in functional capabilities of the restraint-monitoring function.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties with no indication of restraint state; loss of the annunciated cue removes their ability to take timely action if a strap slackens — a significant increase in workload/uncertainty at the moment a restraint condition would otherwise be caught.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Class turns on whether an undetected slackening strap can progress to a payload shift or CG excursion that reaches a structural or flight-safety limit before landing; the SDD states single-loop monitoring and neighbour load-sharing but does not quantify how far degradation can go undetected. A restraint fault-tree / structural analysis showing an undetected strap loss cannot reach a hazardous shift would confirm Major; evidence it can would raise it.

fha.effAc: Total loss of conditioned-air supply to the flight deck (and hold); with no conditioning the aircraft must descend and divert to a habitable environment — a significant reduction in functional capabilities requiring an unplanned descent/diversion within the low operating ceiling (FL260 max).
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the loss, don oxygen if the pressurisation environment degrades, initiate descent and manage a diversion — a significant increase in workload above the normal automatic operation.
fha.effPax: No occupants carried in the hold; no passenger effect.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of cabin pressure differential control
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Complete loss of active pressurisation control; differential is held only by the independent relief valves, leaving the flight deck to depressurise toward ambient. Significant reduction in functional capabilities requiring a descent to a safe altitude.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted by cabin-altitude alerting, don quick-donning oxygen masks and initiate an emergency descent to a safe altitude and divert — a significant increase in workload but within trained procedure at FL260.
fha.effPax: Hold is unoccupied in flight; no occupants other than flight crew, who are protected by crew oxygen during the descent.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the crew detecting depressurisation and donning oxygen in time; the SDD credits masks fed the ECS cabin-altitude signal and FL260 ceiling. If time-of-useful-consciousness margin at the actual hold/flight-deck altitude proves inadequate, or detection is delayed, this rises toward Hazardous — confirm crew-oxygen adequacy and alerting response time.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on the crew detecting depressurisation and donning oxygen in time; the SDD credits masks fed the ECS cabin-altitude signal and FL260 ceiling. If time-of-useful-consciousness margin at the actual hold/flight-deck altitude proves inadequate, or detection is delayed, this rises toward Hazardous — confirm crew-oxygen adequacy and alerting response time. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Below FL260 with crew oxygen and a trained emergency-descent procedure the effect is a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" and a "significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of cabin pressure differential control
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced pressurisation control authority with one controller or outflow valve retained (either valve sufficient per architecture); differential still controlled at a degraded schedule. Slight reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the degraded configuration; single-controller/single-valve operation continues with a slight increase in workload and no immediate emergency action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no effect on occupants other than flight crew.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With a redundant controller and outflow valve available ("either valve being sufficient"), the residual effect is a "slight reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin pressure differential control — under-pressure
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Control drives an erroneously low differential / high cabin altitude while indicating normally is not assumed here (this is the annunciated case); the flight deck climbs toward an unsafe cabin altitude. Significant reduction in functional capabilities requiring descent.
fha.effCrew: Cabin-altitude alerting warns the crew, who don oxygen and descend to a safe altitude — a significant increase in workload within trained procedure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew protected by crew oxygen during descent.
fha.judgementNote: Depends on the under-pressure being detected and the crew acting in time; SDD credits the ECS cabin-altitude alert and crew oxygen at FL260. If detection is unreliable this converges with the undetected case (M3); confirm alerting coverage.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Depends on the under-pressure being detected and the crew acting in time; SDD credits the ECS cabin-altitude alert and crew oxygen at FL260. If detection is unreliable this converges with the undetected case (M3); confirm alerting coverage. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With the erroneous under-pressure annunciated and crew oxygen plus emergency descent available, a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" with "significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Erroneous cabin pressure differential control — over-pressure
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Control commands an erroneously high differential; the independent positive pressure relief valve limits the differential and protects the structure regardless of the control fault, capping the excursion. Slight reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew annunciated of the pressurisation fault and select manual mode; slight-to-significant increase in workload with the relief valve preventing a structural excursion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no effect on occupants other than flight crew.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the independent positive relief valve fully bounds over-pressure so structural rupture is not credited; SDD states relief "independently of the control system". If relief valve capacity is inadequate for the maximum erroneous demand this rises toward Hazardous/Catastrophic — confirm relief sizing against the worst-case control-commanded differential.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes the independent positive relief valve fully bounds over-pressure so structural rupture is not credited; SDD states relief "independently of the control system". If relief valve capacity is inadequate for the maximum erroneous demand this rises toward Hazardous/Catastrophic — confirm relief sizing against the worst-case control-commanded differential. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: The independent relief valve bounds the outcome to a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" with increased crew workload, not structural failure, AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous cabin pressure differential control — under-pressure
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Control drives an erroneously low differential / high cabin altitude with the fault undetected; the flight deck depressurises without crew recognition. Large reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue their duties without acting on the condition; if the corrupted ECS channel also feeds the cabin-altitude cue and the crew-oxygen logic, the crew may reach physical distress from hypoxia before recognising the state — flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; the flight crew are the exposed occupants and are at risk of incapacitation if the condition remains undetected.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether the cabin-altitude detection/alert that would warn the crew is independent of the erroneous ECS control channel. The SDD shows ECS supplies the cabin-altitude signal to the crew-oxygen logic, so a common ECS fault could defeat the cue — assumed here, giving Hazardous. If an independent cabin-altitude sensor annunciates regardless of the ECS control fault, this reduces to the detected M case (Major). Confirm the independence of cabin-altitude sensing/alerting from the pressurisation control channel.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on whether the cabin-altitude detection/alert that would warn the crew is independent of the erroneous ECS control channel. The SDD shows ECS supplies the cabin-altitude signal to the crew-oxygen logic, so a common ECS fault could defeat the cue — assumed here, giving Hazardous. If an independent cabin-altitude sensor annunciates regardless of the ECS control fault, this reduces to the detected M case (Major). Confirm the independence of cabin-altitude sensing/alerting from the pressurisation control channel. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss of the pressurisation cue producing "physical distress or excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4; loss of annunciation is a failure condition in its own right, §5.4.2. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous cabin pressure differential control — over-pressure
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent
fha.effAc: Erroneous, undetected commanding of the outflow valves toward closure raises differential above the low design value; independent positive-pressure mechanical relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities rather than structural failure.
fha.effCrew: No annunciation of the erroneous control; crew continue normally until relief-valve operation or a secondary cue, then a significant increase in workload to reconfigure to manual pressurisation and descend.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aft of the flight deck. Flight deck occupants experience physical discomfort from the differential excursion prior to relief.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the hold pressurisation differential (preliminary, ~8,800 m equivalent) and on the relief valves capping the excursion below structural limits; if the relief valves do not bound the over-pressure to a non-hazardous level, or the residual differential is set higher when frozen, the class rises toward Hazardous. Confirm relief-valve setting margin against structural limits.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on the hold pressurisation differential (preliminary, ~8,800 m equivalent) and on the relief valves capping the excursion below structural limits; if the relief valves do not bound the over-pressure to a non-hazardous level, or the residual differential is set higher when frozen, the class rises toward Hazardous. Confirm relief-valve setting margin against structural limits. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Independent mechanical relief valves cap the differential and prevent structural failure, so the credited outcome is a controlled excursion, not hull loss: "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. Loss of annunciation combined with the erroneous control is assessed against the un-annunciated effect per §5.4.2. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of surface and inlet ice protection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Complete loss of protection of wing leading edges, engine inlet cowls and stabiliser surfaces; in the icing envelope of the certification basis, ice accretion on lifting and control surfaces and engine inlets produces a large reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities, degrading lift, drag, control effectiveness and engine operability.
fha.effCrew: Ice detection remains (separate function) so the crew are alerted; assumed to exit the icing envelope by altitude or route change, with physical distress or excessive workload managing degraded handling if unable to exit promptly.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight deck occupants exposed to the consequences of degraded handling in icing.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the crew can detect (detection function available) and exit the icing envelope before accretion becomes uncontrollable; the SDD gives no icing exposure time or degraded-handling data. If the envelope cannot be exited in time in a foreseeable operating condition, the accreted-ice handling loss could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm icing-envelope exposure and degraded handling analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes the crew can detect (detection function available) and exit the icing envelope before accretion becomes uncontrollable; the SDD gives no icing exposure time or degraded-handling data. If the envelope cannot be exited in time in a foreseeable operating condition, the accreted-ice handling loss could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm icing-envelope exposure and degraded handling analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of required ice protection across surfaces and inlets in the icing envelope credits an escape (exit the envelope) rather than hull loss: "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of surface and inlet ice protection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Partial loss (e.g. a lost stabiliser heater zone, or bleed protection available from one side only through the cross-bleed manifold) leaves protection degraded but present; a lost electrical zone is annunciated and the remaining zones and cross-bleed path continue protection, giving a significant reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Lost zone annunciated; crew reconfigure and apply the associated icing limitations, a significant increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect beyond the flight deck.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the degradation is a bounded partial (single zone / single-side bleed) that is annunciated and leaves adequate protection for the encountered envelope; the SDD does not quantify the protected fraction retained. If a partial loss removes protection from a flight-critical surface in the envelope, the class rises. Confirm minimum protected configuration.

fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent surface and inlet ice protection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach
fha.effAc: Inadvertent (uncommanded) operation of surface and inlet ice protection outside icing conditions applies the wing anti-ice bleed demand, reducing pack capacity and applying a performance penalty; effect is a slight reduction in functional capabilities with no structural or control threat.
fha.effCrew: Performance penalty of wing anti-ice in use is applied automatically to displayed performance; crew workload to detect and deselect is a slight increase.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no occupant effect.
fha.comments: ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Take-off, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Inadvertent activation only imposes a bleed/performance penalty that is automatically accounted and readily deselected: "slight reduction in safety margins" / "slight increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of probe and windshield ice protection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Complete loss of heating to probes, static ports and windshields in the icing envelope leads to unreliable air data (blocked/iced pitot-static and AOA) and loss of forward visibility, a large reduction in safety margins and functional capabilities; three air data inertial reference units and a standby instrument exist but share the loss of the sensed source when the probes themselves ice.
fha.effCrew: Individual monitoring of heated elements alerts the crew; assumed to exit the icing envelope and manage on remaining information, with physical distress or excessive workload if air data becomes unreliable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight deck occupants exposed to the consequences of unreliable air data / lost visibility in icing.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes probe/element loss is individually monitored so the crew are alerted and can exit the icing envelope, and that redundant ADIRUs do not protect against a common icing of the sensed probes. The SDD gives no icing exposure or unreliable-airspeed procedure data. If probe icing produces undetected misleading air data feeding all references, the condition could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm probe redundancy/heating monitoring and unreliable-airspeed handling.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes probe/element loss is individually monitored so the crew are alerted and can exit the icing envelope, and that redundant ADIRUs do not protect against a common icing of the sensed probes. The SDD gives no icing exposure or unreliable-airspeed procedure data. If probe icing produces undetected misleading air data feeding all references, the condition could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm probe redundancy/heating monitoring and unreliable-airspeed handling. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of all probe/windshield protection in icing threatens the integrity of air data common to primary and standby sensing and forward visibility, crediting escape from the envelope rather than hull loss: "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: A subset of heated probes/static ports/windshields loses protection; remaining protected sensing and dissimilar redundant air-data sources continue to provide valid data, giving a slight reduction in functional capabilities in icing conditions.
fha.effCrew: Loss of a heated zone is annunciated and monitored individually; crew selects protection and manages the affected sensing, a slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes a partial loss leaves at least one valid air-data/vision path per the three ADIRUs and individual zone monitoring; if a partial loss can silently corrupt all primary airspeed sources this rises toward Major/Hazardous. fha.effAc: Erroneous heating (over- or under-heat at probes/ports) degrades air-data quality; if it corrupts primary airspeed/altitude in icing, the flightcrew's primary references are affected, a significant reduction in functional capabilities.

fha.judgementNote: Assumes uncommanded heating does not damage the sensing element or corrupt air data before deselection; if sustained inadvertent probe heating can bias the measured value this rises to Major. Confirm element thermal design margins and any air-data bias effect.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Probe ice protection is lost without annunciation; in icing the probes/ports accrete ice and primary air-data sources degrade or fail with no crew warning, a large reduction in safety margins as the crew flies on corrupted or lost airspeed/altitude references.
fha.effCrew: Crew continues normal duties unaware; onset of unreliable air data in icing produces physical distress or excessive workload such that they cannot be relied upon to diagnose and revert accurately in time.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ice accretion detection
fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Automatic ice detection is lost; ice protection remains available and can be selected manually, but the crew must rely on visual/other cues to recognise icing, a significant reduction in functional capabilities of the protective envelope.
fha.effCrew: Detection is advisory; loss of the detection annunciation increases crew monitoring workload to recognise icing onset and manually select protection, a significant increase in workload — loss of annunciation is itself a failure condition per §5.4.2.
fha.effPax: No effect on occupants; hold unoccupied in flight.
fha.judgementNote: Applies the §5.4.2 loss-of-annunciation default (Major) because detection is advisory and manual protection selection remains; if the crew cannot otherwise recognise icing and unprotected accretion follows, the combined condition could be more severe. Confirm alternate icing cues and any auto-on logic dependency on the detectors.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One of two identical ice detectors remains; icing detection coverage on one side of the forward fuselage is degraded. Ice protection can still be selected manually at any time, so a slight reduction in functional capabilities results.
fha.effCrew: Crew must weigh reduced detection confidence and consider selecting ice protection manually rather than relying on automatic activation — a slight increase in workload.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect on the flight crew beyond the stated workload.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the second identical detector plus manual-on capability keep icing recognition adequate after partial loss; the two detectors are the same type (recorded commonality item), so if the loss is a common-mode degradation affecting recognition confidence in both, severity would rise. Confirm detector independence and crew procedure for degraded detection.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of ice accretion detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection is lost without annunciation; the crew is unaware and continues normally. In an icing encounter, ice may accrete on protected surfaces before the crew recognises it from airframe cues and selects ice protection manually, allowing a period of unprotected accretion that reduces safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew take no action regarding the failure (unaware) and rely on secondary cues to recognise icing late, with a significant increase in workload once accretion is recognised and manual protection is invoked in a degraded state.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no effect on the flight crew beyond the stated workload.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the loss is truly unannunciated and that crew recognition of icing from other cues occurs late enough to allow meaningful unprotected accretion within the icing envelope; if a monitor annunciates the detection loss, or manual protection is habitually selected on entering known icing regardless of detector state, severity reduces toward Minor. Confirm detection-loss monitoring and icing-entry procedure.

Confirm detection-loss monitoring and icing-entry procedure. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected loss removes the primary means of recognising accretion in an icing encounter, giving a period of unprotected accretion and a significant reduction in margins with increased crew workload; "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3; loss of annunciation is classified major unless shown otherwise, §5.4.2. fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of flight and navigation display
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: One or more display units or a display processor is lost; with three display processors, dual networks and any-format-on-any-unit reversion, the remaining displays continue to present primary flight and navigation information. A significant reduction in display redundancy results but full information remains available.
fha.effCrew: Crew perform a reversionary display selection and continue with reduced redundancy — a significant increase in workload during reconfiguration and thereafter reduced margin against a further display failure.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; the flight crew face the workload described above.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss consumes display redundancy and imposes reversionary reconfiguration while full information remains presentable; "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3; "significant increase in flightcrew workload", §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Displayed flight and navigation information is erroneous but the discrepancy is detectable by the crew against independent flight information; crew cross-checks, reverts to a trustworthy source and continues, giving a significant reduction in functional capability during the reversion.
fha.effCrew: Significant increase in flightcrew workload to detect the discrepancy, identify the affected display and manage reversion to a trusted source.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the crew detecting the erroneous display via independent flight information and reverting in time; the SDD provides an independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (§5.11.3), supporting detectability. If detection cannot be credited at aircraft level this migrates toward the undetected case (SF-023-M2). Confirm crediting of an independent cross-check at aircraft-function level.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected erroneous flight and navigation display
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Erroneous flight and navigation information is presented without the crew detecting it; crew flies on misleading data with no cross-check credited, giving a large reduction in safety margins that can progress to loss of control or controlled flight into terrain.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading information as if valid; no workload increase is credited because the error is undetected — the hazard is acting confidently on false data.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; consequence follows the aircraft outcome.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether ANY independent source remains that could eventually reveal the error before an unrecoverable state; if no independent cross-check exists at all the class rises to Catastrophic. The three-ADIRU / independent standby architecture (§5.11) argues an independent source persists, holding this at Hazardous. Confirm no single common source drives all displays simultaneously with a plausible, non-detectable error.

[anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of air data and inertial reference
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Total loss of air data and inertial reference removes primary airspeed, altitude and attitude sourcing; crew reverts to independent standby flight information and continues on degraded but flyable information, a large reduction in functional capability.
fha.effCrew: Physical distress or excessive workload flying on standby-only information across the diversion, with reduced situational awareness.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; consequence follows the aircraft outcome.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on an independent standby means surviving the same event; the SDD states standby attitude/airspeed/altitude on the DC essential bus sharing no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries (§5.11.2–3), so total loss of the three reference units still leaves standby — holding this at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If the standby shares a common failure path with the reference units the class rises. Confirm standby independence at aircraft level.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of air data and inertial reference
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Loss of one of the redundant air data/inertial reference sources with the remaining sources continuing to supply valid data; a slight reduction in safety margins with full primary information retained through reconfiguration.
fha.effCrew: Slight increase in flightcrew workload to recognise the degraded reference and confirm reconfiguration to remaining sources.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; no direct occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on how much of the function is lost in the partial case; classified for loss of one of the three reference units leaving two valid. If 'partial' were taken to mean loss of two of three (leaving one), the class would approach the total-loss/Hazardous end. Confirm the intended partial-loss depth for this row.
