fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No detection available in any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, main gear bays, hold); an engine, APU, duct-overheat or hold fire develops with no warning and no crew cue to discharge extinguishing, permitting an uncontained/uncontrolled fire and a large reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins.
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire/overheat alert and take no protective action (fire handle, engine shutdown, diversion); with an undetected developing fire the crew cannot be relied upon to manage the event, a large reduction in safety margins.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew (up to four) exposed to serious or fatal consequences of an uncontrolled onboard fire.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether an actual fire coincident with total detection loss is credited within this single condition or handled as a combination. SDD gives dual-loop detection per zone and crew-commanded extinguishing but no probability data; if the coincident fire is credited the class moves to Catastrophic. Fault-tree/combination analysis (FHA+CMA) and the hold-suppression substantiation would confirm or overturn.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on whether an actual fire coincident with total detection loss is credited within this single condition or handled as a combination. SDD gives dual-loop detection per zone and crew-commanded extinguishing but no probability data; if the coincident fire is credited the class moves to Catastrophic. Fault-tree/combination analysis (FHA+CMA) and the hold-suppression substantiation would confirm or overturn. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detection is lost but a fire is not simultaneously present in every case; the credited outcome is an undetected fire that develops without the crew cue to extinguish — "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. Not classified Catastrophic because loss of detection alone is not hull loss until combined with an actual fire event. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection lost in one zone or degraded to single-loop logic while other zones remain monitored; a fire in the affected zone may be detected late or missed, a significant reduction in the detection safety margin.
fha.effCrew: Loss of coverage annunciated (a lost loop degrades to single-loop logic and is reported); crew manage with reduced coverage and consider dispatch/continuation, a significant increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; crew exposed to a delayed-detection fire risk in the affected zone only.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Coverage remains in the other monitored zones and degraded single-loop logic still warns; "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Erroneous detection either fails to warn of a real event (missed) or misreports zone/state, biasing crew response; where a real fire is misreported as absent the safety margin is largely reduced, where a nuisance or wrong-zone indication drives an unnecessary engine shutdown or discharge the functional capability is significantly reduced.
fha.effCrew: Crew act on misleading fire information — potentially shutting down a healthy engine or failing to act on a real fire — a significant to large increase in workload and impaired decision-making.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; crew exposed to consequences of misdirected fire response.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether erroneous detection can present as a false 'no-fire' during a real event (masking) versus only a false 'fire' warning. SDD states dual-loop AND logic for warning but does not describe cross-monitoring that would reject a stuck-clear loop; if masking is precluded by design the class reduces to Major. Detailed system FMEA of the detection logic would confirm.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on whether erroneous detection can present as a false 'no-fire' during a real event (masking) versus only a false 'fire' warning. SDD states dual-loop AND logic for warning but does not describe cross-monitoring that would reject a stuck-clear loop; if masking is precluded by design the class reduces to Major. Detailed system FMEA of the detection logic would confirm. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Misleading detection can suppress the crew cue to a real fire or provoke an unnecessary engine shutdown in a critical phase; "physical distress or excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: False fire/overheat warning with no actual fire; may prompt an unnecessary precautionary engine shutdown or extinguisher discharge and a diversion, a significant reduction in available thrust/functional capability if acted upon.
fha.effCrew: Crew respond to a valid-appearing false warning — run the fire drill, potentially shut down a healthy engine, and divert — a significant increase in workload.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect beyond the diversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A false warning drives a precautionary shutdown/diversion but the aircraft retains three remaining engines and full detection integrity elsewhere; "significant increase in flightcrew workload", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Detection function is lost AND the loss itself is not annunciated: the crew believe protection is available when it is not, so a subsequent fire develops with no warning and no crew action, permitting an uncontained/uncontrolled fire — a large reduction in safety margins, and hull loss where the coincident fire is credited.
fha.effCrew: Crew continue normal duties assuming detection is healthy and take no action for the latent loss or the ensuing undetected fire; they cannot be relied upon to manage an event they receive no cue for.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; crew exposed to serious or fatal consequences of a latent, undetected onboard fire.
fha.judgementNote: Latent-plus-fire combination: if the coincident fire is credited within this condition the class is Catastrophic (undetected fire to hull loss); if the latent loss is treated in isolation with the fire handled as a separate combined event, Hazardous holds. Depends on whether the detection loss is self-monitored/annunciated — SDD does not state built-in monitoring of loop integrity. §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment and CMA would confirm.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Latent-plus-fire combination: if the coincident fire is credited within this condition the class is Catastrophic (undetected fire to hull loss); if the latent loss is treated in isolation with the fire handled as a separate combined event, Hazardous holds. Depends on whether the detection loss is self-monitored/annunciated — SDD does not state built-in monitoring of loop integrity. §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment and CMA would confirm. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Latent loss of the detection function combined with a subsequent fire the crew are never warned of; loss of annunciation is itself a failure condition and "the combination of a system failure with failure of its annunciation must meet the objective of the un-annunciated effect" (AC 25.1309-1B §5.4.2), here "a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", §3.1.4. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No direct effect on airplane systems; the protective function against smoke/fume and depressurisation events is degraded.
fha.effCrew: Erroneous delivery (wrong flow/mixture or contaminated supply) at a mask degrades crew protection during a smoke/fume or depressurisation event; system status is displayed, crew can select the crossover and use per-mask regulators, but detecting and working around the fault imposes a significant increase in flightcrew workload during an already-demanding event.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers aboard, no direct effect on occupants.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes erroneous delivery is detectable via status indication and worked around (crossover / per-mask regulators / mask-off breathing tolerable at FL260) before it incapacitates a crew member. If erroneous delivery can silently deliver a contaminated or oxygen-deficient supply to all masks during a depressurisation, undetected, the crew axis rises to fatalities or incapacitation and the class to Hazardous or Catastrophic — an FMEA of the delivery/manifold and a smoke/fume + depressurisation scenario would confirm or overturn.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes erroneous delivery is detectable via status indication and worked around (crossover / per-mask regulators / mask-off breathing tolerable at FL260) before it incapacitates a crew member. If erroneous delivery can silently deliver a contaminated or oxygen-deficient supply to all masks during a depressurisation, undetected, the crew axis rises to fatalities or incapacitation and the class to Hazardous or Catastrophic — an FMEA of the delivery/manifold and a smoke/fume + depressurisation scenario would confirm or overturn. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous delivery degrades crew protection during a smoke/fume or depressurisation event but the second cylinder crossover, per-mask regulators and continuous status indication support crew workaround at FL260: "physical discomfort or significant increase in flightcrew workload" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3, Major). [anchor MAJ-2 — Major] Levels: Aircraft none · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (crew axis governs). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach
fha.effAc: Inadvertent deployment of an inboard-engine reverser in flight produces significant reverse/spoiling and a large asymmetric yawing-and-rolling moment at the inboard moment arm. Deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock; defeat of those interlocks is required. If it occurs at speed the resulting upset may exceed the aircraft's controllable envelope, credited as loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities — crew aboard; the upset is credited as not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — hull loss credited (Table A6 CAT-1 joint state).
fha.judgementNote: Assumes an in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed exceeds the aircraft's recoverable envelope (credited as hull loss). If FCS controllability analysis demonstrates the aircraft is controllable through a single inboard reverser-in-flight deployment across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. The multi-layer inhibit (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) bears on likelihood/architecture, not on the classified severity of the effect. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes an in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed exceeds the aircraft's recoverable envelope (credited as hull loss). If FCS controllability analysis demonstrates the aircraft is controllable through a single inboard reverser-in-flight deployment across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. The multi-layer inhibit (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) bears on likelihood/architecture, not on the classified severity of the effect. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment on a large asymmetric moment arm is credited as a condition that would "result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5). This is the joint top step (Table A6 CAT-1); crew and occupant axes follow the aircraft axis automatically. On the ground / during landing roll, inadvertent reverse is the commanded regime and is not this condition. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach
fha.effAc: Uncommanded in-flight reverser deployment (not crew-initiated) on an inboard engine produces significant thrust opposite to that commanded and a large asymmetric upsetting moment at speed. In-flight deployment is inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock; occurrence requires defeat of those interlocks. Credited as exceeding the controllable envelope — loss of the airplane.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities — crew aboard; upset credited as not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — hull loss credited (Table A6 CAT-1 joint state).
fha.judgementNote: Same controllability assumption as SF-002-M: an uncommanded in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed is credited as exceeding the recoverable envelope (hull loss). If FCS analysis shows the aircraft is controllable through this event across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Same controllability assumption as SF-002-M: an uncommanded in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed is credited as exceeding the recoverable envelope (hull loss). If FCS analysis shows the aircraft is controllable through this event across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight is a condition that would "result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5); this is the same reverser-in-flight upset as SF-002-M arising without crew command. Joint top step (Table A6 CAT-1) — crew and occupant axes follow automatically. Inhibits and mechanical lock bear on likelihood, not on the classified severity. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Complete loss of fuel delivery starves all four engines, producing total loss of thrust. With no thrust the aircraft cannot sustain flight and is credited as loss of the airplane. (Loss of thrust caused by fuel starvation is a total-loss-of-thrust condition, distinct from a single-engine loss the aircraft is designed to continue on.)
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities — crew aboard; total thrust loss with insufficient means to reach a landing is credited as not recoverable.
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities — hull loss credited (Table A6 CAT-1 joint state).
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of fuel delivery to all engines removes all thrust; the resulting condition would "result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5). Joint top step (Table A6 CAT-1) — crew and occupant axes follow the aircraft axis automatically. Effects are the same across every phase (total thrust loss is not escapable), so one row carries all phases. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No means remains to command roll: both aileron segments and the multi-function spoilers are unavailable. The aircraft cannot be maintained in coordinated lateral trim or manoeuvred laterally; on a high-wing four-engine freighter this prevents continued safe flight and landing and is credited as not recoverable, giving hull loss.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities — crew aboard; loss of the aircraft is credited as not recoverable by crew action.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; the credited outcome is loss of the aircraft.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether any residual lateral control (e.g. differential thrust from the four engines, or rudder-induced roll) can be credited to make the flight recoverable; the SDD gives no roll authority from other means, so complete loss of both aileron and spoiler roll is assumed unrecoverable. Confirm whether differential thrust provides usable roll control in the FCS SFHA — if credited, the aircraft axis and class could be reduced.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on whether any residual lateral control (e.g. differential thrust from the four engines, or rudder-induced roll) can be credited to make the flight recoverable; the SDD gives no roll authority from other means, so complete loss of both aileron and spoiler roll is assumed unrecoverable. Confirm whether differential thrust provides usable roll control in the FCS SFHA — if credited, the aircraft axis and class could be reduced. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of the ability to control roll prevents continued safe flight and landing; per AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5 Note 1 such a condition "should be classified as catastrophic", CAT-1. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: All restraint of a single unitised payload of up to 72.6 t occupying the full 108 m hold length is lost in flight; the blade is free to shift longitudinally with no in-flight means of re-restraint (§5.8.6), producing an uncontrolled centre-of-gravity excursion and hold structural loading beyond the design case, credited as not recoverable by crew action — hull loss.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities / crew incapacitation follow the loss of the aircraft (joint top step).
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities (joint top step); hold unoccupied but the outcome is loss of the aircraft.
fha.comments: ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Take-off, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A free 72.6 t single-item payload in flight with no in-flight re-restraint produces an uncontrollable CG and structural excursion that would "result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5 (CAT-1); the top step is joint. [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Restraint releases when not commanded; because straps are tensioned by electric winches and locked mechanically with no in-flight adjustment (§5.8.2/§5.8.6), an inadvertent release removes the tensioned restraint of the 72.6 t blade in flight with no crew re-restraint means, credited as progressing to loss of the payload restraint and an uncontrollable CG/structural excursion — hull loss.
fha.effCrew: Multiple fatalities / crew incapacitation follow the loss of the aircraft (joint top step).
fha.effPax: Multiple fatalities (joint top step); hold unoccupied but the outcome is loss of the aircraft.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes an inadvertent release affects enough of the restraint (multiple straps/saddles) to be equivalent to loss of restraint; if a single inadvertent release is bounded by the mechanical lock and neighbour load paths to a partial degradation, the class reduces toward the SF-016-PL Major level. The release-command architecture and how many independent releases are needed to unrestrain the blade would confirm or overturn.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes an inadvertent release affects enough of the restraint (multiple straps/saddles) to be equivalent to loss of restraint; if a single inadvertent release is bounded by the mechanical lock and neighbour load paths to a partial degradation, the class reduces toward the SF-016-PL Major level. The release-command architecture and how many independent releases are needed to unrestrain the blade would confirm or overturn. | ⚠ PHASES DROPPED — the model named Take-off, not in this project's phase table; exposure is computed without them. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded release of the tensioned restraint of a single 72.6 t in-flight payload, with mechanical lock defeated and no in-flight re-restraint, credits to the same uncontrollable outcome as complete loss — would "result in multiple fatalities, usually with the loss of the airplane", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.5 (CAT-1). [anchor CAT-1 — Catastrophic] Levels: Aircraft hull loss · Crew fatalities or incapacitation · Occupants multiple fatalities → Catastrophic (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight and navigation display
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: All primary flight and navigation display is lost. Flight continues on the independent integrated standby instrument (attitude, airspeed, altitude) which shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primaries. Aircraft remains flyable but on markedly reduced information, a large reduction in functional capabilities.
fha.effCrew: Crew fly on standby instrumentation alone, without primary flight/navigation displays, in a demanding partial-panel state — physical distress or excessive workload approaching the limit of reliable task performance, particularly in IMC, on approach and landing.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; the flight crew face the workload described above.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes the independent standby instrument remains available on total loss of the primary display chain (it shares no supply/sensor/processing per §5.11.3) and provides a survivable but degraded means to fly and land, keeping the condition Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If total display loss can occur concurrently with, or take out, the standby means, the condition becomes Catastrophic. Confirm the standby instrument's independence holds under the credited total-loss cause and quantify partial-panel approach/landing capability in IMC.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes the independent standby instrument remains available on total loss of the primary display chain (it shares no supply/sensor/processing per §5.11.3) and provides a survivable but degraded means to fly and land, keeping the condition Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If total display loss can occur concurrently with, or take out, the standby means, the condition becomes Catastrophic. Confirm the standby instrument's independence holds under the credited total-loss cause and quantify partial-panel approach/landing capability in IMC. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of primary display leaves only standby instrumentation; a large reduction in functional capabilities with crew workload such that reliable task performance is threatened; "a large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities", AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4; "excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely", §3.1.4 (HAZ-2). [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Hazardous (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: With detection retained but no means to extinguish a nacelle or APU fire, an in-flight fire that would otherwise be suppressed can propagate to structure, fuel and adjacent systems — a large reduction in functional capabilities and safety margins that can progress to loss of the airplane if the fire is not otherwise controlled.
fha.effCrew: Crew are alerted by the retained fire warning but the fire handle discharge produces no extinguishing; workload rises sharply managing an uncontrollable fire and expediting diversion/landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; occupant risk is confined to the flight crew, exposed to a potentially uncontrollable fire.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on whether a detected nacelle/APU fire, with extinguishing lost, is reliably controllable by engine shutdown + fuel isolation before propagation to structure. Assumed controllable-but-degraded (Hazardous). Firewall integrity substantiation and fire-propagation timing would confirm; evidence that shutdown does not arrest the fire would move this to Catastrophic.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on whether a detected nacelle/APU fire, with extinguishing lost, is reliably controllable by engine shutdown + fuel isolation before propagation to structure. Assumed controllable-but-degraded (Hazardous). Firewall integrity substantiation and fire-propagation timing would confirm; evidence that shutdown does not arrest the fire would move this to Catastrophic. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Detection is retained; the loss is of the extinguishing means only. A fire that cannot be extinguished by the assumed means is a "large reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4). Not credited as Catastrophic on the aircraft axis because a nacelle/APU fire may still be controlled by engine shutdown, fuel isolation and expedited landing — a fire that reliably escalates to hull loss would carry CAT-1. sevBasis HAZ-1. [anchor HAZ-1 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft large · Crew large · Occupants severe injuries or few fatalities → Hazardous (all three axes at the catastrophic step). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Reduced extinguishing capability — e.g. one bottle of a cross-plumbed pair unavailable, or single-zone loss — leaves the remaining agent to address a fire; a significant reduction in functional capabilities but a first-shot discharge into the affected nacelle remains available.
fha.effCrew: Fire warning and handle function retained for at least one discharge; crew workload significantly increased if a re-shot is needed and unavailable, but the primary extinguishing action is still commandable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; occupant risk confined to flight crew.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes 'partial' leaves at least one usable discharge into the affected zone (cross-plumbed two-bottle-per-pair architecture). If the partial loss instead removes all agent from a single nacelle with no cross-feed to it, that nacelle's classification approaches the complete-loss (Hazardous) case; the specific partial state needs definition.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes 'partial' leaves at least one usable discharge into the affected zone (cross-plumbed two-bottle-per-pair architecture). If the partial loss instead removes all agent from a single nacelle with no cross-feed to it, that nacelle's classification approaches the complete-loss (Hazardous) case; the specific partial state needs definition. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: With detection and at least a first extinguishing shot retained, the loss is a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3). Not Hazardous because a fire can still be addressed by the remaining agent. sevBasis MAJ-1. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants discomfort → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: Uncommanded discharge of an extinguisher bottle into a nacelle or the APU expends agent with no fire present, leaving that zone without extinguishing capacity should a real fire subsequently occur — a slight-to-significant reduction in functional capability depending on whether a re-shot remains.
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted to a discharge; workload to assess a false/inadvertent event and to note the depleted agent, and dispatch impact for the return sector given no line maintenance at the strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no direct occupant effect.
fha.judgementNote: Assumes inadvertent discharge is of one bottle and does not itself create a hazard (agent release into an unmanned nacelle). If a spurious discharge is coincident with a real fire in the same pair, the residual capacity is reduced — that combination is a CMA/combination item, not this single-condition row.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Assumes inadvertent discharge is of one bottle and does not itself create a hazard (agent release into an unmanned nacelle). If a spurious discharge is coincident with a real fire in the same pair, the residual capacity is reduced — that combination is a CMA/combination item, not this single-condition row. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An inadvertent discharge with no fire present produces a "slight reduction in safety margins" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.2) — the agent is expended but no fire is aggravated and the second bottle of the pair (cross-plumbed) remains. sevBasis MIN-1. [anchor MIN-1 — Minor] Levels: Aircraft slight · Crew slight · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Minor (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew oxygen supply
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No direct effect on airplane systems; the airplane remains fully controllable. The consequence is realised only if a pressurisation loss, smoke or fume event then occurs, at which point the crew have no protective breathing means.
fha.effCrew: With oxygen supply lost, a subsequent depressurisation at FL260 or a smoke/fume event leaves the flight crew without breathing oxygen — physical distress or incapacitation such that the crew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks; there is no passenger oxygen and only two crew nominally aboard.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no passengers exposed.
fha.judgementNote: Turns on the combination: total oxygen loss is benign in isolation but Hazardous when coincident with depressurisation at FL260 or a smoke event. Cylinder pressure is a displayed dispatch item, so total loss is normally detected on the ground; an in-flight latent total loss coincident with a pressurisation event is the sizing case. If the combination is shown extremely improbable and detected, the isolated-condition classification is lower; DER disposition and CMA needed.
fha.comments: ⚠ JUDGEMENT CALL — classified on limited information; engineer to confirm. Turns on the combination: total oxygen loss is benign in isolation but Hazardous when coincident with depressurisation at FL260 or a smoke event. Cylinder pressure is a displayed dispatch item, so total loss is normally detected on the ground; an in-flight latent total loss coincident with a pressurisation event is the sizing case. If the combination is shown extremely improbable and detected, the isolated-condition classification is lower; DER disposition and CMA needed. | AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Loss of crew oxygen is latent until a pressurisation/smoke event; combined with such an event the crew face "physical distress or excessive workload such that the flightcrew cannot be relied upon to perform their tasks accurately or completely" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.4). Not Catastrophic on its own because it requires the coincident event; the un-annunciated combination is a §25.1309/CMA item. sevBasis HAZ-2. [anchor HAZ-2 — Hazardous] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew large · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Hazardous (crew axis governs). — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of crew oxygen supply
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effAc: No direct effect on airplane systems. Reduced oxygen quantity/flow shortens the protected diversion time available after a depressurisation or smoke event.
fha.effCrew: One cylinder or one regulator lost leaves the crossover-fed manifold supplying the crew at reduced reserve — either cylinder is stated capable of supplying the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve; crew workload significantly increased managing a shortened protected diversion.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; no passengers exposed.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Partial loss preserves crew breathing oxygen at reduced reserve for the required duration, so a subsequent event still leaves protection but with reduced margin — a "significant reduction in safety margins or functional capabilities" (AC 25.1309-1B §3.1.3). Not Hazardous because the crew retain a usable protective breathing means. sevBasis MAJ-1. [anchor MAJ-1 — Major] Levels: Aircraft significant · Crew significant · Occupants none or slight inconvenience → Major (aircraft and crew axes govern). — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.text: NZD open/close/latch and lock-sensing are aircraft functions, while the door's single-load-path structural and pressure-boundary integrity is structure, not a function.
assumptions.rationale: §5.7 mixes a mechanised behaviour (operate/latch/sense) with an explicit structural role; the modeling rule bars structure as a function, so I split them.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the safety organisation elects to carry door structural integrity functionally, an additional aircraft function would be added; otherwise it is handled by structural analysis and PRA.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide cargo access and pressure boundary at nose (all three sub-functions)

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure

assumptions.text: CRG blade restraint (straps, winches, tension monitoring) is a function, while the hold floor hard points that react restraint loads are structure.
assumptions.rationale: §5.8.3 states the hard points carry no redundancy and are structural; the mechanised restraint is a behaviour and is captured as a function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hard-point integrity is to be tracked functionally rather than by structural analysis/PRA, an additional function or interface would be required.
assumptions.usedFor: Restrain payload (both sub-functions)

citations.quote: There is no redundancy in the hold floor hard points

assumptions.text: The four resource systems (FUE, HYD, EPS, EWS) are not authored as aircraft functions; fuel delivery to engines is retained as a behaviour because the SDD states FUE 'delivers' and 'manages' rather than merely supplying a passive resource.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 tags FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS as resources, but §5.2.1 describes FUE performing active delivery and mass-management behaviours; the modeling rule bars power/fuel as functions, creating a judgement boundary.
assumptions.ifWrong: If 'deliver fuel to engines' is judged a pure resource provision, that function and its two sub-functions are removed and captured only in the Resources model.
assumptions.usedFor: Deliver fuel to engines (both sub-functions)

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems rather than to act on the aircraft

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen is authored as an aircraft function ('Provide crew oxygen') despite the SDD classifying OXY as a resource in the §2.1 inventory.
assumptions.rationale: §2.1 tags OXY 'Resource' but §5.13.1 describes a crew-protection behaviour the aircraft accomplishes; the resource/function boundary is ambiguous for a consumable that acts on the crew.
assumptions.ifWrong: If OXY is strictly a resource, the 'Provide crew oxygen' function and its sub-function are removed and the capability is captured only in the resources model.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide crew oxygen / Supply breathing oxygen to crew masks

citations.quote: OXY Crew Oxygen Resource Supplies flight crew; consumes ECS signal

assumptions.text: The nose cargo door is decomposed only as the open/close/lock behaviour (a function); its structural and pressure-boundary role is excluded from the functional decomposition.
assumptions.rationale: §5.7.3 states the door 'is treated as structure', and the modeling rule excludes structural support from functional-FHA items, but the same door also performs an operable behaviour.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the door's pressure-boundary integrity is to be treated functionally rather than structurally, an additional function would be required and the PRA/structural split changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide cargo access / Open, close and lock the nose cargo door

citations.quote: the door is a single load path and is treated as structure.

assumptions.text: Per-engine thrust is captured as one generic 'Generate propulsive thrust per engine' sub-function rather than four separately-failing rows.
assumptions.rationale: §5.1.5 shows left/right pairs in separate zones with non-commingled services, implying independence, but the SDD does not mandate four discrete function rows; granularity is a judgement.
assumptions.ifWrong: If per-engine independence must be modelled explicitly at function level, this single row splits into four independent sub-functions feeding the asymmetric-thrust directional-control case.
assumptions.usedFor: Provide thrust / Generate propulsive thrust per engine

citations.quote: Left and right engine pairs sit in separate zones.

assumptions.text: Fuel mass distribution error can develop below the 1,200 kg imbalance annunciation threshold, justifying a crew-Unaware malfunction variant for SF-004.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the annunciation threshold but not the detection resolution below it, so an undetected sub-threshold drift is plausible and must carry its own Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-004 Unaware row is removed and only the Aware malfunction row remains.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004 Unaware row (Undetected fuel mass distribution error)

citations.quote: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg and is limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

assumptions.text: An erroneous or slowly-diverging roll command/response can develop below crew detection thresholds when envelope protection and displays mask small deviations, justifying a crew-Unaware SF-005 malfunction row.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes annunciated degraded laws but does not establish detection thresholds for small erroneous roll behaviour, so an undetected variant cannot be dismissed for the whole function.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-005 Unaware row is removed and both roll malfunction variants remain only on the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005 Unaware row (erroneous/uncommanded roll — undetected)

citations.quote: Degraded laws are annunciated.

assumptions.text: Reverse thrust is provided by the two inboard engines only, so its total loss and asymmetric partial loss are configuration facts feeding the SF-002 conditions.
assumptions.rationale: The reverser architecture governs which SF-002 partial/malfunction conditions are physically meaningful; the row wording assumes this two-inboard arrangement.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-002 asymmetric partial and inadvertent-deployment conditions would be re-scoped to the actual reverser count and placement.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002 row (all conditions)

citations.quote: Thrust reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only.

assumptions.text: Erroneous or uncommanded pitch and yaw behaviour can develop below the crew's detection threshold, justifying a distinct crew-Unaware malfunction row for each axis.
assumptions.rationale: The function list and SDD give the actuation architecture but no detection-threshold data for the control axes, forcing a judgement on whether the unaware variant is applicable.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-006/SF-007 Unaware rows collapse into the Aware rows and the undetected malfunction conditions drop out of the matrix.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006 Unaware row, SF-007 Unaware row

citations.quote: asymmetry and jam discretes

assumptions.text: Erroneous gear position indication can persist undetected because the two downlock circuits reporting agreement gives the crew no independent cue that the indication itself is wrong.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD grounds dual downlock sensing and flight-deck indication but does not state whether a failed indication is independently cross-checkable, forcing a judgement on the unaware case.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-010 Unaware row is removed and erroneous indication is captured only on the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010 Unaware row

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: Ground-load-support failures produce intrinsic, self-evident cues (attitude, ground contact) so no crew-Unaware variant is authored for SF-009.
assumptions.rationale: The function is a ground load-path behaviour with no annunciation described in the SDD; the awareness-dismissal reasoning is filed here per house style rather than in the matrix cell.
assumptions.ifWrong: An SF-009 Unaware row would be required for any degradation that can develop without a physical cue.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009 Aware row

citations.quote: supports the aircraft on the ground, absorbs landing and taxi loads

assumptions.text: Ground deceleration and steering failures produce immediate heading/deceleration cues during the ground roll, so the crew-unaware variant is inapplicable except for a bias developing below the crew detection threshold.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives brake-temperature and steering command paths but no explicit alert for a small steering/braking bias, forcing a judgement on where the awareness split falls.
assumptions.ifWrong: If sub-threshold bias is not physically possible, the SF-012 Unaware row is deleted; if larger undetected losses are possible, the Unaware rows on SF-011/SF-012 must be broadened.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware row (Undetected erroneous ground steering); SF-011 awareness split

citations.quote: Brake temperature is monitored continuously and a turnaround limit is displayed.

assumptions.text: The nose visor is a ground-only function that cannot be operated in flight, so its failure conditions are confined to ground phases and the in-flight pressure-boundary hazard is carried by SF-014 lock integrity.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the door cannot be operated in flight, which determines whether SF-013 carries any in-flight condition or defers it to SF-014.
assumptions.ifWrong: If in-flight visor motion is credible, SF-013 gains an in-flight uncommanded-motion condition rather than deferring it to SF-014.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-013 rows

citations.quote: cannot be operated in flight. Lock status is displayed on the flight deck at all times

assumptions.text: A false 'locked' indication from the lock sensing (SF-015) is a crew-unaware condition because the crew has indication only and would continue on the reported state, mitigated by the dual dissimilar sensing paths.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes two dissimilar sensing paths but does not state that a common-mode false-locked report is precluded, forcing a judgement that the Unaware condition is retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the dual dissimilar paths preclude a common false-locked report, the SF-015 Unaware row narrows or is removed and the SF-014+SF-015 combined condition is downgraded.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-015 Unaware row; SF-014 Unaware row

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.text: The blade restraint tension monitoring loop can fail such that a loss of restraint develops without annunciation, because the loop is a single instrumented run whose coverage is unconfirmed.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD flags the loop's coverage as a recorded item, so the crew-unaware variant of loss/erroneous restraint cannot be dismissed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If coverage is complete and independently confirmed, the SF-016/SF-017 Unaware rows collapse and only the Aware rows remain.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016 Unaware row, SF-017 Unaware row

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.text: Cabin pressure differential errors can develop below crew detection thresholds because differential/cabin-altitude indication is a single sensed source shared into the avionics and oxygen logic.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not establish an independent second cue that would make every pressurisation malfunction self-evident, so a crew-unaware variant is retained.
assumptions.ifWrong: If differential errors are always independently annunciated (e.g. by the relief-valve activation being observable), the SF-019 Unaware row collapses into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019 Unaware row

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: SF-016 (winches), SF-017 (tension loop), SF-018 (controllers/valves/fans) and SF-019 (controllers/valves) consume electrical power, and SF-018/SF-020 additionally consume engine bleed, as resources rather than functions.
assumptions.rationale: Resource consumption is captured in the Resources model, not as functions; noted so the FHA does not author 'provide power/bleed' failure conditions here.
assumptions.ifWrong: No condition changes; this prevents mis-authoring resource losses as function-level failure conditions.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-016, SF-017, SF-018, SF-019, SF-020 all rows

citations.quote: Two air cycle packs are supplied with bleed air from the four engines through a cross-bleed manifold

assumptions.text: Loss of probe/windshield heat can develop undetected below crew detection thresholds despite individual monitoring, so a crew-Unaware variant of the erroneous/undetected condition is retained.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the elements are 'monitored individually' but does not establish the detection latency or alerting coverage, so undetected accretion cannot be excluded.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-021 Unaware row is removed and the undetected condition folds into the Aware row.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-021 Unaware row (Undetected loss of probe ice protection)

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually

assumptions.text: Erroneous flight/navigation display and erroneous air data/inertial reference can be presented without an accompanying alert (misleading but plausible data), supporting a crew-Unaware row for each.
assumptions.rationale: The provided text establishes redundancy and cross-monitoring intent but not that every erroneous-data mode is annunciated, so a below-threshold undetected variant must be carried.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-023 and SF-024 Unaware rows are removed if all erroneous-data modes are shown to be annunciated.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-023 Unaware row, SF-024 Unaware row

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data

assumptions.text: The standby instrument, sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays, provides independent cross-check such that erroneous standby data is detectable by disagreement, so no separate Unaware row is emitted for SF-025.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the standby shares nothing with the primaries; without a modelled alert this cross-check is assumed available, and awareness-dismissal reasoning is filed here rather than in a matrix cell.
assumptions.ifWrong: An SF-025 crew-Unaware row carrying 'Undetected erroneous standby flight information' must be added.
assumptions.usedFor: Absence of an SF-025 Unaware row

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Common erroneous air data (SF-024) may simultaneously corrupt primary displays (SF-023) and mislead the standby cross-check (SF-025), constituting a combined failure condition to be assessed together.
assumptions.rationale: The pitot/static/AOA sensing feeds multiple consumers; the provided text does not confirm full sensor dissimilarity between primary and standby air data, forcing a combined-condition flag.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Combined-column flag is dropped if the standby air data source is shown fully dissimilar and independent from the ADIRU air data.
assumptions.usedFor: Combined condition flag across SF-023/SF-024/SF-025

citations.quote: pitot, static and angle-of-attack sensing

assumptions.text: The crew alerting function can fail in ways that are not self-annunciated, so a crew-Unaware variant of its partial loss and erroneous behaviour is applicable.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes dual independent processing channels but does not state that loss or corruption of the alerting output is itself alerted, so I cannot ground crew detection of an alerting-function failure.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an independent monitor annunciates alerting-function health, the SF-026 crew-Unaware row collapses and only the Both row remains.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026 crew-Unaware row (Undetected partial loss of crew alerting; Undetected erroneous crew alerting)

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: A dormant loss of fire/overheat detection can exist below crew detection thresholds because there is no positive continuous confirmation the detection is live until a fire occurs.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states AND logic degrading to single-loop but does not state that total loss of detection is itself annunciated to the crew, so undetected loss cannot be ruled out.
assumptions.ifWrong: If loss of both loops is continuously annunciated, the SF-027 crew-Unaware row is removed and detection loss is fully crew-Aware.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-027 crew-Unaware row (Undetected loss of fire and overheat detection)

citations.quote: an AND logic between them for warning, degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.text: Crew oxygen failures are treated as crew-Aware because cylinder pressure is displayed continuously and low-pressure alerting is provided, and mask flow is evident on donning.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives continuous pressure display and low-pressure alerting but not whether a delivery fault at the mask is annunciated; awareness-dismissal reasoning is filed here rather than in the matrix cell.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an in-line delivery fault can occur without pressure-display or flow cues, SF-029 needs a crew-Unaware row for the undetected erroneous-delivery condition.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-029 Both row awareness assignment

citations.quote: Cylinder pressure is displayed continuously on the flight deck and is a dispatch item

assumptions.text: Fire extinguishing is treated as crew-Aware because discharge status is reported to the crew and extinguishing is a deliberate crew action through the fire handles.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states discharge status is an output and extinguishing is crew-commanded, so both failure to discharge and inadvertent discharge present crew cues; no crew-Unaware variant is grounded.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a bottle can fail to discharge without status feedback, SF-028 needs a crew-Unaware row for undetected loss of extinguishing.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-028 Both row awareness assignment

citations.quote: discharge status; automatic APU shutdown and fuel isolation on APU fire

assumptions.text: The adjacent, separately-clipped-and-shielded A/B brake bundles in each main gear bay do not, as currently installed, defeat a single tyre-burst trajectory taking both systems.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the A/B gear-bay co-location as an item to be examined but provides no shielding geometry or debris-cone analysis to confirm separation is adequate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If separation is already adequate, the tyre-burst CSFL against dual braking collapses and the first proposed requirement becomes verification-only rather than a finding.
assumptions.usedFor: Tire burst PRA row — CSFL and requirements against SF-011 braking

citations.quote: That co-location is a recorded zonal item.

assumptions.text: The air-data probes and static ports feeding the three ADIRUs are mounted on the forward fuselage within the bird-strike-exposed region.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms the two ice detectors are forward-fuselage-mounted but does not explicitly state probe/static-port locations; ADIRU exposure to strike is inferred from conventional siting.
assumptions.ifWrong: If probes are sited outside the credible strike region, the air-data-redundancy portion of the bird-strike CSFL and the first bird-strike requirement drop.
assumptions.usedFor: Bird strike PRA row — CSFL and requirement against SF-024/SF-023 air data

citations.quote: Two ice detectors of the same type are installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage.

assumptions.text: The fly-by-wire FCS uses no non-conductive/composite primary structure whose lightning protection differs from metallic bonding assumptions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not state the airframe material, and the lightning coupling path and the applicable protection means (bonding vs composite design) depend on it.
assumptions.ifWrong: The Lightning mitigation and requirement candidates shift toward composite lightning-protection design (§25.1316) and the affected-zone coupling assessment changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Lightning PRA row mitigation and requirements

citations.quote: For nonmetallic components, compliance with paragraph (a) of this section may be shown by

assumptions.text: The DC-essential-bus and standby-instrument independence claim is intended to survive a single lightning/HIRF event coupling into the primary electronics.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts the standby shares no supply/sensor/processing but does not qualify that claim against an electromagnetic common-mode event.
assumptions.ifWrong: The CSFL for both rows widens and additional segregation/shielding requirements are needed to preserve the last-resort display path.
assumptions.usedFor: Lightning and HIRF CSFL and standby-instrument requirement candidates

citations.quote: a standby instrument sharing nothing with the primaries

assumptions.text: The hail/ice impact and icing threats are assessed at drawing/model stage because the SDD describes routing, detector positions and the ice envelope as preliminary and not frozen.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly flags routing, gear/bogie count and the ice envelope as preliminary, so no fixed installation geometry is available to model trajectories against.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the installation were frozen, the studies would move from survivability-at-model-stage to a fixed-geometry assessment and specific separation distances could be stated rather than deferred.
assumptions.usedFor: Both PRA rows (Hail; Ice)

citations.quote: The routing definition is preliminary. Bundle contents are assigned but final bundle build and clamping positions are not frozen.

assumptions.text: The two ice detectors, being of the same type on opposite sides of the forward fuselage, are exposed to a common hail/ice-impact and icing environment such that both may be lost from one event.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the same-type commonality as an item for examination but does not establish that the two channels survive a single environmental event independently.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detector independence to the impact/icing environment is substantiated, the detector common-source loss is removed from the CSFL and the SHOWN-ACCEPTABLE claim on detection is not needed.
assumptions.usedFor: CSFL and detection requirement in both rows; SF-022

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.text: Wing anti-ice, cowl anti-ice and ECS pack conditioning share the cross-bleed manifold such that a manifold loss or contention is a common source across those functions.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states ice protection bleed is taken from the same manifold that supplies the environmental packs, but does not quantify isolation or contention behaviour.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the manifold provides isolated segments that prevent common loss/contention, the shared-manifold common source is removed from the Ice CSFL.
assumptions.usedFor: Ice-row CSFL and the anti-ice single-source requirement; SF-020, SF-021

citations.quote: taken from the same manifold that supplies the environmental packs, through piccolo distribution.

assumptions.text: The single-blade payload presents no combustible palletised fire load, so hold detection-only (no suppression) is the design intent to be substantiated rather than an omission.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD records the no-suppression decision as an assumption to be substantiated but does not provide the fire-load analysis that would close it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a credible combustible hold fire load exists, the no-suppression decision fails acceptability and a hold suppression requirement becomes mandatory, changing the mitigation and requirements of this PRA row.
assumptions.usedFor: In-flight cabin/hold fire and smoke — mitigation GAP and requirement on detection-only substantiation

citations.quote: the hold carries a single blade and no combustible palletised load, and hold suppression is deliberately not fitted

assumptions.text: FCC 2 (zone 300) and FCC 3 (zone 400), plus the HV/LV crossing points in zone 300, are physically close enough that a single hold fire could thermally damage more than one, defeating the claimed FCC/network independence.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD places FCC 2 and the HV/LV crossing points both in zone 300 but gives no thermal-separation distances to confirm a fire cannot bridge them.
assumptions.ifWrong: If thermal separation is adequate, the common-cause CSFL claim and the second requirement are unnecessary and the row's severity emphasis on flight-control loss drops.
assumptions.usedFor: csfl claim and the flight-control common-mode requirement in this PRA row

citations.quote: Mid hold (stations 4–6) Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points

assumptions.text: Nacelles 610–640 house engines 1–4 in outboard-to-inboard-to-outboard numbering, with 610/620 driving HYD A and 630/640 driving HYD B.
assumptions.rationale: §3 lists nacelles 610–640 generically; the engine number and hydraulic-pump assignment per nacelle is inferred from §5.1.2/§5.4.2 rather than stated per zone.
assumptions.ifWrong: The housedFunctions and the HYD-A/HYD-B attributions on the four nacelle rows shift, changing which fault trees receive the common-cause note.

citations.quote: System A is pumped by engine-driven pumps on engines 1 and 2; system B by engine-driven pumps on engines 3 and 4

assumptions.text: FCC 1, FCC 2 and FCC 3 are the three dissimilar flight control computers of §5.3.2, one installed in each of the forward (120), mid (300) and aft (400) equipment bays.
assumptions.rationale: §3 places 'FCC' in zones 120/300/400 and §5.3.5 names three separate bays, but the SDD does not explicitly map each numbered FCC to a zone.
assumptions.ifWrong: The independence/separation findings on rows 120, 300 and 400 (three-computer dissimilarity preserved by three-bay installation) would be mis-stated.

citations.quote: The three flight control computers are installed in three separate bays — forward equipment bay, mid equipment bay and aft equipment bay

assumptions.text: The APPLICABLE tyre-burst and rotor/engine-burst particular risks that bear on the gear bays and nacelles are (or will be) captured in dedicated PRAs, so the ZSA references rather than re-analyses them.
assumptions.rationale: App K.3.1 assigns cross-zone well-known physical hazards to the PRA; the project PRA register contains a tyre-burst entry (PRA-81342) but no rotor/engine-burst entry yet.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no rotor/engine-burst PRA is raised, those inherent nacelle hazards would need to be carried as ZSA findings in 610–640 rather than referenced out.

citations.quote: its routing is retained as an item requiring particular-risk and zonal attention

assumptions.text: The consolidated crew alert list applies the standard warning/caution/advisory prioritisation hierarchy and attention-getting cues required by §25.1322 even though the document states only that it is 'prioritised'.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names a single prioritised alert list but does not describe alert categories, colour convention, or dual-sense attention cues, forcing an assumption about how §25.1322 is met.
assumptions.ifWrong: The alerting rows judged against detection/intelligibility (multi-alert) considerations would need reclassification and additional findings against §25.1322(b)/(c)/(e).
assumptions.usedFor: Consolidated prioritised crew alert list rows

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: The single prioritised crew alert list is the primary cue by which the crew perceives a source loss, imbalance, or degraded-law condition.
assumptions.rationale: The document describes a consolidated alerting list but does not enumerate which specific conditions raise which alert level, so the mapping of condition to cue is assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: Perception-level rows that rely on the alerting list as the cue would need a different or additional cue, or become findings of a missing cue.
assumptions.usedFor: Loss of a source row; degraded flight control law row

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.text: Loss of thrust from all four engines is not recoverable by crew action and results in hull loss.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the one-engine-inop dispatch case and a mature-engine IFSD rate but does not state the outcome of losing all four engines or any glide/restart credit.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a credited glide-and-restart or independent thrust source exists that makes the all-engine case survivable, SF-001-TL drops below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-001-TL

citations.quote: designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: An uncommanded or erroneous thrust event is detectable by the crew via engine parameter display and counterable within available time, and its magnitude is bounded such that it does not exceed available directional-control authority at the outboard moment arm.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD credits FADEC overspeed/overtemperature protection and displays engine parameters but does not bound an uncommanded/erroneous thrust excursion magnitude at the 28 m moment arm.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a large single-engine uncommanded/erroneous excursion near V1 can exceed rudder authority, SF-001-M and SF-001-M2 rise toward Hazardous.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: An in-flight inboard-engine thrust-reverser deployment at operating speed exceeds the aircraft's controllable envelope and is credited as loss of the airplane.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states in-flight deployment is inhibited but gives no controllability/recoverability analysis for the case where the inhibits are defeated, forcing a credited outcome for the classification.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-M and SF-002-M2 reduce from Catastrophic to Hazardous, and their crew/occupant axes come down with the aircraft axis.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-M (Inadvertent reverse thrust deployment), SF-002-M2 (Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight)

citations.quote: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

assumptions.text: Wheel braking (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) plus the 1,800 m/~1,080 m margin keep loss of reverse thrust within stopping margin on the semi-prepared surface, so reverse thrust is not credited to meet the landing-distance requirement.
assumptions.rationale: No landing-performance analysis distinguishing dry/contaminated stopping distance with and without reverse thrust is provided, so the stopping-margin dependence on reverse thrust had to be assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-TL rises from Minor toward Major and SF-002-PL from Major toward Hazardous if reverse thrust is required to meet 1,800 m on a wet/contaminated strip.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-TL (Complete loss of reverse thrust), SF-002-PL (Partial loss of reverse thrust — asymmetric)

citations.quote: predicted landing rollout is approximately 1,080 m, and the margin between the two is the basis on which braking degradation is assessed.

assumptions.text: Asymmetric reverse thrust on one inboard engine during the landing roll can be arrested by nose-wheel steering and differential braking without a runway excursion on the semi-prepared surface.
assumptions.rationale: No directional-control analysis for one-side reverse at the inboard moment arm on a low-friction strip is provided, so the recoverable-outcome credit had to be assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-002-PL rises from Major to Hazardous if the asymmetric-reverse yaw produces an unrecoverable excursion.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-002-PL (Partial loss of reverse thrust — asymmetric)

citations.quote: Nose wheel steering is hydraulic, commanded from tillers and rudder pedals

assumptions.text: Complete loss of fuel delivery starves all four engines simultaneously (the APU cannot sustain flight), giving total loss of thrust rather than a single-engine loss.
assumptions.rationale: SF-003 is the aircraft function 'deliver fuel at engine demand' to all engines; its complete loss is total, but the classification depends on treating it as removing thrust from all four engines together.
assumptions.ifWrong: If 'complete loss' is scoped to less than all engines, SF-003-TL is over-classified; total delivery loss to all engines is the credited case here.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-TL (Complete loss of fuel delivery)

citations.quote: The fuel system stores fuel, delivers it to the four engines and the APU at the pressure and flow the engines require

assumptions.text: After a single-engine fuel-delivery loss, cross-feed/collector reserve restores the affected engine or the aircraft safely continues three-engine to a suitable aerodrome.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states redundant feed paths and single-engine-out continuation but does not state whether the affected engine's delivery is restored or the timing of continuation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the affected engine cannot be restored and margins erode near the ground, SF-003-PL rises above Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-003-PL

citations.quote: continue to a suitable aerodrome following the loss of any one engine at or after V1

assumptions.text: Erroneous fuel delivery pressure is annunciated and bounded to a single engine, not a common multi-engine condition acting through the shared cross-feed gallery.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD provides per-engine collectors and low-pressure discretes but does not bound simultaneous erroneous pressure across engines sharing the single spanwise gallery.
assumptions.ifWrong: If undetected and simultaneously erroneous across multiple engines, SF-003-M rises to Hazardous or higher.

citations.quote: low-pressure and imbalance discretes to the flight deck

assumptions.text: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation, cued by the 1,200 kg imbalance annunciation, reliably arrest CG and wing-bending migration before the 3,000 kg structural limit.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD gives the annunciation threshold, the structural limit and the manual reversion capability but not the timing or authority of the manual recovery.
assumptions.ifWrong: If manual reversion cannot hold CG/wing-bending within limits, SF-004-TL rises to Hazardous.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-TL

citations.quote: The crew can select manual cross-feed and can isolate any tank

assumptions.text: No passengers are carried in flight; the hold is unoccupied, so occupant effects are none for every fuel failure condition.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the hold is not occupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried, the passenger axis on each row would need reassessment.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Loss of the wing-imbalance annunciation is credible and, when it occurs, the imbalance can progress past the 3,000 kg structural limit before other cues prompt crew action.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the annunciation and the structural limit but does not describe the annunciation's independence or the aircraft's response at the limit, forcing an assumption for the undetected case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the annunciation cannot credibly be lost, or the aircraft response at 3,000 kg imbalance is benign/recoverable, SF-004-M3 drops from Hazardous to Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004-M3 — Undetected fuel mass distribution error

citations.quote: Fuel imbalance between left and right wings is annunciated at 1,200 kg and is limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

assumptions.text: No usable roll control remains from other means (e.g. differential thrust across the four engines) after complete loss of ailerons and spoilers.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names ailerons and spoilers as the roll effectors but does not state whether differential thrust or rudder-induced roll can be credited as a survivable roll means.
assumptions.ifWrong: If differential thrust provides usable roll control, SF-005-TL is not hull loss and the class reduces below Catastrophic on the aircraft axis.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-005-TL — Complete loss of roll control

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers; pitch by an all-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser

assumptions.text: An undetected erroneous or uncommanded roll develops into an unrecoverable roll departure before the crew can detect and arrest it.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes FCS redundancy but does not state annunciation coverage, handling margin, or time-to-departure for an undetected roll malfunction, which the class turns on.
assumptions.ifWrong: If independent alerting or handling margin ensures timely crew detection and recovery, SF-005-M3 and SF-005-M4 drop from Catastrophic to a lower class.

citations.quote: three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: An aware erroneous or uncommanded roll is detectable from aircraft motion and displays and arrestable by crew corrective input, holding effects at a significant (not large) reduction in safety margins.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD does not quantify roll authority remaining or crew response time for the aware case; the Major class assumes the crew reliably recovers.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the aware roll excursion cannot be reliably arrested within margins, SF-005-M and SF-005-M2 escalate above Major.

citations.quote: Roll is by two-segment ailerons and multi-function spoilers

assumptions.text: The mechanical reversion path provides pitch control only via stabiliser trim, so a complete loss of pitch control means every pitch means (elevators, stabiliser, and reversion) is unavailable together.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states a mechanical reversion path to the stabiliser trim; SF-006-TL is only complete loss if that path is also lost, which the FCIM row asserts.
assumptions.ifWrong: If reversion via stabiliser trim survives, the condition is a partial loss (SF-006-PL), not a complete loss, and would be classified separately.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-TL

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim

assumptions.text: The flight crew can detect an erroneous or uncommanded pitch response and revert to a degraded control law or mechanical stabiliser trim in time to arrest divergence in the aware cases.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dissimilar FCCs and a mechanical reversion path exist but gives no monitor coverage, alerting or handling-quality timing to confirm timely crew recovery.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-006-M and SF-006-M2 would rise from Hazardous to Catastrophic where the crew cannot arrest the divergence at a critical phase.

citations.quote: A mechanical reversion path exists to the stabiliser trim and to the lower rudder segment only

assumptions.text: No independent FCS monitor reliably annunciates an erroneous pitch command in the undetected case, so no crew action is credited.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes voting FCCs and annunciation of degraded laws but does not establish detection/annunciation of an erroneous command that passes the vote, which the undetected split assumes absent.
assumptions.ifWrong: If effective independent monitoring annunciates the erroneous command, SF-006-M3 reverts from Catastrophic toward the aware Hazardous case.

citations.quote: Primary control is fly-by-wire with three dissimilar flight control computers voting on command

assumptions.text: Residual pitch authority in the within-MAC partial loss is sufficient to continue and land, while the outside-MAC partial loss cannot assure recovery.
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM splits SF-006 partial loss into within-MAC and outside-MAC but the SDD gives no remaining-authority figures to bound each case.
assumptions.ifWrong: If within-MAC residual authority is insufficient, SF-006-PL rises to Hazardous; if outside-MAC recovery is in fact assured, SF-006-PL2 falls to Major.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-006-PL, SF-006-PL2

citations.quote: the control authority required across the flight envelope including the engine-out and blade-loaded cases

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so occupant effects below hull loss are limited to the flight crew.
assumptions.rationale: Occupant axis classification requires knowing who is aboard; the SDD states crew-only operation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants other than crew were carried, the occupant axis on the partial/malfunction rows could raise their class.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The outboard-engine-out case at the 28 m moment arm is the design-critical directional-control condition, so total loss of yaw prevents continued safe flight and landing.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the engine-out directional case as the rudder sizing case but does not state the classification consequence of losing yaw control against it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If yaw control is not flight-critical against the sizing case, SF-007-TL could drop from Catastrophic to Hazardous and the outside-MAC/erroneous rows soften.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.text: An undetected uncommanded pitch excursion grows unchecked because crew alerting is absent, and the credited worst-phase outcome is Hazardous rather than unrecoverable.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes pitch architecture but gives no excursion rate or detectability-from-cues data to settle whether an undetected departure is recoverable near the ground.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the undetected pitch departure is credibly unrecoverable in takeoff/landing, SF-006-M4 becomes Catastrophic.

citations.quote: pitch by an all-moving trimmable horizontal stabiliser with elevators

assumptions.text: Erroneous and partial-authority yaw malfunctions are magnitude-limited (by FCS command monitoring and split-segment authority) so the worst credited outcome is a recoverable large-margin loss, not hull loss.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual actuation and split rudder segments but does not quantify the maximum erroneous deflection or residual authority after a partial loss.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a full-authority erroneous or outside-MAC yaw condition is credible and unrecoverable, SF-007-M and SF-007-PL2 become Catastrophic.

citations.quote: each with its own actuation and its own hydraulic supply

assumptions.text: No occupants other than flight crew are aboard in any flight phase, so the occupant axis never drives the class above the crew/aircraft axes.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states the hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only.
