citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant-injury effects reduce to crew fatalities on hull loss and there are no passengers to injure short of hull loss.
assumptions.rationale: The effPax axis needs to know who is aboard; the FCIM/functions do not state occupancy so it is taken from the SDD.
assumptions.ifWrong: If persons are carried in the hold, the occupant axis on SF-007-M2 and SF-008 rows could rise and change the derived class.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: Uncommanded/erroneous yaw at the outboard 28 m moment arm can produce a large directional excursion that is arrestable by the crew when detected but unrecoverable when undetected.
assumptions.rationale: No handling-qualities or monitor-coverage data is provided; the class for the aware vs undetected yaw rows depends on this recovery/detection split.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection/recovery is reliable even in the undetected-labelled cases, SF-007-M3/M4 drop from Catastrophic to Hazardous; if unrecoverable when detected, SF-007-M2 rises to Catastrophic.

citations.quote: the sizing case for directional control is an outboard engine failure at V1 with the maximum blade payload

assumptions.text: A landing at the semi-prepared destination cannot be diverted to a longer commercial runway once committed, so degraded landing performance is assessed against the 1,800 m field length.
assumptions.rationale: The high-lift loss class depends on whether a longer field is reachable; the operating concept fixes the destination as a semi-prepared strip.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a longer diversion field is routinely available, SF-008-TL could drop to Major and SF-008-PL toward Minor.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-008-TL, SF-008-PL

citations.quote: delivered to a semi-prepared strip at the wind farm rather than to a commercial airport

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states asymmetry brakes exist but gives no arrest angle, response time or roll-margin data to confirm the split is arrested within controllable limits.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-008-M and SF-008-M2 rise from Major to Hazardous, and SF-008-M3 could reach Catastrophic if the asymmetry is unrecoverable near the ground.

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.text: Without asymmetry annunciation the crew detect an asymmetric high-lift deployment only from aircraft response and therefore respond late during the takeoff/approach/landing phases.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a robust independent cue restores timely crew correction, SF-008-M3 falls from Hazardous to Major.

assumptions.text: Complete loss of ground load support occurs under weight at touchdown or on the ground roll and is not recoverable by crew action, producing hull loss.
assumptions.rationale: The provided function is stated at aircraft level with no residual load-path or partial-support detail; the credited end effect had to be assumed to classify the top step.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a residual load path keeps the aircraft supported after the failure, SF-009-TL falls below Catastrophic.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-009-TL

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-010-TL escalates from Major toward Hazardous/Catastrophic because a gear-up landing becomes the credited outcome rather than a successful alternate extension.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-TL

citations.quote: Retraction and extension is by hydraulic system A with a free-fall alternate extension.

assumptions.text: A partial-gear landing on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip remains controllable without hull loss for the leg/bogie loss combinations of interest.

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-010-PL escalates from Major toward Hazardous if the residual footprint cannot carry the landing on a semi-prepared surface.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-010-PL

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-010-M drops below Hazardous if a positive WoW retraction inhibit makes ground collapse not credible, or the in-flight-only case dominates.

citations.quote: Uplocks and downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released

assumptions.ifWrong: SF-010-M3 drops from Hazardous to Major if the dissimilar cross-check keeps the true state detectable, restoring crew awareness before landing.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

assumptions.text: The Aeolus HL-1 hold is unoccupied in flight, so ground-deceleration failures expose only the two-to-four flight crew, not passengers.

assumptions.ifWrong: If occupants were carried in the hold the occupant axis on SF-011-TL and SF-011-M2 would rise and could push those rows toward Catastrophic.

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only

assumptions.text: The credited deceleration margin is the ~720 m difference between the 1,800 m landing-distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on the design semi-prepared surface.
assumptions.rationale: The FHA function objective states 'decelerate on the ground' but the margin driving loss/partial-loss severity comes only from the SDD figures, which are preliminary.

assumptions.rationale: The asymmetric-braking classification turns on whether the excursion is recoverable, which the SDD describes qualitatively but does not substantiate for the design surface.
assumptions.ifWrong: If ground-handling analysis shows the excursion is reliably arrested within strip width, SF-011-M2 lowers to Major.

citations.quote: Nose wheel steering is hydraulic, commanded from tillers and rudder pedals

assumptions.text: Rudder and differential/asymmetric braking provide adequate directional control on the ground roll after loss of nose-wheel steering on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.

assumptions.ifWrong: If alternate directional means are inadequate, SF-012-TL rises from Major toward Hazardous on the ground-roll phases.

assumptions.ifWrong: If steering hardware faults propagate to an in-flight consumer, additional flight-phase rows would be needed for the malfunction conditions.

assumptions.ifWrong: If an in-flight opening path exists, SF-013-M and SF-013-M2 remain Catastrophic as drafted; if the ground-only inhibit is fully substantiated, their in-flight class is removed and only a ground personnel hazard remains.

assumptions.ifWrong: If the interlock plus in-flight inhibit are substantiated as preventing any in-flight opening, SF-013-M/M2 in-flight class is removed; if not, the Catastrophic class stands and drives the derived integrity requirement.

assumptions.ifWrong: If closure geometry alone secures the door for flight and the pins are only a back-drive interlock, SF-014-TL in-flight severity may reduce; if the pins are the securing means, Catastrophic stands.

assumptions.ifWrong: If sensing/config-check independence is fully substantiated, SF-014-TL reduces to a detected ground dispatch stop plus a Major annunciation-loss combination; if not, the undetected in-flight Catastrophic class stands.

assumptions.ifWrong: If bogies share a common load-path element or the count changes, the OR width and independence of the SF-009-PL contributors change.

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

citations.quote: The number of gear legs and bogies is preliminary design data and is not frozen.

assumptions.text: Uncommanded retraction requires both an uplock/downlock release AND an unintended retraction drive, with a weight-on-wheels / gear-lever interlock normally preventing it.

citations.quote: Uplocks and downlocks are mechanically held and hydraulically released

assumptions.text: Erroneous gear indication requires both independent downlock proximity circuits to agree on a wrong state, because a single-circuit fault produces a disagreement the crew can see.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dual independent downlock sensing per unit but does not describe the voting/disagreement logic that turns two circuits into one indication.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a single erroneous circuit can drive the indication with no disagreement flag, the AND gate over the two circuits becomes an OR and each circuit becomes an order-1 cut set.

citations.quote: downlock status is sensed by two independent proximity circuits per unit

citations.quote: normally from system B and alternately from system A, with accumulator-supported emergency braking

citations.quote: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through each main gear bay in adjacent bundles

citations.quote: Anti-skid operates per wheel pair.

citations.quote: A → retraction / extension, steering; B → normal braking (A alternate)

assumptions.text: The single cross-bleed manifold is a common bleed-supply node whose failure removes bleed from both packs, making it an order-1 cut set for SF-018-TL.

assumptions.ifWrong: If the manifold segregates fully, the SPF basic event collapses into two independent side-supply branches and the SF-018-TL OR-input becomes an AND across sides.

citations.quote: a cross-bleed manifold with three isolation valves, so that either pack can be supplied from either side

assumptions.text: Electrical power (EPS) to the two pack controllers, outflow-related controls and distribution fans is treated as a resource basic event, and a total EPS loss to both controllers/fans can cause complete loss of conditioning.
assumptions.rationale: ECS interfaces list electrical power to controllers, valves and fans but the SDD does not give the bus split feeding each pack's controls and fans.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each pack's controls/fans are on segregated independent buses, the single 'loss of electrical power to both' basic event becomes an AND of two independent bus-loss events, removing that SPF.

citations.quote: electrical power to the controllers, valves and fans

assumptions.text: The two air cycle packs are independent such that loss of both requires two separate pack failures (AND), no shared pack-internal component is a single point.

assumptions.ifWrong: If a shared component (e.g. a common ram-air path or shared controller) exists, an additional order-1 basic event must be added under the SF-018-TL top as an OR input.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL 'Loss of conditioned-air generation (both packs unavailable)' AND gate

citations.quote: Two packs, four bleed sources through a cross-bleed manifold, two controllers, two outflow valves

assumptions.text: Bleed sources group into left-side engines, right-side engines and APU for the total-bleed-loss AND gate.

assumptions.ifWrong: If per-engine bleed availability must be modelled individually, the AND gate expands to four engine basic events plus APU, altering cut-set order.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-TL 'Loss of all bleed sources feeding the manifold' AND gate

citations.quote: bleed air from the four engines and the APU

assumptions.text: The two air cycle packs constitute two independent erroneous-output channels rather than a single shared conditioning path.

assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-018-M pack-channel OR branch collapses to a single basic event, removing that redundancy from the tree.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-018-M pack-channel OR gate

citations.quote: Two air cycle packs are supplied with bleed air from the four engines through a cross-bleed manifold with three isolation valves

assumptions.text: Independent positive and negative mechanical relief valves contribute to retaining differential control such that complete loss requires both control paths, the pneumatic backup and mechanical relief all unavailable.

assumptions.ifWrong: If mechanical relief does not count toward differential control, the top AND loses its mechanical-relief input and the tree admits a shallower cut set.

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The pneumatic backup mode is independent of the two digital controller/outflow-valve control paths.

assumptions.ifWrong: If the pneumatic backup shares an outflow valve with a digital path, that basic event must be merged as a repeated event and the AND independence claim revised.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-TL pneumatic-backup basic event

citations.quote: A pneumatic backup mode drives one outflow valve directly on cabin pressure.

assumptions.text: The two pressurisation controllers are supplied from distinct electrical sources so a single bus loss does not fail both.

citations.quote: Pressurisation control is by two digital controllers driving two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD says either valve is sufficient for control, which implies a single valve open can bleed differential; not explicitly stated for the failure direction.
assumptions.ifWrong: If both valves must open for a significant under-pressure, the erroneous-command branches become AND gates and the SPF flag is void.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-M single-outflow-valve-fails-open OR branch

citations.quote: two outflow valves, either valve being sufficient

assumptions.text: Independent positive/negative mechanical relief is a protection against over/under pressure structural limits and is not a contributor to erroneous under-pressure control below the relief band.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists relief as independent of the control system; its role as protection vs contributor for the under-pressure FC needs engineer confirmation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If negative-pressure relief maloperation itself causes under-pressure, an additional basic-event branch is required in SF-019-M.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-M exclusion of relief from the cause tree

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The positive pressure relief valve is functionally independent of the two digital controllers and the two outflow valves, so no single common failure defeats both control and relief.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states relief protects structure independently of the control system but does not evidence power, sensing or physical separation between relief and control at part-piece level.
assumptions.ifWrong: The SF-019-M2 top AND collapses toward an OR and a common-cause candidate appears, defeating the no-single-point claim.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-M2 top AND gate; the 'positive pressure relief valve fails to relieve' basic event

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The 'undetected' arm of SF-019-M3 corresponds to failure of the differential-pressure/cabin-altitude indication path to avionics and the crew, not to a controller mistaken-belief inside the control loop.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names the ECS output to avionics and crew-oxygen logic as the awareness path but does not decompose the indication chain, so it is seated as a single undeveloped event.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection is layered (independent monitor plus alerting), this basic event expands into a sub-gate and the tree gains depth.

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states mechanical relief is independent of the control system but does not detail its sensing/actuation, forcing an independence assumption for the AND gate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If relief shares sensing or power with the controllers, the SF-019-M4 AND gate collapses toward a common-cause OR and the top event probability rises.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-M4 tree — 'Independent positive-pressure mechanical relief valve fails to open' AND branch

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system.

assumptions.text: The differential-pressure indication and the crew alerting channel are independent of the pressurisation controllers, so an undetected over-pressure requires a separate indication failure.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD shows differential pressure is sent to avionics and crew oxygen logic but does not confirm indication independence from the controllers.
assumptions.ifWrong: If indication is derived from the same failed controller sensing, the 'undetected' AND branch reduces to a single common failure and detection credit is lost.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-019-M4 tree — 'Over-pressure not annunciated to crew' branch

citations.quote: differential pressure and cabin altitude to the avionics and to the crew oxygen logic

assumptions.text: The bleed anti-ice protection (wing/cowl) and the electrical stabiliser-zone heating are independent means such that complete loss of surface/inlet protection requires both to fail.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes bleed protection for wings/cowls and electrical protection for stabilisers as separate means but both ultimately draw on shared resources (cross-bleed manifold, EPS buses).
assumptions.ifWrong: If a common resource (cross-bleed manifold loss driving pack/EPS loss, or a shared bus) takes both means, the top-level AND is a common-cause single point and SF-020-TL becomes more likely.

citations.quote: Wing leading edges and the engine inlet cowls are protected by hot bleed air

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names a shared cross-bleed manifold as the bleed source but does not decompose the piccolo distribution redundancy, bounding tree depth on the bleed branch.
assumptions.ifWrong: If piccolo distribution has its own single-point failures, an additional basic-event layer is warranted on the bleed OR branch.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-TL tree — bleed-protection OR branch

citations.quote: taken from the same manifold that supplies the environmental packs, through piccolo distribution

assumptions.text: Wing/cowl bleed ice protection remains available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold, so a total bleed-branch loss requires both sides to fail.

assumptions.ifWrong: The AND under the bleed branch collapses to an OR and a single manifold/side fault becomes an order-1 contributor to partial loss.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-020-PL bleed branch AND gate

citations.quote: Bleed protection is available from either side through the cross-bleed manifold.

assumptions.text: The six stabiliser electric zones and the probe/windshield elements are independently supplied, so each is an independent OR input.

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

citations.quote: the system may also be selected on manually at any time

citations.quote: AC and DC electrical power to the heated elements and controllers

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

citations.quote: Probes, static ports, windshields and the two ice detectors are electrically heated and are monitored individually.

assumptions.text: The two ice detectors are independent to first order and both must fail for complete loss of detection.

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes electrically heated/monitored elements but does not give controller, channel or bus detail per probe/detector, so depth stops at element+supply.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detectors/heaters share a controller or bus, additional common contributors and gate depth are missing from both trees.
assumptions.usedFor: Both trees' OR sub-gates

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated.

assumptions.ifWrong: If partial loss requires degradation of both channels, SF-022-PL becomes an AND of the two detector-channel gates rather than an OR.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-PL tree root gate logic

assumptions.rationale: The SDD lists TAT and airspeed as detector inputs but does not confirm whether the two detectors draw on independent or shared air-data sources.

assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-M shared-input basic event

citations.quote: total air temperature and airspeed from the avionics; crew selection

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly records the detector commonality as an item for examination; CCF modelling is a CMA/engineer decision, not derivable structure here.

assumptions.usedFor: SF-022-PL and SF-022-M tree structure (CCF omitted)

citations.quote: The two ice detectors are identical in type and their commonality is recorded as an item for examination

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states detection is advisory to the flight deck but does not describe a dedicated detector-health annunciation path, so the crew-unaware branch is inferred.

assumptions.text: Partial display loss is any single-channel loss among a display unit, a display processing unit, or a network channel; total loss is out of scope for this FC.

assumptions.usedFor: SF-023-M2 top AND-gate second branch (Loss of independent standby-instrument cross-check)

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: Erroneous source data originating in an ADIRU is modelled as an undeveloped contributor to be traced to SF-024 rather than developed inside the AVI display trees.

assumptions.ifWrong: If it should be developed in-tree, both trees gain an ADIRU subtree (three units, two on main buses, one on DC essential) instead of an undeveloped node.
assumptions.usedFor: Undeveloped node 'Erroneous source data from reference unit' in both SF-023-M and SF-023-M2

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data.

assumptions.text: The three ADIRUs are independent to the level that a complete loss requires all three to fail (AND), with only shared electrical supply and the data network as common contributors.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states three reference units on separated supplies but does not assert unit-to-unit independence or a shared part number, forcing an independence assumption for the AND gate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the three ADIRUs share a common cause (e.g. common part number, common sensing), the SF-024-TL top event gains a lower-order cut set and the AND structure understates the risk.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024-TL top-event AND gate over ADIRU 1/2/3

citations.quote: Three air data inertial reference units supply air data and inertial data. Two are supplied from the main buses and one from the DC essential bus.

assumptions.text: The dual deterministic data network is the sole distribution path for reference data to the display processors, so loss of both channels denies the reference regardless of ADIRU health.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes a dual redundant deterministic network carrying the data but does not state whether an alternate distribution path exists, forcing this architecture assumption for the network OR branch.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an independent alternate data path exists, the network branch of SF-024-TL is not sufficient on its own and should move deeper or be removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024-TL network AND branch; SF-024-PL network OR branch

citations.quote: Four display units and two head-up displays are driven by three display processing units on a dual redundant deterministic data network.

assumptions.rationale: The SDD names three reference units and a two-channel alerting system but does not describe an explicit ADIRU cross-comparison/voting monitor, so the detection branch that separates M from M2 had to be assumed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no cross-comparison monitor exists, SF-024-M and SF-024-M2 collapse toward the same tree and the AND detection branch in M2 is invalid; the OR/AND logic must be rebuilt.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-024-M top OR and SF-024-M2 detection AND branch

citations.quote: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels.

assumptions.text: The three reference units share the pitot/static/angle-of-attack sensing and take power from only two independent classes (main buses and DC essential), so a common-cause corrupting multiple units and defeating comparison is credible.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two units are on main buses and one on the DC essential bus and lists shared pitot/static/AoA sensing at aircraft level, but does not confirm sensor-source independence per unit.
assumptions.ifWrong: If each reference unit has fully independent sensing and power, the common-mode AND branch in both trees is not a real cut set and should be removed.
assumptions.usedFor: common-mode AND branch in SF-024-M and OR contributor in SF-024-M2

citations.quote: Two are supplied from the main buses and one from the DC essential bus.

assumptions.text: The integrated standby instrument is a single line-replaceable unit with no internal redundancy, so its loss is an order-1 cut set for SF-025-TL.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD names 'an independent integrated standby instrument' as one unit and states no internal redundancy for it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the ISI carries internal dual-channel redundancy, the SF-025-TL SPF basic event splits into an AND gate and the tree gains one level of depth.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025-TL top event and its 'Loss of integrated standby instrument unit' basic event

citations.quote: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus

assumptions.text: The DC essential bus is held up by a TRU-fed path and a battery-supported path that must both be lost to lose the bus.
assumptions.rationale: §5.5.2 describes four TRUs feeding the DC buses and two batteries plus the hot battery bus supporting the DC essential bus, but the exact feed-combination logic is not drawn.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the essential bus can be lost by a single feed failure, the AND gate under 'Loss of DC essential bus supply' becomes an OR and the standby loss probability rises.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025-TL 'Loss of DC essential bus supply' AND gate and its two feed basic events

citations.quote: The DC essential bus is the aircraft's final electrical resort

assumptions.text: The standby instrument has no documented per-parameter partial-degradation architecture, so SF-025-PL cannot be decomposed below one undeveloped contributor without supplier data.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states attitude/airspeed/altitude are provided by one integrated instrument but gives no internal partial-failure breakdown.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the ISI degrades per parameter, SF-025-PL gains OR branches per lost parameter; the current single undeveloped event is replaced.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025-PL top event and its single undeveloped contributor

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: The integrated standby instrument shares no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays, so its erroneous output is independent of the primary flight/nav display chain.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts the shared-nothing claim in prose; it must be verified rather than assumed for the SF-025-M tree to be a valid standalone OR.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-025-M would need common-cause inputs shared with SF-023-M (primary display) and the OR gate would gain a shared basic event.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-025-M tree top OR gate and its three basic events

citations.quote: an independent integrated standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.text: The two alerting processing channels are electrically and physically independent with no shared presentation node, so complete loss requires both to fail (AND).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two independent channels but does not confirm their alert output is presented through a non-shared path; the AND logic depends on that independence.
assumptions.ifWrong: SF-026-TL would gain a single-point common node (shared avionics presentation) turning part of the AND into an OR, defeating the redundancy claim.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026-TL top AND gate across channel 1 and channel 2 sub-trees

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list ... driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: The two alerting processing channels are independent such that a single channel fault only partially degrades alerting rather than eliminating it.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD asserts two independent channels but provides no dissimilarity or independence argument to substantiate it.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the channels share a common fault path, SF-026-PL contributors would need an AND/common-cause restructure and the top logic would change.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026-PL top OR gate; SF-026-M channel basic event

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: Erroneous input data from a monitored aircraft system reaches the alert list regardless of which alerting channel is healthy (no cross-channel input comparison credited).
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes alerting consolidation but does not describe input-data monitoring or comparison for the alerting function.
assumptions.ifWrong: If input comparison/monitoring exists, the erroneous-input branch of SF-026-M would gain an AND with a monitor-failure event rather than standing as a single OR contributor.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026-M erroneous-input basic event

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.text: Either alerting processing channel independently generating a spurious active alert is sufficient to present a nuisance alert to the crew.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two independent processing channels but does not describe cross-channel voting on the emission (false-alert) direction.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a false alert requires both channels to agree, the SF-026-M2 top gate becomes AND on the two channel branches, removing those single points.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026-M2 top OR gate, channel-1 and channel-2 basic events

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.text: There is no dedicated alerting-integrity monitor that annunciates loss of alerting coverage to the crew.
assumptions.rationale: The SDD describes alerting consolidation and dual channels but does not describe any monitor of the alerting function's own health, so the detection-defeat branch cannot be decomposed.
assumptions.ifWrong: If an alerting-health monitor exists, the undeveloped 'not revealed' node decomposes into failure of that monitor, and the undetected-loss top event gains an added independent term.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-026-PL2 AND gate, 'Loss of alerting coverage not revealed to crew' undeveloped node

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states dissimilar software from one of two teams but does not map which team built which of the three computers, so a shared-team pair among three is forced by pigeonhole.
assumptions.ifWrong: If dissimilarity is somehow complete across all three (e.g. three teams or provably independent partitions), the G-061 common-software CCF contributor is removed and the clean 3-way AND stands, strengthening the DAL-A basis.
assumptions.usedFor: G-061 three-FCC CMA row; the common-specification/software CCF contributor and the DAL-A allocation caveat

assumptions.text: HYD B and HYD C provide the two roll-surface actuation supplies and, unlike A/B, do not share a wing-root run.

assumptions.ifWrong: If HYD B and HYD C share a routing or zone for roll actuation, the G-063 hydraulic leg gains an installation common-cause contributor and the dual-supply mitigation is overstated.

assumptions.ifWrong: If alerting and the FCC roll-command path are on genuinely segregated, non-common sources, the EPS common-resource contributor drops and the AND-gate independence (and the DAL-A reduction) is better supported.

assumptions.usedFor: G-064 (node 172), SF-005-M4 top AND (node 175), G-067 (node 180)

praData.threat: Tire burst / flailing tread — main gear bogie (§25.734, AC 25.734-1)
praData.desc: Burst of a main-bogie tyre or thrown tread within a left/right main gear bay (Z710/Z720). Twenty tyres on six three-wheel bogies; gear-leg/bogie count is preliminary per SDD §1.2. Debris/tread is high-energy, radial and tangential, confined initially to the bay but able to sever or damage the adjacent brake hydraulic lines and, via the shared wing-root transit, the HYD A/B run in Z300.
praData.systems: LDG (brakes, wheel/tyre), HYD (systems A and B), FCS (surfaces on A/B supply)
praData.csfl: HYD A and B brake lines run through each main gear bay in adjacent, separately-clipped-and-shielded bundles sharing the bay (SDD §5.6.5) — a single burst in-bay is a common-cause candidate that can degrade both A and B braking; A and B also share a wing-root run (SDD §5.4.5), so bay debris reaching that transit threatens supplies to rudder/aileron/elevator actuation.
praData.mitigation:
Confirm bundle separation/shielding in the gear bay defeats a single tyre/tread trajectory taking both A and B; verify HYD A/B wing-root run is outside the credible tyre-debris cone; substantiate accumulator emergency braking (six applications, SDD §5.4.3) covers the degraded case. Outcome sought: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE via separation + accumulator reserve — to be substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • The LDG installation shall separate or shield the HYD A and B brake bundles in each main gear bay such that a single tyre burst or thrown tread cannot damage both.
• The HYD A/B wing-root run shall be located outside the credible tyre-debris trajectory from the main gear bays, or shielded against it.
aiRequirements: The LDG installation shall separate or shield the HYD A and B brake bundles in each main gear bay such that a single tyre burst or thrown tread cannot damage both.
The HYD A/B wing-root run shall be located outside the credible tyre-debris trajectory from the main gear bays, or shielded against it.

praData.threat: Bird strike — forward-facing structure, inlets and windshield (§25.571(e)(1)/§25.631/§33.76)
praData.desc: Bird impact on forward-facing surfaces: the four engine inlets (Z610–640), the flight-deck windshield (Z130), the wing leading edges (Z510/520) and the nose visor structure (Z110). Impact energy can ingest into an engine, crack a windshield, damage a leading edge and its anti-ice ducting, and strike the forward-fuselage-mounted probes and the two ice detectors.
praData.systems: PRP (inlets/ingestion), AVI (windshield, probes/air-data via forward-fuselage probes), IPS (leading-edge ducting, two same-type ice detectors), NZD (visor structure)
praData.csfl: The two ice detectors are of the same type, mounted on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (SDD §5.10.2) — a strike pattern is a common-mode candidate against ice detection; probes/static ports feeding the three ADIRUs are forward-fuselage-mounted and exposed. Ingestion into one engine is single-side; a flocking event challenging multiple inlets is the multi-engine scenario to be studied.
praData.mitigation:
Confirm windshield bird-strike capability per §25.631/§25.775; verify probe and ice-detector siting so a single strike cannot defeat air-data or ice-detection redundancy; substantiate engine ingestion tolerance per §33.76 against the inlet geometry. Outcome sought: SHOWN TO BE ACCEPTABLE (structure/windshield) and MINIMISED (multi-sensor loss via siting) — to be substantiated.
Proposed requirements: • The AVI/IPS installation shall site the air-data probes and the two ice detectors so that a single bird strike cannot simultaneously defeat air-data redundancy and ice-detection redundancy.
• The flight-deck windshield and forward structure shall withstand bird strike per the applicable §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631 threat without penetration endangering the crew.
aiRequirements: The AVI/IPS installation shall site the air-data probes and the two ice detectors so that a single bird strike cannot simultaneously defeat air-data redundancy and ice-detection redundancy.
The flight-deck windshield and forward structure shall withstand bird strike per the applicable §25.571(e)(1)/§25.631 threat without penetration endangering the crew.

praData.desc: Lightning attaches at aircraft extremities (nose visor, wing tips, engine nacelles, empennage) and conducts through the airframe. Survivability concern is coupling into the fly-by-wire FCS, avionics and electrical distribution carried on the six EWS routes; the two identified HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 and the wing-root region where the HV feeder co-transits with bleed ducts are the credible coupling points. Not a structural-integrity study (that is PRA/structural for the visor single load path); this row addresses the systems/electrical survivability.
praData.systems: FCS, AVI, EPS, EWS, PRP (FADEC), IPS
praData.csfl: A common electromagnetic transient could couple simultaneously into the three dissimilar flight control computers and the electrical distribution they depend on, defeating the FCS redundancy that is otherwise argued from three computers on three sources and three hydraulic systems.
praData.mitigation:
Bonding of metallic components and airframe per §25.581; nonmetallic/composite lightning protection design; transient protection and shielding of the EWS routes; separation of HV and LV routes maintained except at the two shielded crossing points; standby instrument on the DC essential bus wired on an independent route. Outcome claimed: effects SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1316 qualification — pending test/analysis.
Proposed requirements: • The aircraft structure and metallic components shall be bonded to the airframe to protect against catastrophic effects of lightning (§25.581).
• The electrical and electronic systems performing functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the effects of lightning to §25.1316 levels.
• The EWS HV/LV route separation and the two shielded crossing points shall be shown to preserve FCS/AVI independence under a lightning transient.
aiFunctions: SF-023 Provide flight and navigation display
SF-024 Provide air data and inertial reference
aiRequirements: The aircraft structure and metallic components shall be bonded to the airframe to protect against catastrophic effects of lightning (§25.581).
The electrical and electronic systems performing functions whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be protected against the effects of lightning to §25.1316 levels.
The EWS HV/LV route separation and the two shielded crossing points shall be shown to preserve FCS/AVI independence under a lightning transient.

praData.desc: External radiated fields couple into the low-voltage signal routes, the two data network channels and the electronic units (FCC, ADIRU, display processors) distributed along the fuselage. Survivability concern is erroneous or misleading data reaching the control laws and displays rather than structural effect; the two HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 and the data-network routing (zones 120,200,300,400,800) are the credible coupling paths.
praData.csfl: A radiated field is by nature a common-mode threat that can couple simultaneously into otherwise-independent LV/data routes and the three flight control computers and three reference units, so the independence argued from routing on opposite sides must be shown to hold under illumination.
praData.mitigation:
HIRF protection design and equipment qualification to §25.1317; shielding and bundle segregation of the LV and data routes; opposite-side routing of the two data network channels sharing no connector or penetration; the standby integrated instrument sharing no supply, sensor or processing with the primary displays as an independent means. Outcome claimed: effects SHOWN ACCEPTABLE via §25.1317 qualification — pending test/analysis.
Proposed requirements: • Each electrical and electronic system that performs a function whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be designed and installed to be unaffected by HIRF to §25.1317 levels.
• The two data network channels and the LV signal routes shall be shown to preserve avionics independence under HIRF illumination.
• The standby integrated instrument independence (no shared supply, sensor or processing) shall be substantiated under a HIRF environment.
aiFunctions: SF-023 Provide flight and navigation display
SF-024 Provide air data and inertial reference
aiRequirements: Each electrical and electronic system that performs a function whose failure would be Catastrophic or Hazardous shall be designed and installed to be unaffected by HIRF to §25.1317 levels.
The two data network channels and the LV signal routes shall be shown to preserve avionics independence under HIRF illumination.
The standby integrated instrument independence (no shared supply, sensor or processing) shall be substantiated under a HIRF environment.

praData.threat: Hail / ice impact on forward-facing structure, inlets and probes
praData.desc: App L survivability study of hail/ice impact per §25.571(e)(2) on forward-facing surfaces. Model: hail/ice mass striking wing/stabiliser leading edges, the four engine inlet cowls, windshields and the pitot/static/AoA probes and the two forward-fuselage ice detectors. Drawing/model-stage installation per SDD — routing and detector positions are described, not frozen; treat trajectory/geometry as preliminary. Direct in-zone strike on leading edges (510/520) and engine inlets (nacelles 610-640); windshield and probe strike at the forward fuselage/flight deck (120/130).
praData.csfl: Ice detectors are of the same type installed on opposite sides of the forward fuselage (SDD §5.10.2/§5.10.3) — a single hail/ice-impact environment strikes both, a common-source loss of both detection channels defeating the assumed detector redundancy for ice accretion detection. Probe/windshield heating and the primary air-data path can be degraded concurrently with the standby path where both face the impact environment; independence of the standby instrument from the airstream sensing is not established for a common environmental impact.
praData.mitigation:
Existing design features: probes, static ports, windshields and both ice detectors are electrically heated and individually monitored (§5.10.2); wing leading edges and inlet cowls have bleed anti-ice available from either side via the cross-bleed manifold (§5.10.3); wing anti-ice ducting shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition (§5.10.5). CLAIM: effects on ice-protection availability are MINIMISED by heated-element monitoring and cross-bleed redundancy; the two-same-type ice-detector common-source loss must be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE. Impact-resistance of windshields, leading edges and inlets is a structural showing under §25.571(e)(2) not settled here.
Proposed requirements: • The forward-facing structure, engine inlets and windshields shall withstand the hail/ice impact threat of the certification basis without loss of a Catastrophic or Hazardous function.
• The two ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection following a single hail/ice-impact environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.
aiRequirements: The forward-facing structure, engine inlets and windshields shall withstand the hail/ice impact threat of the certification basis without loss of a Catastrophic or Hazardous function.
The two ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection following a single hail/ice-impact environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.

praData.threat: Icing / ice accretion and ice shedding
praData.desc: App L survivability study of in-flight icing per §25.1419 / AC 20-73A within the type-design ice envelope. Model: ice accretion on unprotected or under-protected surfaces, inlets, probes and detectors; and ice shed from wing/stabiliser leading edges, inlet cowls and the fuselage into the engine inlets and onto aft structure. Direct in-zone effect on wing/stabiliser leading edges (510/520/800), engine inlets (610-640) and forward-fuselage probes/windshields/detectors (120/130). Drawing/model-stage installation — ice-envelope refinement and detector positions per SDD are preliminary.
praData.csfl: Wing and inlet anti-ice both draw hot bleed from the SAME cross-bleed manifold that supplies the ECS packs (§5.10.2) — loss or contention of that manifold is a common source degrading wing anti-ice, cowl anti-ice and pack conditioning together. Both same-type ice detectors accrete in the same icing environment, defeating detection redundancy (§5.10.3). Shed ice from a leading edge/cowl can enter one or more of the four inlets, a single environmental event reaching multiple otherwise-independent engines.
praData.mitigation:
Existing design features: bleed protection to wings and cowls available from either side via the cross-bleed manifold; six independently supplied electrically-heated stabiliser zones with a lost zone annunciated; individually monitored heated probes/ports/windshields; ice detection advisory with automatic activation and manual selection (§5.10.2/§5.10.3). CLAIM: effects on continued safe flight in icing are MINIMISED by dual-side bleed, independent stabiliser zones and monitored probe heat; the shared cross-bleed-manifold common source and the two-same-type detector common-source loss must be SHOWN ACCEPTABLE; engine ingestion of shed ice is an engine/installation showing (§33.76/§25.1093) not settled here.
Proposed requirements: • The ice protection system shall provide continued safe flight and landing within the certification-basis icing envelope with any single anti-ice bleed source or manifold segment lost.
• Ice shed from protected and unprotected surfaces shall be shown not to cause a Hazardous or Catastrophic effect on the engine installation or aft structure.
• The two same-type ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection in the design icing environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.
aiRequirements: The ice protection system shall provide continued safe flight and landing within the certification-basis icing envelope with any single anti-ice bleed source or manifold segment lost.
Ice shed from protected and unprotected surfaces shall be shown not to cause a Hazardous or Catastrophic effect on the engine installation or aft structure.
The two same-type ice detectors shall be shown to retain ice-accretion detection in the design icing environment, or the common-source loss shall be substantiated as acceptable.

praData.desc: Fire or smoke originating in the pressurised hold (zones 200/300/400) or the forward equipment bay/flight deck (120/130). Hold carries smoke detection at nine stations along its length with NO suppression fitted (SDD §5.12.2) — a deliberate design decision recorded as an assumption to be substantiated. Zone 120 houses oxygen cylinders and forward avionics racks; zone 130 is the occupied flight deck with fire handles and crew oxygen masks. Cross-zone propagation reaches otherwise-separated equipment along shared runs: the HV feeder (610/620,530,300,200), LV signal (120,200,300,400,800), data channels (120,200,300,400,800) and the restraint tension monitoring loop (200,300,400), all of which transit the hold zones. A hold fire beneath the blade near an FCC bay (FCC 2 in zone 300, FCC 3 in zone 400) or the HV/LV crossing points in zone 300 could defeat the three-computer / dual-network independence claim by common-cause thermal damage.
praData.systems: FPR (detection zones 200/300/400, no hold suppression), CRG (restraint tension loop + winches in hold), AVI (FCC 2 zone 300, FCC 3 zone 400, network channels), EPS (HV feeder transit), OXY (cylinders zone 120), FCS (via FCC common-mode), ECS (conditioning/smoke evacuation of hold and flight deck)
praData.csfl: A hold fire in zone 300 concurrently threatens FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network, and via routing reaches FCC 3 (zone 400) and the HV feeder to zone 200 — a single localised thermal event as common cause across the flight-control computer, electrical feeder and data-network independence claimed in SDD §5.3.5 and §5.11.5.
praData.mitigation:
Detection: dual-loop continuous detection in nacelle/APU zones, nine-station smoke detection along the hold (SDD §5.12.2). Segregation: HV and LV routes separated throughout except two shielded crossing points in zone 300; data channels on opposite sides sharing no connector/penetration; three FCCs in three separate bays. Crew: fire handles and portable extinguishers at flight deck and hold access door; crew oxygen with smoke goggles. GAP — NO hold suppression is fitted; acceptability of detection-only rests on the single-blade / no-combustible-palletised-load argument and MUST be substantiated. Consequence for the crossing points, FCC bays and HV/LV co-location in zone 300 is not yet shown ELIMINATED, MINIMISED or ACCEPTABLE.
Proposed requirements: • The FPR system shall provide the means to detect fire/smoke throughout the hold at a coverage and response time consistent with the no-suppression decision, and the acceptability of detection-only shall be substantiated by analysis of hold fire load and propagation (SDD §5.12.2 open assumption).
• The installation shall demonstrate that a single hold fire in zone 300 cannot simultaneously defeat the independence of FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network channels claimed for flight-control and display functions (thermal separation/shielding at the zone-300 crossing points).
aiRequirements: The FPR system shall provide the means to detect fire/smoke throughout the hold at a coverage and response time consistent with the no-suppression decision, and the acceptability of detection-only shall be substantiated by analysis of hold fire load and propagation (SDD §5.12.2 open assumption).

The installation shall demonstrate that a single hold fire in zone 300 cannot simultaneously defeat the independence of FCC 2, the HV/LV crossing points and the data network channels claimed for flight-control and display functions (thermal separation/shielding at the zone-300 crossing points).

zsaData.desc: Nose visor structure — pressure boundary when closed, unpressurised when open. Houses visor latches, lock pins, lock actuator, sensing harness (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Twelve rotary latches on common torque shaft, eight locking pins, lock actuator, proximity sensing harness
zsaData.interference: Single load-path door structure with no structural redundancy; lock sensing harness transits 110→120→130 and must stay separated from door actuation power and from the mechanical indicator linkage. Installation/maintenance error could commingle the two dissimilar sensing paths or the sensing harness with actuation power, defeating the dual-dissimilar sensing claim.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify sensing harness routed opposite door actuation power and separated from mechanical indicator linkage throughout, with the two bulkhead penetrations at the flight-deck bulkhead separated (SDD §5.7.5); confirm pressure interlock wiring integrity. Door structural integrity substantiated by structural analysis / PRA, not by ZSA.

zsaData.desc: Forward equipment bay — pressurised, conditioned. Houses FCC 1, oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Flight control computer 1, high-pressure oxygen cylinders, forward avionics racks; LV signal and data channel routes originate/transit here
zsaData.interference: Co-location of high-pressure oxygen cylinders with FCC 1 and avionics racks; an oxygen cylinder overpressure/leak or a maintenance handling error near energised avionics is an inherent physical hazard assessed regardless of functional criticality (App K.3.1). LV signal left/right and data channels 1/2 transit this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm cylinders installed outside any high-energy electrical source zone per SDD §5.13.5 and thermal discharge routed overboard; verify FCC 1 separation from the other two FCCs (mid/aft bays) is preserved so the three-computer dissimilarity is not defeated by common installation in this bay. Bonding/segregation of oxygen supply line clear of feeders.

zsaData.desc: Flight deck — pressurised, occupied. Houses displays, inceptors, standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Four display units, inceptors, integrated standby instrument, fire handles, crew oxygen masks
zsaData.interference: Occupied compartment; standby instrument must share no supply/sensor/processing with primary displays (SDD §5.11.3) — an installation error commingling the standby feeder with primary display feeders defeats the independence claim. Lock-status indication and fire-handle runs terminate here.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify standby instrument wired directly to DC essential bus on a route independent of primary display feeders (SDD §5.11.5); confirm crew-oxygen mask stowage and quick-don access unobstructed. Housekeeping/materials-compatibility checkpoint for an occupied zone.

zsaData.desc: Forward hold (stations 1–3) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 1–3, restraint straps, tension loop, smoke detectors (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 1–3 with two tension straps each, single instrumented restraint tension loop, smoke detectors; HV feeder, LV signal, data channels, HYD C run and fuel gallery vent transit
zsaData.interference: The single instrumented restraint tension monitoring loop runs full hold length on the left side and shares this zone with the fuel gallery vent and the left-side electrical route (SDD §5.8.5) — a single event in the shared zone could disable restraint monitoring and expose an electrical/fuel-vapour co-location. HV feeder and HYD C also transit.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm the single tension loop separation from the fuel gallery vent and left electrical route; verify smoke-detector coverage at the station; confirm HV feeder / HYD C separation maintained through the zone. Co-location of the single-loop monitor is a recorded item (SDD §5.8.5).

zsaData.desc: Mid hold (stations 4–6) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2, HV/LV crossing points (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 4–6, mid equipment bay, FCC 2; HYD A+B shared wing-root run, HYD C, HV feeder L/R, LV signal, data channels, bleed cross-bleed manifold, restraint loop all transit
zsaData.interference: This zone concentrates several nominally independent items: the two HV↔LV crossing points (SDD §5.5.5/§5.14.2), the HYD A+B shared wing-root run (SDD §5.4.5), the cross-bleed manifold joining both sides (SDD §5.9.5), and FCC 2. A single installation/maintenance event here could defeat multiple independence claims at once — the primary common-mode candidate zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify HV/LV crossing points use the defined shielding and minimum distance; confirm HYD A and B bundles separately clipped where they share the run; confirm FCC 2 separation from FCC 1/3 preserved. Reflect the A+B shared run and HV/LV crossings as common-cause contributors in the affected fault trees (ARP4761A particular-risk/zonal complement).

zsaData.desc: Aft hold (stations 7–9) — low differential, unoccupied. Houses saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3 (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Saddles 7–9, aft equipment bay, FCC 3; HYD C run, LV signal, data channels and restraint loop transit
zsaData.interference: FCC 3 co-located with restraint saddles and HYD C run; the third of three dissimilar computers must remain separated from FCC 1 (120) and FCC 2 (300) for the dissimilarity argument to hold. Restraint tension loop continues through this zone.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm FCC 3 bay separation preserves the three-bay computer distribution (SDD §5.3.5); verify HYD C run and restraint loop separation maintained; smoke-detection coverage at aft stations.

zsaData.desc: Left wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present. Houses fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Integral fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route
zsaData.interference: Flammable-fluid zone with a hot bleed anti-ice duct and an electrical route sharing the leading edge behind a shielded partition (SDD §5.10.5). Installation error or partition degradation co-locates an ignition source with fuel vapour. The single spanwise cross-feed gallery — the only path from one wing to the opposite engines — transits here.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify the shielded partition integrity between anti-ice ducting and the outboard electrical route along the full run; confirm tank vent/surge lines routed outboard of all electrical harnesses (SDD §5.2.5); drainage and ventilation of the flammable zone. Cross-feed gallery retained for particular-risk/zonal attention.

zsaData.desc: Right wing box and leading edge — flammable fluid present. Mirror of 510: fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Integral fuel tanks, cross-feed gallery, wing anti-ice ducting, outboard electrical route; single pressure refuel/defuel point at right wing root
zsaData.interference: Flammable-fluid zone as 510 (mirrored). Additionally the single pressure refuel/defuel point is in the right wing root (SDD §5.2.2) — a refuelling/servicing error is a maintenance-error checkpoint. Hot anti-ice duct shares the leading edge with the outboard electrical route behind a shielded partition.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify shielded partition integrity; confirm overflow protection circuit independence at the refuel point (SDD §5.2.2); tank vent lines outboard of electrical harnesses; drainage/ventilation of the flammable zone.

zsaData.desc: Left wing root — pressure boundary transit. Houses HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: HYD systems A and B share this wing-root run where both cross the pressure boundary (SDD §5.4.5) — a claim about independence the SDD itself flags for a dedicated zonal item. A single event at this run could take both A and B, degrading flight controls, gear and braking simultaneously. HV feeder and bleed duct penetrate the same boundary region.
zsaData.mitigation: Confirm A and B are on separate routes to the maximum extent and separately clipped where they share the run; verify bleed duct kept clear of the HV feeder with the minimum separation (SDD §5.9.5). Reflect the A+B shared run as a common-cause contributor in the FCS/LDG fault trees.

zsaData.desc: Right wing root — pressure boundary transit. Mirror of 530: HYD A and B wing-root run, bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: HYD A and B wing-root run (shared), bleed duct penetration, HV feeder transit
zsaData.interference: As 530 (mirrored): HYD A and B share the wing-root run crossing the pressure boundary; bleed duct and HV feeder transit the same region. Single-event common-cause candidate for both A and B.
zsaData.mitigation: As 530 — confirm A/B separate clipping, bleed-duct/HV separation, and reflect the shared run as a common-cause contributor in the affected fault trees.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 2 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 2, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181 as 610. Rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned hazards. Dual-loop detection separation and cross-bottle plumbing to nacelle 1 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As 610 — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, and cross-plumbing to the paired nacelle. Cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 3 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 3, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD B), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181. Nacelle 3 drives HYD B; rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned. Dual-loop detection separation and cross-bottle plumbing to nacelle 4 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As 610/620 — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, cross-plumbing to nacelle 4; cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 4 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 4, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD B), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181. Outboard engine 4 is the sizing case for asymmetric-thrust directional control (SDD §5.1.3); rotor/engine burst are cross-zone PRA-owned. Detection separation and cross-plumbing to nacelle 3 must be preserved.
zsaData.mitigation: As the other nacelles — verify loop separation, fire-zone drainage/ventilation, cross-plumbing to nacelle 3; cross-reference rotor-burst/engine-burst PRA.

zsaData.desc: Left main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Houses three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, steering and brake electrical harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: Brake hydraulic lines for systems A and B run through the bay in adjacent (separately clipped) bundles, sharing the zone (SDD §5.6.5) — a single bay event (tyre burst / flailing tread, brake overheat) could affect both supplies. Tyre burst is an APPLICABLE cross-zone particular risk (PRA-81342). Steering and brake harnesses on opposite sides.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify A/B brake bundles separately clipped and shielded per SDD §5.6.5; confirm overheat detection coverage; confirm steering vs brake harness separation. Tyre-burst/flailing-tread debris addressed by PRA-81342 (co-located), reflected as common-cause where it defeats A/B independence.

zsaData.desc: Right main gear bay — unpressurised, overheat detection fitted. Mirror of 710: three bogies, brake lines A and B, steering and brake harnesses (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Three three-wheel bogies, brake hydraulic lines A and B, steering and brake electrical harnesses, overheat detection
zsaData.interference: As 710 (mirrored): brake lines A and B share the bay; tyre burst is an APPLICABLE cross-zone particular risk (PRA-81342); brake overheat detection fitted.
zsaData.mitigation: As 710 — verify A/B brake bundle separation, overheat coverage, harness separation; cross-reference tyre-burst PRA-81342.

zsaData.desc: Nose gear bay — unpressurised. Houses nose unit, steering actuator, tow disconnect (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Twin-wheel steerable nose unit, hydraulic steering actuator, tow disconnect (mechanical)
zsaData.interference: Steerable nose unit with a mechanical tow disconnect — a maintenance/towing error (disconnect not re-engaged, steering mis-rigged) is a maintenance-error checkpoint. Tyre burst on the nose unit is a co-located APPLICABLE particular risk (PRA-81342).
zsaData.mitigation: Verify tow-disconnect re-engagement is a positive, indicated action per operating procedure; confirm steering actuator supply integrity; drainage of the unpressurised bay. Cross-reference tyre-burst PRA-81342.

zsaData.desc: Aft fuselage and empennage — mixed; APU is a fire zone (§25.1181). Houses rudder control runs, stabiliser heater feeders, APU compartment (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Rudder upper/lower control runs, stabiliser heater feeders (six zones), APU compartment with dedicated fire bottle
zsaData.interference: Mixed-environment zone flagged as a candidate for sub-partitioning per App K.4.1: it contains a designated fire zone (APU per §25.1181) alongside rudder control runs and stabiliser heater feeders. Rudder upper/lower segments and their control runs are on opposite sides of the aft fuselage; stabiliser heater feeders must stay opposite the rudder runs (SDD §5.10.5). An APU fire or a heater-feeder fault must not take both rudder segment runs.
zsaData.mitigation: Recommend sub-partitioning the APU fire zone from the control-run bay for a uniform environment (App K.4.1); verify rudder upper/lower runs on opposite sides and stabiliser heater feeders opposite the rudder runs; confirm APU auto-discharge and fuel-isolation on the ground unattended (SDD §5.12.2), and APU-zone drainage/ventilation.

zsaData.desc: Engine nacelle 1 — high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone (§25.1181). Houses engine, FADEC, generator, EDP, fire detection loops, extinguisher plumbing (SDD §3).
zsaData.equip: Engine 1, dual-channel FADEC, 150 kVA generator, engine-driven hydraulic pump (HYD A), dual fire-detection loops, extinguisher plumbing
zsaData.interference: Designated fire zone per §25.1181 with flammable fluid and high-energy rotating machinery. Inherent physical hazards — uncontained rotor burst and high-energy engine burst — extend beyond the zone and are PRA-owned (App K.3.1). Dual detection loops must be routed on opposite sides of the zone for the AND logic to survive a single event.
zsaData.mitigation: Verify the two detection loops routed separately/opposite sides and separately clipped (SDD §5.12.5); confirm drainage and ventilation of the fire zone (§29.1187 analogue for transport per §25.1181); confirm extinguisher cross-plumbing to the paired nacelle. Rotor/engine burst debris addressed by PRA-81342-class rotor-burst/engine-burst analysis, not this ZSA row.

cmaData.subject: FADEC channel A/B independence — engine 1 (G-001, SF-001-M)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Dual-redundant FADEC channels, independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only. FADEC channel A and channel B fail independently so a single spurious channel does not cause an uncommanded thrust change
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence. (1) Common design/software — both channels are the same FADEC part number on one engine | a systematic error is present in both channels simultaneously | SDD asserts dual redundant channels but does not claim channel dissimilarity; treat as common-cause contributor. (2) Data cross-link between channels | erroneous data propagates A→B | SDD: channels 'cross-linked to the opposite channel for data only'; a corrupt cross-fed datum could bias both — test the cross-monitor. (3) Common environment — both channels co-located in nacelle 1 (zone 610, fire zone) | a single nacelle thermal/fire/HIRF event disables both | zone 610 is high-energy, flammable-fluid fire zone; PRA rotor/engine burst and fire strike both channels. (4) Common power | SDD states independent power feeds arranged so no single bus loss affects more than one engine | supports independence at engine granularity; confirm A and B feeds within engine 1 are also distinct.
cmaData.mitigation:
Dissimilarity or independent monitoring between channels; cross-monitor that rejects erroneous cross-fed data; nacelle particular-risk (rotor/engine burst, fire, HIRF) substantiation that both channels are not defeated together; confirm distinct intra-engine power feeds to A and B.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Channel A and channel B of the engine-1 FADEC shall not share a common design/software fault that produces the same erroneous thrust command (independence/dissimilarity argument required).
• The FADEC cross-monitor shall detect and reject an erroneous command from either channel before it reaches thrust actuation.
• The nacelle installation shall be shown by particular-risk and zonal analysis not to disable both FADEC channels of engine 1 by a single event.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Dual-redundant FADEC channels, independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only
aiRequirements: Channel A and channel B of the engine-1 FADEC shall not share a common design/software fault that produces the same erroneous thrust command (independence/dissimilarity argument required).
The FADEC cross-monitor shall detect and reject an erroneous command from either channel before it reaches thrust actuation.
The nacelle installation shall be shown by particular-risk and zonal analysis not to disable both FADEC channels of engine 1 by a single event.

cmaData.subject: G-007 FADEC channel A/B independence — engine 4 spurious command
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independent dual-channel FADEC with independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only.. The two dual-redundant FADEC channels on engine 4 fail independently, so a spurious thrust command requires both channels to fail (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence — Common design/software (both channels are the same FADEC part) | A generic design or software error commands both channels alike, defeating the AND | Dual-channel independence is asserted but the SDD does not state channel dissimilarity; residual common-mode design error remains. — Common environment, nacelle 4 / zone 640 (high energy, flammable fluid, fire zone) | A fire, overheat or thermal/EMI event in the nacelle disables both co-located channels together | Both channels reside in the same engine nacelle; no physical separation between channels is claimed. — Cross-channel data link | A corrupt datum passed A↔B propagates to both | SDD states channels are 'cross-linked to the opposite channel for data only'; monitor/voting behaviour not described.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require channel dissimilarity or an independent overspeed/overtemperature protection that is not shared between channels; require the cross-channel data link to be monitored so a corrupt datum cannot command both channels; carry nacelle-4 fire/overheat as a particular/zonal common cause against this AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The engine 4 FADEC shall provide overspeed and overtemperature protection by a means independent of both command channels.
• The engine 4 FADEC cross-channel data link shall be monitored such that a single corrupt datum cannot cause both channels to command the same erroneous thrust.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independent dual-channel FADEC with independent power feeds, cross-linked for data only.
aiRequirements: The engine 4 FADEC shall provide overspeed and overtemperature protection by a means independent of both command channels.
The engine 4 FADEC cross-channel data link shall be monitored such that a single corrupt datum cannot cause both channels to command the same erroneous thrust.

cmaData.subject: G-010 Boost pump A/B independence — collector 1
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Two AC boost pumps per collector operating in parallel, either sufficient for full engine demand at all altitudes.. The two parallel AC boost pumps on collector 1 fail independently, so loss of collector-1 boost feed requires both pumps to fail (AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence — Shared AC electrical resource (EPS) | Loss of the AC supply feeding both pumps disables the pair simultaneously | SDD states boost pumps are AC-driven; whether the two pumps on a collector draw from different AC buses is not stated. — Common design (both pumps same type/part) | A generic design or wear-out defect fails both pumps in the same interval | Two pumps of the same design in parallel; dissimilarity not claimed. — Common environment, wing box / zone 510 (flammable fluid present) | A tank-region thermal, contamination or fuel-quality event affects both co-located pumps | Both pumps serve the same collector cell in the same wing tank; no separation between them.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the two collector-1 boost pumps to be supplied from different AC sources so no single AC-source loss defeats the pair; note the gravity feed path below FL150 as an independent alternate reducing the AND's exposure; carry wing-tank particular/zonal risk against this AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two boost pumps of collector 1 shall be supplied from independent AC sources such that no single electrical-source loss disables both pumps.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Two AC boost pumps per collector operating in parallel, either sufficient for full engine demand at all altitudes.
aiRequirements: The two boost pumps of collector 1 shall be supplied from independent AC sources such that no single electrical-source loss disables both pumps.

cmaData.subject: G-016 — Both boost pumps failed — collector 3 (dual AC boost pump independence, SF-001-PL2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two parallel AC boost pumps feeding collector 3 (either sufficient for full engine demand).. The two AC boost pumps on collector 3 fail independently, so the AND gate holds and a single cause cannot fail both.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common AC electrical resource — both boost pumps are AC-driven (SDD §5.2.4) | Loss/degradation of the AC supply feeding collector 3 defeats both pumps at once | SDD does not state the two pumps take power from separate AC channels; gravity feed below FL150 partially mitigates — segregation to be confirmed
(2) Common design/part number — 'Two AC boost pumps per collector operate in parallel' (SDD §5.2.2), pump part-number commonality not addressed | A common design or software/material deficiency fails both identical pumps | No dissimilarity claimed for the pumps in the SDD; substantiation open
(3) Common installation zone — collector 3 pumps co-located in the right wing box (zone 520, flammable fluid present) | A zonal event (fire, mechanical) in zone 520 strikes both pumps | Reconcile with PRA/ZSA (zone 520); gravity feed path partial mitigation
(4) Common maintenance/manufacturing lot | A single maintenance error or lot defect disables both pumps | Not addressed in SDD — open
cmaData.mitigation:
Require separate AC channels to the two collector-3 boost pumps; confirm pump dissimilarity or add gravity-feed / cross-feed credit; verify zonal separation within zone 520; stagger maintenance. Retain gravity feed below FL150 and cross-feed gallery as independent mitigations.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two collector-3 AC boost pumps shall be supplied from independent AC sources such that no single bus loss fails both.
• The independence of the collector-3 dual-boost-pump group shall be substantiated against common part number, common installation zone (520), and common maintenance action.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two parallel AC boost pumps feeding collector 3 (either sufficient for full engine demand).
aiRequirements: The two collector-3 AC boost pumps shall be supplied from independent AC sources such that no single bus loss fails both.
The independence of the collector-3 dual-boost-pump group shall be substantiated against common part number, common installation zone (520), and common maintenance action.

cmaData.subject: G-019 — Both boost pumps failed — collector 4 (dual AC boost pump independence, SF-001-PL2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two parallel AC boost pumps feeding collector 4 (either sufficient for full engine demand).. The two AC boost pumps on collector 4 fail independently, so the AND gate holds and a single cause cannot fail both.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common AC electrical resource — both boost pumps are AC-driven (SDD §5.2.4) | Loss/degradation of the AC supply feeding collector 4 defeats both pumps at once | SDD does not state the two pumps take power from separate AC channels; gravity feed below FL150 partially mitigates — segregation to be confirmed
(2) Common design/part number — parallel identical pumps per collector (SDD §5.2.2), pump part-number commonality not addressed | A common design or material deficiency fails both identical pumps | No dissimilarity claimed for the pumps in the SDD; substantiation open
(3) Common installation zone — collector 4 pumps co-located in the right wing box (zone 520, flammable fluid present) | A zonal event in zone 520 strikes both pumps | Reconcile with PRA/ZSA (zone 520); gravity feed path partial mitigation
(4) Common maintenance/manufacturing lot | A single maintenance error or lot defect disables both pumps | Not addressed in SDD — open
cmaData.mitigation:
Require separate AC channels to the two collector-4 boost pumps; confirm pump dissimilarity or add gravity-feed / cross-feed credit; verify zonal separation within zone 520; stagger maintenance. Retain gravity feed below FL150 and cross-feed gallery as independent mitigations.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two collector-4 AC boost pumps shall be supplied from independent AC sources such that no single bus loss fails both.
• The independence of the collector-4 dual-boost-pump group shall be substantiated against common part number, common installation zone (520), and common maintenance action.
