cmaData.subject: G-023 — Erroneous FADEC-commanded thrust response (dual-channel FADEC independence, SF-001-M2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of FADEC channel A and channel B in generating an erroneous thrust command for the affected engine.. The two FADEC channels (A and B) fail independently, so a coincident erroneous thrust command from both (the AND gate) is not caused by a single shared source.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common cross-link data path — channels are 'cross-linked to the opposite channel for data only' (SDD §5.1.2) | Corrupted cross-channel data could drive both channels to the same erroneous command | Cross-link is data-only, not command; monitor/voting behaviour to be confirmed
(2) Common design/software — both channels are the dual redundant channels of one FADEC of a single engine type (SDD §5.1.2); dissimilarity not claimed | A common software or specification error produces the same erroneous command in both channels | No dissimilarity argument stated for FADEC channels (contrast FCS §5.3.2 dissimilar teams) — open
(3) Common installation zone — both channels reside in the engine nacelle (fire zone 610/620/630/640) | A nacelle environmental event affects both channels | Reconcile with PRA/ZSA and engine burst / rotor burst particular risks
(4) Common power — independent power feeds claimed ('independent power feeds', SDD §5.1.2) | Confirms channel supply independence | Mitigating factor present per SDD
(5) Common maintenance/calibration | A single erroneous calibration or software load applied to both channels | Not addressed in SDD — open
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm FADEC channel-to-channel dissimilarity or the cross-monitor/voting that rejects a single erroneous command; verify the data-only cross-link cannot propagate a command fault; confirm independent software loads/calibration procedures per channel. Credit the independent power feeds already claimed.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FADEC channel cross-link shall be data-only and shall not permit an erroneous command in one channel to drive the opposite channel.
• The independence of FADEC channels A and B shall be substantiated against common software error and common calibration/maintenance action.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of FADEC channel A and channel B in generating an erroneous thrust command for the affected engine.
aiRequirements: The FADEC channel cross-link shall be data-only and shall not permit an erroneous command in one channel to drive the opposite channel.
The independence of FADEC channels A and B shall be substantiated against common software error and common calibration/maintenance action.

cmaData.subject: SF-002-TL — Complete loss of reverse thrust (AND of inboard eng 2 / eng 3 reverser branches)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the eng 2 and eng 3 reverser deploy paths, including the deploy-enable (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement) supplied to each.. The two inboard reverser branches (engine 2, engine 3) fail independently, so complete loss requires both to fail.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1. Shared deploy-enable logic (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement) | A single erroneous/absent WoW or RA-agreement state inhibits BOTH inboard reversers simultaneously, defeating the AND | SDD states inhibit by WoW and RA agreement with mechanical sleeve lock; independence of the WoW/RA sources to each branch is NOT established in the provided material.
2. Common electrical resource (EPS) to both reverser command paths | Loss/upset of a shared bus disables both deploy commands | EPS is a shared resource supplying all systems (SDD §2.1); per-branch bus separation for reversers not described.
3. Co-location / common environment — inboard nacelles 620 and 630 are separate fire zones | A zonal fire is confined to one nacelle, so does not by itself defeat the AND | Nacelles are distinct zones (§25.1181 fire zones), providing physical separation between the two branches.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the WoW and radio-altimeter deploy-enable to each inboard reverser to be derived from independent source sets (no shared single WoW discrete / RA channel across both branches); require reverser command paths on separate electrical sources. Verify no shared connector/penetration for the two enable feeds.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The deploy-enable to the engine 2 and engine 3 reversers shall be derived from independent weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter sources such that no single source loss inhibits both reversers.
• The engine 2 and engine 3 reverser command paths shall be supplied from independent electrical sources.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-built segregation of the WoW/RA enable feeds and reverser command electrical sources between the two inboard branches; reconcile with EPS bus allocation.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the eng 2 and eng 3 reverser deploy paths, including the deploy-enable (weight-on-wheels + radio-altimeter agreement) supplied to each.
aiRequirements: The deploy-enable to the engine 2 and engine 3 reversers shall be derived from independent weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter sources such that no single source loss inhibits both reversers.

cmaData.subject: SF-003-PL — Partial loss of fuel delivery, single engine (AND of collector-feed and gravity/cross-feed loss)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the collector boost-pump pair, the gravity feed path, and the cross-feed gallery serving the affected engine.. The independent-failure logic combining loss of both boost pumps, the gravity feed path, and cross-feed availability holds, so single-engine fuel loss requires the concurrent loss of all paths.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1. Common AC electrical supply to the two boost pumps | A shared AC bus loss disables both boost pumps together (the G-033 AND) | Gravity path below FL150 is dissimilar (no electrical dependency) and provides a diverse backup — but only below FL150.
2. Single spanwise cross-feed gallery through the wing box | The cross-feed path is a single run; it cannot rebalance if the gallery itself is lost, and is retained for PRA/ZSA attention | SDD flags the gallery as a single spanwise run requiring particular-risk and zonal attention; it is the ONLY inter-side path.
3. Co-location of collector/pumps in a flammable-fluid wing zone (510/520) | A zonal event (fire/leak) in the wing box could affect the collector, both pumps and the cross-feed gallery together | Wing box zones carry flammable fluid; PRA/ZSA coverage needed to confirm the paths are not defeated by one zonal event.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the two boost pumps of a collector to be fed from independent AC sources; retain and substantiate the gravity path as a dissimilar backup with its altitude limitation stated; carry the single cross-feed gallery into PRA/ZSA. Confirm cross-feed isolation valves are independently drivable.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two boost pumps serving a given collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
• The single spanwise cross-feed gallery shall be assessed under particular-risk and zonal analysis for events that could defeat it together with the affected-side collector feed.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm independent AC feeds to the paired boost pumps and to reconcile the cross-feed gallery and collector routing against the PRA/ZSA findings for the wing-box zones.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the collector boost-pump pair, the gravity feed path, and the cross-feed gallery serving the affected engine.
aiRequirements: The two boost pumps serving a given collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
The single spanwise cross-feed gallery shall be assessed under particular-risk and zonal analysis for events that could defeat it together with the affected-side collector feed.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm independent AC feeds to the paired boost pumps and to reconcile the cross-feed gallery and collector routing against the PRA/ZSA findings for the wing-box zones.

cmaData.subject: G-033 — Loss of both boost pumps to the collector (AND: boost pump A AND boost pump B)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two parallel AC boost pumps on a single collector.. Boost pump A and boost pump B of the collector fail independently, so loss of the pair is the product of independent failures.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
1. Common AC electrical supply | If both pumps draw from the same AC bus, a single bus loss defeats the AND | SDD does not establish independent bus assignment for the two pumps; both are AC-driven and both serve one collector.
2. Common design / part number (identical pumps in parallel) | A common design or manufacturing-lot defect could fail both pumps within a short interval | Both pumps are the same type operating in parallel; dissimilarity is not claimed for the pump pair.
3. Co-location in the same collector / wing zone (510/520) | A single local thermal, mechanical or flammable-fluid event affects both pumps together | Both pumps serve one collector cell in a flammable-fluid wing zone; separation between the paired pumps is not described.
4. Common maintenance / calibration action | A single incorrect maintenance action applied to both pumps introduces a shared latent fault | Not addressed in the provided material; maintenance independence to be established.
cmaData.mitigation:
Feed boost pump A and boost pump B from independent AC sources; if the pair shares a part number, either stagger overhaul intervals or substantiate the common-mode failure rate; separate the physical mounting/routing of the two pumps within the collector bay; require independent maintenance procedures. Model the residual common cause as an explicit contributor in G-033 rather than relying on the bare AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Boost pump A and boost pump B of a collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources.
• Where the paired collector boost pumps share a part number, a common-cause contributor shall be modelled explicitly and staggered overhaul intervals applied.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm independent AC feeds, physical separation of the paired pumps within the collector bay, and that the fault tree G-033 carries an explicit common-cause contributor for the identical parallel pumps.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two parallel AC boost pumps on a single collector.
aiRequirements: Boost pump A and boost pump B of a collector shall be supplied from independent AC electrical sources.
Where the paired collector boost pumps share a part number, a common-cause contributor shall be modelled explicitly and staggered overhaul intervals applied.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm independent AC feeds, physical separation of the paired pumps within the collector bay, and that the fault tree G-033 carries an explicit common-cause contributor for the identical parallel pumps.

cmaData.subject: G-038 — Loss of affected-side collector feed (both boost pumps fail) [SF-003-PL2]
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two parallel boost pumps feeding one collector cell.. The two AC boost pumps on the affected collector fail independently (AND-gate: BP1 AND BP2 on affected collector).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: SDD states two AC boost pumps per collector operate in parallel but does not state an electrical source split between them — a shared AC supply loss would fail both, defeating the AND. Development/Design: pumps are of the same type (implied redundant pair) — a common design/lot deficiency is credible. Installation Design / Environment: both pumps are in the same wing box (zone 510/520, flammable fluid present, single spanwise gallery region) — a zonal event strikes both. Table M2 concerns: [1] Shared AC bus | both pumps unpowered | mitigating factor NOT established in SDD; [2] Common pump part number | simultaneous wear/design failure | staggered overhaul not stated for pumps; [3] Zone 510/520 co-location | fire/leak fails both | separate clipping not stated.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the two boost pumps on each collector to be supplied from different electrical sources (different AC buses); confirm gravity feed below FL150 as an independent backstop leg (already modelled at node 90); apply zonal separation/clipping to the pump pair within the wing box. Where source split cannot be assured, add a shared-AC-supply common-cause contributor to the G-038 AND rather than leaving a bare independent AND.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Each collector's two boost pumps shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single AC bus loss disables both.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-built electrical source assignment of the two boost pumps per collector and confirm zonal separation; close against wiring/EPS installation drawings.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two parallel boost pumps feeding one collector cell.
aiRequirements: Each collector's two boost pumps shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single AC bus loss disables both.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm as-built electrical source assignment of the two boost pumps per collector and confirm zonal separation; close against wiring/EPS installation drawings.

cmaData.subject: G-041 — Asymmetric partial loss of fuel delivery (one side degraded) [SF-003-PL2]
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the cross-feed rebalance path from the affected-side collector loss.. The three legs (affected-side collector feed lost AND cross-feed gallery cannot rebalance AND gravity feed unavailable) are independent.
cmaData.findings: Common Resources / Installation Design: SDD states cross-feed is a SINGLE spanwise gallery through the wing box and is 'the only path by which fuel from one side reaches an engine on the other' — a single blockage/isolation-valve failure defeats the rebalance leg, so the AND overstates protection if the gallery and the collector share a common wing-box cause. Environment: the single gallery transits zones 510, 530, 300, 540, 520 (flammable fluid / pressure-boundary transit) — a zonal event on the wing box can strike both the affected collector and the gallery. The SDD itself flags the gallery for particular-risk and zonal attention. Table M2 concerns: [1] Single spanwise cross-feed gallery | rebalance leg not independent of collector loss when a common wing-box event acts | SDD flags gallery for PRA/ZSA; [2] Cross-feed isolation valves (four) | common drive/design | valve fails to last position stated but common-cause valve fault not excluded; [3] Gravity path availability tied to altitude (below FL150) | not an independent leg above FL150 | operational limit.
cmaData.mitigation:
Reconcile the G-041 AND with the single-gallery finding: treat cross-feed gallery blockage as a common element and ensure the tree does not credit the rebalance leg where a single wing-box event can also fail the collector; carry the gallery into PRA/ZSA (SDD already retains it). Confirm the four isolation valves do not share a single drive/command that could fail the gallery closed.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The cross-feed rebalance capability shall not be credited as independent of an affected-side collector loss where a single wing-box event can act on both.
• The four cross-feed isolation valves shall not share a single command/drive channel whose loss isolates the gallery.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA plus PRA/ZSA on the single spanwise cross-feed gallery routing to confirm no common wing-box event defeats both the collector feed and the rebalance path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the cross-feed rebalance path from the affected-side collector loss.
aiRequirements: The cross-feed rebalance capability shall not be credited as independent of an affected-side collector loss where a single wing-box event can act on both.
The four cross-feed isolation valves shall not share a single command/drive channel whose loss isolates the gallery.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA plus PRA/ZSA on the single spanwise cross-feed gallery routing to confirm no common wing-box event defeats both the collector feed and the rebalance path.

cmaData.subject: SF-004-TL — Complete loss of fuel mass management (auto scheduling AND manual cross-feed both lost)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the automatic scheduling path from the manual cross-feed path.. Loss of automatic fuel mass scheduling and loss of manual cross-feed capability are independent (top AND).
cmaData.findings: Common Resources: the fault tree already shows both legs depend on 'Loss of transfer/cross-feed valve actuation' (nodes 115 and 119) — the same valve actuation hardware is a shared element across both AND inputs, so the two legs are NOT fully independent; this is a repeated-event common cause. Development/Design: automatic scheduling uses two valve-drive electrical channels (nodes 113/114); manual cross-feed uses crew selection plus the same valve actuation — the valves and their drive are common. Installation Design: transfer/isolation valves and the cross-feed gallery sit in the wing box (zones 510/520/300) — a zonal event acts on the shared valve set. Table M2 concerns: [1] Shared transfer/cross-feed valve actuation | present in both AND legs | should appear as a repeated event / common-cause gate, not two independent legs; [2] Two valve-drive electrical channels | common design/routing | dissimilarity/routing split not stated; [3] Wing-box co-location of valves | single zonal event | separation not stated.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model the shared transfer/cross-feed valve actuation explicitly as a repeated event (or a dedicated common-cause gate) under the SF-004-TL top AND rather than as two independent legs, so the AND does not overstate protection; confirm the two valve-drive electrical channels are independently sourced and routed; carry valve co-location into ZSA. This principle underpins any DAL reduction on SF-004 — if the shared valve independence fails, the reduction resting on the AND is invalidated.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The shared transfer/cross-feed valve actuation common to the automatic and manual paths shall be modelled as a common-cause contributor in the SF-004-TL fault tree.
• The two valve-drive electrical channels shall be independently sourced and separately routed.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-built independence of the two valve-drive channels and to confirm the SF-004-TL tree carries the shared valve actuation as a repeated/common-cause event.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the automatic scheduling path from the manual cross-feed path.
aiRequirements: The shared transfer/cross-feed valve actuation common to the automatic and manual paths shall be modelled as a common-cause contributor in the SF-004-TL fault tree.
The two valve-drive electrical channels shall be independently sourced and separately routed.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm as-built independence of the two valve-drive channels and to confirm the SF-004-TL tree carries the shared valve actuation as a repeated/common-cause event.

cmaData.subject: G-042 — Loss of both valve-drive electrical channels (SF-004-TL)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the two valve-drive electrical channels driving the transfer/cross-feed valves.. Valve-drive electrical channel 1 and channel 2 fail independently, so complete loss of automatic fuel mass scheduling requires both to be lost.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (EPS): the two valve-drive channels are electrically powered; the SDD states each transfer valve 'can be driven from either of two electrical channels' but does not state the source bus of each channel, so a shared main/essential bus or shared DC feed could defeat the AND. | Installation Design (routing): DC power to the valves is carried by the EWS; if both channels share a bundle or route the claim is not assured — SDD does not resolve the per-channel route. | Development/Design: no dissimilarity is claimed between the two channels; a common design/software fault in valve-drive command logic is a candidate common cause. | Environment: valves and drive electronics sit in the wing/wing-box fuel zones (flammable-fluid, zones 510/520/300) — a shared thermal or zonal event is a candidate.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two valve-drive electrical channels shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
• The two valve-drive channels shall be routed in physically separated EWS runs (HV/LV left vs right) with no shared bundle or penetration.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the two valve-drive electrical channels driving the transfer/cross-feed valves.
aiRequirements: The two valve-drive electrical channels shall be supplied from independent electrical sources such that no single bus loss disables both.
The two valve-drive channels shall be routed in physically separated EWS runs (HV/LV left vs right) with no shared bundle or penetration.

cmaData.subject: SF-004-M3 outer AND — Undetected fuel mass distribution error
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the fuel-distribution error branch and the imbalance-detection/annunciation branch.. An erroneous fuel mass distribution and the failure to annunciate it are independent, so the undetected condition requires both to coincide.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (EPS/AVI): the distribution branch (transfer/cross-feed valves and scheduler) and the annunciation branch (imbalance monitor + fuel-quantity indication + crew alerting) both draw on electrical power and avionics; a common EPS or avionics loss can both mis-schedule distribution and suppress its annunciation, defeating the AND. | Common Resource (sensing): erroneous tank quantity/CG data feeds BOTH the automatic scheduler (causing the error) AND the quantity indication/imbalance annunciation (masking it) — a single erroneous quantity source is a shared cause across both branches and should appear as a repeated event. | Development/Design: the imbalance annunciation function and fuel-quantity indication path are avionics-hosted; common software/host is a candidate common cause. | Latency: the annunciation branch is a latent/monitor function — its dormancy is the coupling that makes the outer AND a latent-plus-active combination requiring exposure-time treatment.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The fuel quantity/CG data used by the automatic transfer scheduler shall be independent of the data used by the imbalance annunciation, or the shared source shall be modelled as a common-cause repeated event.
• The imbalance annunciation function shall not share its electrical source or processing host with the transfer/cross-feed valve command path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the fuel-distribution error branch and the imbalance-detection/annunciation branch.
aiRequirements: The fuel quantity/CG data used by the automatic transfer scheduler shall be independent of the data used by the imbalance annunciation, or the shared source shall be modelled as a common-cause repeated event.
The imbalance annunciation function shall not share its electrical source or processing host with the transfer/cross-feed valve command path.

cmaData.subject: G-053 — Imbalance not annunciated to crew (SF-004-M3)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the imbalance annunciation function and the fuel-quantity indication path.. The imbalance annunciation function and the fuel-quantity indication path fail independently, so loss of crew awareness of imbalance requires both.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource (AVI): both the imbalance annunciation and the fuel-quantity indication are consumers of the avionics system, which 'serves all systems' and consolidates status into a single crew alert list — a single avionics/alerting loss can take both, defeating the AND. | Common Resource (EPS): both paths are electrically powered; imbalance/low-pressure discretes and quantity indication trace to the avionics displays on shared bus feeds — a shared bus loss is a candidate. | Common Resource (sensing): both branches can be driven from the same tank quantity sensing; a single erroneous or lost quantity source removes both the annunciation and the indication. | Development/Design: the alerting system runs on 'two independent processing channels' per the SDD — if the quantity indication and the imbalance annunciation both resolve onto the same avionics channel the independence is not assured; per-channel allocation is not stated.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The imbalance annunciation and the fuel-quantity indication shall be allocated to independent avionics processing/display resources such that a single avionics loss does not remove both.
• The tank quantity sensing feeding the imbalance annunciation shall be independent of, or diverse from, the sensing feeding the quantity indication.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the imbalance annunciation function and the fuel-quantity indication path.
aiRequirements: The imbalance annunciation and the fuel-quantity indication shall be allocated to independent avionics processing/display resources such that a single avionics loss does not remove both.
The tank quantity sensing feeding the imbalance annunciation shall be independent of, or diverse from, the sensing feeding the quantity indication.

cmaData.subject: SF-005-M3 top AND — erroneous-roll-command path vs. loss-of-annunciation path independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the roll-control command/actuation path and the detection/annunciation path (surface-position feedback + crew alerting).. The erroneous roll command (G-063) and the failure to annunciate it (node 172) are independent, so both must fail for the undetected condition.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / AVI processing: surface-position & FCS-status feedback (node 173) and crew alerting (node 174) both stand on the DC essential bus and shared avionics processing, which also serve the FCC command path. A DC-essential or AVI processing loss is a single shared cause that can both corrupt the roll command and suppress its annunciation, collapsing the AND. This is not a functional dependency already modelled, so it is a common-cause contributor. Installation: bay assignment of the alerting channels vs FCCs not resolved in the SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Model DC-essential / AVI-processing common cause as an explicit beta-factor CCF event combined with the AND rather than leaving a bare AND; require the annunciation path (surface-position sensing + alerting) to be powered and processed independently of the FCC command path so that no single bus or processor loss defeats both.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The FCS-status/surface-position feedback and crew-alerting paths shall not share an electrical source or processing resource with the FCC roll-command generation path such that a single failure defeats both detection and command integrity.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm as-built power and processing segregation between the roll-command path and the annunciation path; reconcile against EPS bus allocation and AVI architecture.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the roll-control command/actuation path and the detection/annunciation path (surface-position feedback + crew alerting).
aiRequirements: The FCS-status/surface-position feedback and crew-alerting paths shall not share an electrical source or processing resource with the FCC roll-command generation path such that a single failure defeats both detection and command integrity.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm as-built power and processing segregation between the roll-command path and the annunciation path; reconcile against EPS bus allocation and AVI architecture.

cmaData.subject: G-063 AND — erroneous roll command generation vs. roll-surface actuation independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the FCC command channels and the hydraulic roll-surface actuation supplies (HYD B, HYD C).. Erroneous command generation (G-061) and the actuation drive on HYD B / HYD C (node 169) are independent.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource / hydraulic: aileron/spoiler actuation is on HYD B (node 170) and HYD C (node 171). Per the SDD, systems A and B share a wing-root run but C is routed separately, so the B/C pair used here is genuinely dual-supply and the hydraulic coupling is weak. Residual Installation-Design concern: FCCs and actuator control electronics co-located within equipment bays / along shared routing could couple command generation to actuation drive; the SDD does not resolve ACE installation. Environment/EMI along shared LV signal routing is a further candidate at the two mid-bay HV/LV crossing points.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the B/C dual-supply as the mitigating factor for the hydraulic leg; capture any FCC-to-ACE co-location or shared LV routing as an explicit installation common-cause contributor and verify separation in the ZSA.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Actuator control electronics for roll surfaces shall be installed and routed such that no single zonal event couples the FCC roll-command path to the roll-surface actuation drive.
Verification (SSA/ASA): ZSA/SSA to confirm HYD B and HYD C do not share a wing-root run for roll actuation and that ACE installation is segregated from the FCC command path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the FCC command channels and the hydraulic roll-surface actuation supplies (HYD B, HYD C).
aiRequirements: Actuator control electronics for roll surfaces shall be installed and routed such that no single zonal event couples the FCC roll-command path to the roll-surface actuation drive.
cmaData.aiVerification: ZSA/SSA to confirm HYD B and HYD C do not share a wing-root run for roll actuation and that ACE installation is segregated from the FCC command path.

cmaData.subject: G-061 AND — three-FCC independence for erroneous roll command surviving voting
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three dissimilar flight control computers and their cross-monitor/voting on the roll command.. FCC 1 (forward bay), FCC 2 (mid bay) and FCC 3 (aft bay) independently generate/pass an erroneous roll command, so all three must fail for the command to survive voting.
cmaData.findings: Development/Design common cause: the SDD hosts software from only TWO teams across THREE computers under a dissimilarity argument, so at least two of the three FCCs share a software team — a common specification/software error is a credible shared cause that all three (or at least the co-team pair) could pass identically, defeating the voting AND. Common Resource / power: each FCC is on a different electrical source, which mitigates power common cause. Design (logic): the '-undetected' character depends on the same cross-monitor/voting function, so a common voting-logic defect is itself a shared cause of non-detection. Installation-Design: the three FCCs are in three separate bays (forward/mid/aft), a genuine physical-separation mitigation. This AND underpins the DAL-A allocation on this page; if the dissimilarity or voting-integrity claim fails, that allocation is not supported.

Common Resources (Electrical / Processing) — crew alerting and surface-position feedback both consume EPS/AVI resources | Shared bus or processing loss removes the annunciation while the abnormal condition persists | Alerting driven by two independent processing channels; DC essential bus feeds FCC, standby, alerting (SDD §5.5.2/§5.11.2)
Installation-Design — actuation and its position sensing co-located at the surface | A local mechanical event could both cause motion and disable the sensing at that surface | Independent position sensing; verify sensing not defeated by the same actuator/surface fault
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the pitch surface-position/status feedback and the crew-alerting path do not share a resource or FCC channel with the pitch command generation such that one fault both causes and hides the motion; substantiate the two independent alerting channels.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• Detection of uncommanded pitch motion shall not depend on the same FCC channel or data source that generates the pitch command.
• Loss of a single electrical/processing resource shall not simultaneously permit uncommanded pitch motion and remove its annunciation.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: independence analysis of the pitch surface-position feedback and crew-alerting channels against the pitch command path; confirmation of dual independent alerting processing.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Hazard (uncommanded pitch) and its detection (surface-position feedback + crew alerting) rely on separable resources.
aiRequirements: Detection of uncommanded pitch motion shall not depend on the same FCC channel or data source that generates the pitch command.
Loss of a single electrical/processing resource shall not simultaneously permit uncommanded pitch motion and remove its annunciation.
