cmaData.subject: G-098 (SF-007-M) — erroneous FCC rudder command vs voting/monitor independence
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Command generation and cross-monitor/voting are separable so a monitor catches an errant command.. An erroneous FCC rudder command and the failure of the command voting/monitor to correct it are independent, so both must fail together.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Common Resources (Development/Design — software) — if the voting/monitor is hosted in the same FCC channel that generates the erroneous command, a common design/software fault defeats both | The monitor cannot independently reject an error produced by its own host channel | Three dissimilar FCCs voting on command, software by two teams under a dissimilarity argument (SDD §5.3.2)
Common Resources (Processing / Electrical) — common processing platform or common electrical source across the voting set | A shared resource fault corrupts command and voting together | Each FCC supplied from a different electrical source (SDD §5.3.2)
Common Environment / Installation — three FCCs in three bays (fwd/mid/aft) reduce co-location risk | Zonal event unlikely to strike all three | FCCs in three separate equipment bays (SDD §5.3.5)
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the rudder-command voting/monitor function is not co-hosted with, and does not share software or a common resource with, the FCC channel that can generate the erroneous command; rely on and substantiate the three-way dissimilar FCC voting and dissimilar software teams.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The rudder command voting/monitor shall be independent of the FCC channel generating the command such that a single design or software fault cannot both produce an erroneous command and suppress its rejection.
• Each FCC in the rudder command vote shall be supplied from an independent electrical source.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA: FCC dissimilarity and monitor-independence substantiation confirming voting/monitor is not defeated by the command-source channel; DO-178C dissimilarity argument evidence.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Command generation and cross-monitor/voting are separable so a monitor catches an errant command.
aiRequirements: The rudder command voting/monitor shall be independent of the FCC channel generating the command such that a single design or software fault cannot both produce an erroneous command and suppress its rejection.
Each FCC in the rudder command vote shall be supplied from an independent electrical source.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA: FCC dissimilarity and monitor-independence substantiation confirming voting/monitor is not defeated by the command-source channel; DO-178C dissimilarity argument evidence.

cmaData.subject: FCC voting independence — erroneous rudder command (G-103)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three FCC channels in generating/voting a yaw command. The three dissimilar flight control computers fail independently, so an erroneous rudder command survives voting only by coincident independent channel faults (AND gate 280, SF-007-M2).
cmaData.findings: Common Development/Design: FCS hosts software developed by one of only two teams under a dissimilarity argument, so at least two of the three voting channels can share a software team — a common design/error source that can defeat the voting AND. Common Data/Sensors: all three FCCs consume shared air-data and inertial reference; an erroneous air-data/inertial input can drive a correlated erroneous yaw command across channels (mirrors the modelled leg 'erroneous sensor input'). Installation-Design: FCC 1/2/3 are in three separate bays (fwd/mid/aft) on three different electrical sources — separation supports the claim against physical/power common cause. Common environment/co-location not credible across three bays.
cmaData.mitigation: Retain three-bay physical and electrical separation. Substantiate the two-team dissimilarity argument covers the yaw command path (which channels share a team). Add air-data/inertial input reasonableness/cross-monitoring so a shared erroneous input cannot pass all three channels; model the shared-input common cause explicitly as a contributor to gate 280 rather than as an independent AND.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three FCC channels in generating/voting a yaw command

cmaData.subject: FCC voting independence — erroneous yaw command (G-105)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of FCC channels 1/2/3 in computing the yaw/rudder command. FCC channel 1/2/3 erroneous yaw commands are independent, so a wrong rudder position from computation error requires coincident channel faults (AND gate 287, SF-007-M3).
cmaData.findings: Common Development/Design: software from one of only two teams under a dissimilarity argument means the three voting channels are not fully dissimilar; a common specification or software error is a common-cause contributor to the computation AND. Common Data/Sensors: shared air-data/inertial reference feeding all three channels can produce a correlated computation error. Installation-Design: three separate equipment bays and different electrical sources support separation against physical/power common cause. This gate underpins the DAL-A allocation on the page; a failed dissimilarity/independence claim would invalidate any credit taken for the three-way vote.
cmaData.mitigation: Substantiate that the dissimilarity argument actually separates the yaw computation across teams. Provide independent input monitoring so a shared erroneous air-data/inertial value cannot corrupt all three computations. Represent the shared specification/software and shared-input causes as explicit common-cause events combined with the independent-failure logic of the three-channel group, per NASA-FTH common-cause modelling.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of FCC channels 1/2/3 in computing the yaw/rudder command

cmaData.subject: Erroneous-yaw source vs crew detection independence (SF-007-M3 top AND)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the erroneous-command/response leg and the crew-alerting/annunciation leg. The erroneous yaw surface response and the failure to annunciate asymmetry/jam are independent, so an undetected erroneous yaw response requires both (AND gate 285).
cmaData.findings: Common Development/Design & Data: FCS produces the asymmetry/jam discrete that feeds crew alerting; the same FCC/FCS chain generating the erroneous yaw command also sources the discrete that would annunciate it, so a common FCS fault can both cause the error and suppress its annunciation — defeating the detection AND. Common processing: the two crew-alerting channels (A and B) are consolidated by the AVI alerting system into a single prioritised list on two processing channels; a common alerting-logic error is a common-cause contributor to gate 294. Installation: alerting channels A/B routed to support the two-channel claim — separation credited but the FCS-discrete-to-alerting dependency remains a logical common cause.
cmaData.mitigation: Ensure the asymmetry/jam detection derives from surface-position sensing independent of the command-generation path, not solely from the same FCC that issues the command. Verify the two alerting processing channels do not share the failure mode that would be triggered by the erroneous yaw event. Model the shared FCS-discrete dependency explicitly as a common-cause contributor to the SF-007-M3 top gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the erroneous-command/response leg and the crew-alerting/annunciation leg

cmaData.subject: G-107 — Yaw asymmetry/jam annunciation not provided (undetected)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the yaw-response leg and the crew-annunciation leg of SF-007-M3.. Erroneous yaw surface response AND loss of asymmetry/jam annunciation are independent, so an erroneous yaw response cannot go undetected from a single cause.
cmaData.findings: Both crew-alerting channels (nodes 296/297) draw from the DC essential bus and are hosted by the AVI alerting system; the FCS asymmetry/jam discrete (node 295) is a single discrete into that alerting. Common Resources (DC essential bus, AVI processing) and Development/Design (common alerting software) can defeat the annunciation-independence leg. Verification-phase concern: shared supply/processing couples the two 'fails to annunciate' basic events that the AND-within-annunciation gate treats as independent.
cmaData.mitigation: Confirm the two alerting channels are supplied from segregated buses or that at least one annunciation path does not stand on the DC essential bus; confirm dissimilarity of the two alerting processing channels; verify the FCS asymmetry/jam discrete is not the sole detection source. Where not assured, model the shared supply/processing as a common-cause contributor on the annunciation gate.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the yaw-response leg and the crew-annunciation leg of SF-007-M3.

cmaData.subject: SF-007-M4 — Uncommanded yaw motion — undetected (top AND, G-108)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the uncommanded-deflection leg and the crew-annunciation leg of SF-007-M4.. Uncommanded rudder deflection AND non-annunciation of uncommanded yaw are independent.
cmaData.findings: The annunciation leg (nodes 308/309) uses the same two crew-alerting channels on the DC essential bus and the AVI alerting; the surface-position/asymmetry discrete (node 307) is a single FCS discrete. Common Resources (DC essential bus, AVI processing) and shared routing of the alerting channels can defeat the independence of the two 'fails to annunciate' basic events. Same coupling as G-107 applies to this top AND.
cmaData.mitigation: Segregate the two alerting channel supplies or ensure one annunciation path survives DC-essential loss; verify dissimilar alerting processing; confirm surface-position/asymmetry detection is not a single discrete. Add a common-cause contributor to the annunciation gate where independence is not assured.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the uncommanded-deflection leg and the crew-annunciation leg of SF-007-M4.

cmaData.subject: G-109 — FCC generates uncommanded yaw output
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the three flight control computer channels driving the uncommanded-yaw AND gate.. FCC channels 1, 2 and 3 each independently produce an uncommanded yaw output, so all three must fail together.
cmaData.findings: SDD claims three dissimilar FCCs, each on a different electrical source, installed in three separate bays with dissimilar software from two teams — a genuine Common Resources / Installation-Design / Development-Design mitigation. Residual concerns: (a) Development/Design — the dissimilarity argument covers two teams for three computers, so at least two channels may share a software team; (b) common specification and common tools across all three; (c) FCC-3 (aft equipment bay, zone 400) proximity to the aft rudder control runs (zone 800). These are verification-phase items to confirm the dissimilarity claim genuinely covers all three channels.
cmaData.mitigation: Verify the two-team dissimilarity actually separates at least the pair most relied on; verify no common specification/tool defect defeats all three; confirm the three power sources are genuinely independent per §5.5; substantiate FCC bay separation against zonal/PRA findings. Where the dissimilarity argument underpins a DAL reduction, a failed principle invalidates that reduction.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the three flight control computer channels driving the uncommanded-yaw AND gate.

cmaData.subject: G-111 — SF-007-M4 uncommanded yaw motion undetected: independence of uncommanded-yaw occurrence and failure-to-annunciate
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the FCS uncommanded-yaw output path and the crew-alerting annunciation path. Uncommanded rudder deflection AND loss of annunciation occur independently (AND-gate node 298/306, page SF-007-M4)
cmaData.findings: Alerting is driven by two independent processing channels, and FCS asymmetry/jam discretes feed avionics; however both the FCS command computation and the crew alerting draw on the DC essential bus, and the alerting consolidation is a single prioritised list — a common electrical-resource or alerting-processing failure could both permit the uncommanded yaw and suppress its annunciation, defeating the AND.
cmaData.mitigation:
Confirm the surface-position/asymmetry discrete path and the crew-alerting channels do not share the electrical source that the FCC yaw output depends on; require dual independent alerting processing channels on separated supplies; add a common-cause contributor (shared DC essential bus / shared alerting processing) as a repeated event under the AND gate if commonality is confirmed.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The uncommanded-yaw annunciation path shall not share an electrical source or processing resource with the FCS yaw command output path such that a single failure defeats both.
• Surface-position/asymmetry discretes to avionics shall be independent of the FCC that generates the yaw command.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to verify (this analysis is development-phase, output is independence requirements): confirm electrical-source segregation between FCS yaw output and alerting channels A/B against the as-built EWS routing.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the FCS uncommanded-yaw output path and the crew-alerting annunciation path
aiRequirements: The uncommanded-yaw annunciation path shall not share an electrical source or processing resource with the FCS yaw command output path such that a single failure defeats both.
Surface-position/asymmetry discretes to avionics shall be independent of the FCC that generates the yaw command.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to verify (this analysis is development-phase, output is independence requirements): confirm electrical-source segregation between FCS yaw output and alerting channels A/B against the as-built EWS routing.

cmaData.subject: G-113 — SF-008-TL complete loss of high-lift: independence of the two power drive units
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between high-lift PDU 1 and PDU 2. Power drive unit 1 AND power drive unit 2 fail independently (AND-gate node 311, page SF-008-TL)
cmaData.findings: The SDD states the two independent PDUs drive through a COMMON TORQUE SHAFT with asymmetry brakes at each section. The common torque shaft is a single mechanical element common to both PDU drive paths: a torque-shaft failure defeats the PDU-1-AND-PDU-2 independence claim directly. The tree already carries a separate 'Common torque shaft failure (single-...)' OR input (node 314) — the AND between the two PDUs therefore overstates protection unless the shared shaft and shared hydraulic/electrical motive resource (node 319) are modelled explicitly as they are.
cmaData.mitigation:
Retain the common torque shaft as its own OR contributor under SF-008-TL (already node 314) rather than crediting PDU independence beyond the drive train; verify the two PDUs do not additionally share the same hydraulic supply or electrical source; confirm the asymmetry brakes are independent of the shaft failure they must arrest.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two high-lift power drive units shall not share a hydraulic or electrical motive resource such that a single resource loss disables both.
• The common torque shaft shall be modelled as a single-point common-cause contributor to complete loss of high-lift, not absorbed into the PDU AND gate.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm the torque shaft, PDU motive supplies and asymmetry brakes are represented per the as-built high-lift drive architecture.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between high-lift PDU 1 and PDU 2
aiRequirements: The two high-lift power drive units shall not share a hydraulic or electrical motive resource such that a single resource loss disables both.
The common torque shaft shall be modelled as a single-point common-cause contributor to complete loss of high-lift, not absorbed into the PDU AND gate.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm the torque shaft, PDU motive supplies and asymmetry brakes are represented per the as-built high-lift drive architecture.

cmaData.subject: G-114 — SF-008-TL complete loss of high-lift: independence of high-lift command from FCC 1/2/3
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the three flight control computers' high-lift command outputs. FCC 1 AND FCC 2 AND FCC 3 high-lift command loss occur independently (AND-gate node 315, page SF-008-TL)
cmaData.findings: The three FCCs are dissimilar, installed in three separate bays (forward/mid/aft equipment bay), each supplied from a different electrical source, hosting software from one of two teams under a dissimilarity argument — a genuine independence argument against random and design common cause. Residual common-mode concerns: the high-lift command interface/specification is common to all three, and the two-team software dissimilarity means at most two dissimilar software builds across three channels; a common high-lift requirement error would affect all three.
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the high-lift command specification and interface definition do not introduce a single common requirement/specification error path across all three FCCs; confirm the software dissimilarity split covers the high-lift command function specifically; retain the three-source electrical and three-bay physical separation as the installation-design mitigation.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The high-lift command function specification shall be verified free of a single common error that could disable the command in all three flight control computers.
• The three flight control computers' high-lift command paths shall retain electrical-source and bay separation as installed.
Verification (SSA/ASA): SSA/ASA to confirm dissimilarity coverage of the high-lift command function and physical/electrical separation of the three FCC high-lift command paths as built.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the three flight control computers' high-lift command outputs
aiRequirements: The high-lift command function specification shall be verified free of a single common error that could disable the command in all three flight control computers.
The three flight control computers' high-lift command paths shall retain electrical-source and bay separation as installed.
cmaData.aiVerification: SSA/ASA to confirm dissimilarity coverage of the high-lift command function and physical/electrical separation of the three FCC high-lift command paths as built.

cmaData.subject: High-lift asymmetric-deployment independence (SF-008-M) — PDU/torque-shaft vs asymmetry-brake arrest
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the differential-motion cause from the asymmetry-brake arrest function.. AND gate asserts a differential-motion source (torque shaft disconnect / one PDU driving against a fixed section / single PDU runaway) is independent of the asymmetry brakes failing to arrest it, so both are required for asymmetric deployment.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) Common torque shaft is the SHARED mechanical element between the two PDUs — a disconnect or fracture is simultaneously the differential-motion source AND removes the mechanical tie the arrest logic relies on | Defeats the independence: one mechanical event can appear in both AND inputs | SDD states asymmetry brakes are fitted 'at each section'; whether brake set is independent of torque-shaft integrity is not substantiated — recorded as concern (Installation-Design / Development-Design common cause).
(2) Asymmetry detection and asymmetry-brake command share sensing/control (single monitor commanding the brakes) | If detection is the common element, a detection fault removes arrest for a real asymmetry | SDD does not describe redundant, dissimilar asymmetry sensing — Common Resources (sensing/processing) concern.
(3) Common electrical/hydraulic resource to both PDUs and to the brake actuation | A shared resource loss removes drive symmetry and arrest together | SDD §5.3.4 shows FCS consumes HYD A/B/C and EPS; specific supply to the two PDUs and to the asymmetry brakes not segregated in the description — Common Resources concern.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (development feedback to PSSA): (a) asymmetry-brake set must not depend on torque-shaft integrity or continuity; (b) asymmetry sensing must be independent per half-span and independent of the PDU command path; (c) the two PDUs and the asymmetry-brake actuation must not share a single electrical/hydraulic resource whose loss defeats both AND inputs.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The high-lift asymmetry brakes shall arrest differential surface motion independently of common-torque-shaft integrity.
• The high-lift asymmetry detection shall be independent per half-span and independent of the PDU command path.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the differential-motion cause from the asymmetry-brake arrest function.
aiRequirements: The high-lift asymmetry brakes shall arrest differential surface motion independently of common-torque-shaft integrity.
The high-lift asymmetry detection shall be independent per half-span and independent of the PDU command path.

cmaData.subject: Undetected asymmetric high-lift (SF-008-M3, G-126) — asymmetry occurrence vs its detection/annunciation
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the asymmetry-generating mechanism from the asymmetry detection/annunciation function.. AND gate G-126 asserts the asymmetric high-lift condition occurring is independent of the crew/monitor failing to detect and arrest it, so both are required for the undetected condition.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) The same position-sensing that would detect asymmetry may also be the feedback the drive/monitor relies on | If asymmetry arises from a sensing fault, that fault can equally suppress detection | Common Resources (position sensing) concern; SDD does not describe sensing dissimilar to the asymmetry monitor.
(2) Common torque shaft disconnect (G-126 child) both creates asymmetry AND may deprive the position monitor of a reference on one side | Single mechanical event feeds both AND inputs | Installation-Design / mechanical common cause; brake-set and monitor reference independence from shaft integrity not substantiated.
(3) Shared processing/annunciation channel between asymmetry monitor and crew alerting | A monitor/alerting fault removes detection for any asymmetry cause | SDD §5.3.4 lists 'asymmetry and jam discretes' to avionics but does not show redundant annunciation for this discrete — Common Resources concern.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (development): asymmetry position sensing shall be independent of the drive/torque-shaft reference; the asymmetry-detection-to-crew-alerting path shall not share a single processing channel with the mechanism that generates asymmetry. Verification notes to close in SSA once the sensing and alerting architecture is defined.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• High-lift asymmetry position sensing shall be independent of the PDU/torque-shaft drive reference.
• The high-lift asymmetry detection and annunciation path shall not share a single processing channel with the asymmetry-generating drive.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the asymmetry-generating mechanism from the asymmetry detection/annunciation function.
aiRequirements: High-lift asymmetry position sensing shall be independent of the PDU/torque-shaft drive reference.
The high-lift asymmetry detection and annunciation path shall not share a single processing channel with the asymmetry-generating drive.

cmaData.subject: Asymmetry not detected / arrested (G-125) — asymmetry-brake set vs asymmetry-detection monitor
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence of the mechanical brake-set function from the asymmetry-detection/monitor function.. AND gate G-125 asserts the asymmetry brake failing to set at the affected section is independent of the position-sensing / asymmetry-monitor failing, so both are required for the asymmetry to go un-arrested.
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
(1) If the asymmetry monitor is the element that commands the brakes, a monitor fault removes BOTH the detection and the arrest command | Directly collapses the two AND inputs into one | SDD does not confirm the brake set is triggered independently of the position/asymmetry monitor — Common Resources (sensing/command) concern; this is the load-bearing independence gap.
(2) Common electrical supply to the asymmetry-brake actuation and to the position-sensing/monitor | A single supply loss defeats both inputs | SDD §5.3.4 shows FCS on EPS; per-function segregation of brake actuation vs monitor supply not described — Common Resources concern.
(3) Co-location of brake mechanism and position sensor at each flap/slat section | A local environmental event (mechanical/thermal) at one section could disable both | Installation-Design / Environment concern; separation at section level not substantiated in the SDD.
cmaData.mitigation:
Independence requirements (development): the asymmetry brake shall set on a mechanical/independent trigger not routed through the same monitor that provides detection; brake actuation and position sensing shall draw on segregated supplies; section-level installation shall separate the brake mechanism from its position sensor sufficient to survive a single local event. If the brake command genuinely originates from the same monitor, the AND independence does not hold and any DAL reduction resting on it is invalid.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The high-lift asymmetry brake shall set on a trigger independent of the asymmetry-detection monitor.
• Asymmetry-brake actuation and high-lift position sensing shall draw on segregated electrical supplies.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence of the mechanical brake-set function from the asymmetry-detection/monitor function.
aiRequirements: The high-lift asymmetry brake shall set on a trigger independent of the asymmetry-detection monitor.
Asymmetry-brake actuation and high-lift position sensing shall draw on segregated electrical supplies.

cmaData.subject: NZD lock/unlock — ECS pressure interlock in series with unlock command (SF-014-M, claim G-182)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the unlock command path and the ECS-derived pressure interlock that gates it.. The ECS pressure interlock independently inhibits the unlock command so that an inadvertent unlock cannot occur while the hold is pressurised.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — EPS: the interlock sensing/logic and the unlock command path both draw electrical power; a shared bus/feed loss or corruption could disable the interlock and enable the command together. Common Data — the interlock relies on the ECS residual-differential signal (<0.1 psi); an erroneous ECS pressure state both satisfies the interlock and misrepresents the true condition. Development/Design — interlock logic and unlock command logic co-hosted or common software would couple both. Installation — interlock and command wiring co-routed in zone 110/120 would expose both to one zonal event.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the pressure interlock to be powered and processed independently of the unlock command path (separate source, separate logic). Require the ECS differential signal used by the interlock to be independent of / cross-checked against the source used for annunciation. Require physical separation of interlock sensing harness from unlock command wiring per the EWS separation argument.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The nose-door pressure interlock shall be supplied and processed independently of the lock/unlock command path such that no single electrical-source or logic failure both disables the interlock and enables an unlock.
• The ECS residual-differential signal used by the unlock interlock shall be independent of the pressurisation-control channel used for crew annunciation.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the unlock command path and the ECS-derived pressure interlock that gates it.
aiRequirements: The nose-door pressure interlock shall be supplied and processed independently of the lock/unlock command path such that no single electrical-source or logic failure both disables the interlock and enables an unlock.
The ECS residual-differential signal used by the unlock interlock shall be independent of the pressurisation-control channel used for crew annunciation.

cmaData.subject: NZD lock-pin actuator — spurious run on ground-handling command path (SF-014-M, claim G-184)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the lock-pin actuator drive command and the enable/inhibit conditions that prevent inadvertent operation.. An inadvertent lock-pin actuator run cannot be commanded because the ground-handling command path and its enabling conditions are independent of a single spurious source.
cmaData.findings: Common Resource — EPS/HYD: the lock-pin actuator runs on a separate hydraulic supply and electrical backup drive; a spurious drive command on the electrical backup path plus loss of the enable interlock could couple. Operation — the door is operated from a ground-handling panel and cannot be operated in flight; the in-flight inhibit (WoW/pressure interlock) and the command path must not share a single failure that both removes the inhibit and issues the run. Development/Design — command logic and inhibit logic co-hosted would couple. Installation — command and inhibit wiring co-routed would expose both to one zonal event.
cmaData.mitigation:
Require the inadvertent-operation inhibit (pressure interlock plus operational lockout) to be independent of the lock-pin drive command source. Require the ground-handling command path to be inhibited by an independent enable that no single spurious source can both defeat and drive. Require separation of command and inhibit wiring.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• A spurious command on the lock-pin actuator drive path shall not run the actuator unless an independent enable (pressure interlock and operational lockout) is simultaneously satisfied.
• The lock-pin actuator inadvertent-operation inhibit shall be independent of the actuator drive command source such that no single failure both removes the inhibit and commands a run.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the lock-pin actuator drive command and the enable/inhibit conditions that prevent inadvertent operation.
aiRequirements: A spurious command on the lock-pin actuator drive path shall not run the actuator unless an independent enable (pressure interlock and operational lockout) is simultaneously satisfied.
The lock-pin actuator inadvertent-operation inhibit shall be independent of the actuator drive command source such that no single failure both removes the inhibit and commands a run.

cmaData.subject: NZD lock sensing — undetected loss of door latching and locking (SF-014-TL2, claim SF-014-TL2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: Independence between the proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator that together provide dual dissimilar lock-status detection.. A loss of door latching/locking cannot go undetected because two dissimilar, independently routed lock-sensing paths report status to the flight deck.
cmaData.findings: Common Environment / Installation — both sensing paths cross the zone boundary at the flight-deck bulkhead; although at two separated penetrations, a single bulkhead-region event could challenge both. Common Resource — EPS: the proximity sensing harness and indication draw electrical power; the mechanical indicator is dissimilar (no power) which supports the dissimilarity claim, but the electrical path plus crew alerting share power/processing. Development/Design — dissimilarity between proximity sensing and mechanical linkage mitigates common software/design. Operation/Maintenance — a common calibration or rigging action across both sensing paths, or a common maintenance error at the shared bulkhead penetrations, could defeat detection.
cmaData.mitigation:
Preserve the dissimilar (electrical proximity vs mechanical linkage) and independently-routed sensing argument. Require the two bulkhead penetrations to remain physically separated and not subject to a common zonal event (feed to PRA/ZSA of zone 110/120/130). Require maintenance/rigging procedures that prevent a single action miscalibrating both paths.
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two nose-door lock-sensing paths shall remain dissimilar and independently routed such that no single electrical, physical, or maintenance event defeats both.
• The maintenance/rigging procedure shall preclude a single action from simultaneously invalidating both the proximity sensing harness and the mechanical indicator linkage.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: Independence between the proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator that together provide dual dissimilar lock-status detection.
aiRequirements: The two nose-door lock-sensing paths shall remain dissimilar and independently routed such that no single electrical, physical, or maintenance event defeats both.
The maintenance/rigging procedure shall preclude a single action from simultaneously invalidating both the proximity sensing harness and the mechanical indicator linkage.

cmaData.subject: Door lock-status detection — dual dissimilar sensing independence (SF-014-TL2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing channels (undetected loss of door latching and locking). The proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator fail independently, so both channels are not lost by one cause
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Installation Design / co-location at bulkhead — both sensing paths cross the flight-deck bulkhead (zone 110→120→130) | An event at the shared bulkhead crossing could damage both paths | SDD claims two separated penetrations; separation credit unverified
Installation Design / common indication zone — both channels terminate at flight-deck indication in zone 130 | A zone-130 event or display-path loss defeats both readouts | Dissimilar indication means (electrical harness vs mechanical visual) partially decouples
Common Resource / electrical power to proximity harness | Loss of the harness supply removes the electrical channel, leaving only the mechanical indicator | Mechanical indicator is unpowered and independent of the harness supply
cmaData.mitigation:
Maintain two physically separated bulkhead penetrations for the sensing harness and the mechanical linkage; keep the mechanical visual indicator independent of the harness power feed; substantiate the separation credit by ZSA of zones 110/120/130 and PRA
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The nose door lock sensing harness and the mechanical indicator linkage shall be routed through two separated bulkhead penetrations with no shared support or connector.
• The mechanical visual lock indicator shall remain functional independent of electrical power to the proximity sensing harness.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing channels (undetected loss of door latching and locking)
aiRequirements: The nose door lock sensing harness and the mechanical indicator linkage shall be routed through two separated bulkhead penetrations with no shared support or connector.
The mechanical visual lock indicator shall remain functional independent of electrical power to the proximity sensing harness.

cmaData.subject: Door lock-status detection — dual dissimilar sensing independence (SF-015-TL)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing/indication channels (complete loss of lock status indication). The proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator fail independently, so lock status indication is not completely lost by one cause
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Installation Design / common termination zone — both channels present status in zone 130 (flight deck) | A zone-130 hazard could disable both indications simultaneously | Indication means are dissimilar (electrical display vs mechanical visual read)
Installation Design / paired bulkhead penetrations at zone 110→120→130 | Localised bulkhead damage at the crossing could sever both routed paths | SDD asserts two separated penetrations; credit to be verified by ZSA
Development/Design / dissimilar sensing types | Common specification error in the lock-status definition could affect both channels' logic | Sensing methods are physically dissimilar (proximity vs mechanical linkage)
cmaData.mitigation:
Verify the two indication channels share no display processing, no connector and no penetration; retain the mechanical visual indicator as a non-electrical means; close by ZSA of zone 130 and the 110/120/130 harness run
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The two lock-status sensing channels shall share no common connector, penetration or display processing path.
• Complete loss of lock status indication shall require the independent failure of both the proximity sensing channel and the mechanical visual indicator.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing/indication channels (complete loss of lock status indication)
aiRequirements: The two lock-status sensing channels shall share no common connector, penetration or display processing path.
Complete loss of lock status indication shall require the independent failure of both the proximity sensing channel and the mechanical visual indicator.

cmaData.subject: Door lock-status detection — dual dissimilar sensing independence (SF-015-M2)
cmaData.claim: Independence principle: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing channels (undetected erroneous lock status indication). The proximity sensing harness and the mechanical-linkage visual indicator fail independently, so a single cause does not drive both to the same erroneous lock status undetected
cmaData.findings:
Common Failure/Error Source Concern | Effect on the Principle | Mitigating Factor or Lack of Independence
Development/Design / common lock-status definition | A shared specification/logic error could make both channels indicate the same erroneous 'locked' state | Dissimilar sensing means (proximity reads pin position; linkage reads mechanically) reduces common logic error
Installation Design / paired bulkhead penetrations and common indication zone 130 | A single installation error at the crossing/display could bias both channels alike | SDD asserts separate routing and separated penetrations; credit unverified
Maintenance / common calibration or rigging action on both sensing paths | A shared maintenance error could set both to agree erroneously | Dissimilar channels normally require different maintenance actions; to be confirmed
cmaData.mitigation:
Ensure the two channels are specified, calibrated and maintained by dissimilar means so no single specification or maintenance action affects both; substantiate that an agreed erroneous 'locked' indication requires two independent failures; close by ZSA and maintenance-task independence review
Independence requirements (dev / PASA-PSSA):
• The proximity sensing channel and the mechanical indicator shall not share a common calibration or rigging maintenance action.
• An erroneous 'locked' indication shall require independent failure of both dissimilar lock-status channels to occur undetected.
cmaData.aiPrinciple: AND-gate independence of the two dissimilar lock-status sensing channels (undetected erroneous lock status indication)
aiRequirements: The proximity sensing channel and the mechanical indicator shall not share a common calibration or rigging maintenance action.
An erroneous 'locked' indication shall require independent failure of both dissimilar lock-status channels to occur undetected.

taskRows.task: Isolate a failed engine by closing the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle
Control thrust through four thrust levers with autothrottle
Select manual cross-feed and isolate any fuel tank
Select the hydraulic electric pumps on or off and command the power transfer unit
Manually override ram air turbine deployment
Operate landing gear by gear lever and apply braking by brake pedals, with autobrake available
Perform alternate landing gear extension from the separate handle
Operate the nose cargo door from the ground handling panel with the aircraft on jacks or gear
Verify nose door lock status as part of the take-off configuration check
Select environmental control pack configuration and bleed source
Select ice protection automatic or manual operation
Interact with the displays, flight management computers and alerting list; select reversionary display
Command engine or APU extinguishing through the fire handles
Don crew oxygen mask on crew action
Perform the pre-flight crew oxygen pressure check

cdRows.supports: Identifying non-normal system conditions and the appropriate crew action across every aircraft system
cdRows.finding: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures, driven by two independent processing channels.

cdRows.item: Consolidated prioritised crew alert list — prioritisation hierarchy
cdRows.supports: Detecting and responding to multiple simultaneous alerts in order of urgency
cdRows.finding: The list is described as prioritised but the document does not state the warning/caution/advisory hierarchy, attention-getting cues, or that cues span two senses; alerting means against §25.1322(b)/(c) are [not stated].

cdRows.supports: Crew awareness of reduced roll and pitch control authority following flight control computer or hydraulic degradation
cdRows.finding: Degraded laws are annunciated; reversion to mechanical control is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths.

cdRows.supports: Commanding roll and pitch with envelope protection active in the normal control law
cdRows.finding: The crew flies through conventional inceptors with envelope protection active in the normal control law; degraded laws are annunciated.

cdRows.item: Flight control asymmetry and jam discretes
cdRows.supports: Detecting surface asymmetry or jam affecting roll and pitch control
cdRows.finding: The flight control system outputs surface position, system status, flight envelope protection status, and asymmetry and jam discretes to the avionics displays.

cdRows.supports: Normal thrust control and isolation of a failed engine
cdRows.finding: Normal control is by four thrust levers with autothrottle; the only crew action to isolate a failed engine is to close the associated fuel shut-off and fire handle.

cdRows.supports: Monitoring engine state for detecting loss of forward thrust and uncommanded thrust change
cdRows.finding: Engine parameter data is output to the avionics display system; the FADEC protects against overspeed and overtemperature without crew intervention.

cdRows.supports: Preventing inadvertent or uncommanded reverse thrust in flight
cdRows.finding: Reverser deployment is inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement, with a mechanical lock at the translating sleeve.

cdRows.supports: Detecting loss of fuel delivery pressure and lateral fuel imbalance
cdRows.finding: Low-pressure and imbalance discretes are output to the flight deck; fuel imbalance is annunciated at 1,200 kg and limited structurally to 3,000 kg.

cdRows.item: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation selection
cdRows.supports: Intervening in fuel mass management and delivery when automatic scheduling is inadequate
cdRows.finding: The system is normally automatic; the crew can select manual cross-feed and can isolate any tank.

cdRows.supports: Monitoring fuel mass distribution to detect distribution error
cdRows.finding: Tank quantity and temperature are output to the avionics; the document does not state a means to detect an undetected fuel mass distribution error.

cdRows.supports: Recovering flight, navigation and system information following display or processor loss
cdRows.finding: Any display unit can present any format; reversionary display selection is manual and network reconfiguration is automatic.

cdRows.supports: Providing attitude, airspeed and altitude for pitch and roll control after loss of primary displays
cdRows.finding: Standby attitude, airspeed and altitude are provided by an independent integrated standby instrument on the DC essential bus that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays.

saRows.element: Loss of a source (generator/bus) — bus reconfiguration is otherwise automatic and silent
saRows.cue: Source-loss annunciation on the crew alerting list; battery-only remaining endurance displayed

saRows.element: Wing fuel imbalance between left and right wings
saRows.cue: Imbalance annunciated at 1,200 kg; imbalance discrete to the flight deck

saRows.element: Erroneous or undetected fuel mass distribution given normally automatic transfer/cross-feed
saRows.finding: Transfer and cross-feed are scheduled automatically without crew action; documents describe imbalance annunciation and low-pressure discretes but no cue specific to an undetected distribution error is described

saRows.element: Engine fuel low-pressure condition (partial/complete loss of fuel delivery)
saRows.cue: Low-pressure discretes to the flight deck

saRows.element: Degraded flight control law following loss of command paths
saRows.cue: Degraded laws are annunciated; flight envelope protection status to the avionics displays

saRows.element: Surface asymmetry or jam affecting roll/pitch control authority
saRows.cue: Asymmetry and jam discretes; surface position and system status to the avionics displays

saRows.element: Reversion to mechanical control (all three flight control computers lost)
saRows.finding: Reversion to mechanical control is not a selectable mode and results from loss of all electrical command paths; documents describe degraded-law annunciation but do not describe a dedicated cue for the reversion state itself

saRows.element: Uncommanded reverse thrust in flight — reverser deployment is inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement
saRows.finding: Documents describe the in-flight deployment inhibit and mechanical translating-sleeve lock but do not describe a flight-deck cue that annunciates an uncommanded reverse thrust condition

saRows.element: Thrust levels and engine parameters across four engines (symmetric/asymmetric thrust loss)
saRows.cue: Engine parameter data to the avionics display system; fire and overheat discretes to the flight deck

hfaRows.text: Loss of thrust from all four engines is not recoverable by crew action and results in hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The SDD gives the one-engine-inop dispatch case and a mature-engine IFSD rate but does not state the all-four-engine loss outcome; I credited hull loss as not recoverable. A demonstrated glide/restart capability or an independent thrust source would move this — confirm against the propulsion architecture.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An uncommanded or erroneous thrust event is detectable by the crew via engine parameter display and counterable within available time, and its magnitude is bounded such that it does not exceed available directional-control authority at the outboard moment arm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An in-flight inboard-engine thrust-reverser deployment at operating speed exceeds the aircraft's controllable envelope and is credited as loss of the airplane.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Wheel braking (dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator reserve) plus the 1,800 m/~1,080 m margin keep loss of reverse thrust within stopping margin on the semi-prepared surface, so reverse thrust is not credited to meet the landing-distance requirement.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Asymmetric reverse thrust on one inboard engine during the landing roll can be arrested by nose-wheel steering and differential braking without a runway excursion on the semi-prepared surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Complete loss of fuel delivery starves all four engines simultaneously (the APU cannot sustain flight), giving total loss of thrust rather than a single-engine loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: After a single-engine fuel-delivery loss, cross-feed/collector reserve restores the affected engine or the aircraft safely continues three-engine to a suitable aerodrome.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Erroneous fuel delivery pressure is annunciated and bounded to a single engine, not a common multi-engine condition acting through the shared cross-feed gallery.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Manual cross-feed and tank isolation, cued by the 1,200 kg imbalance annunciation, reliably arrest CG and wing-bending migration before the 3,000 kg structural limit.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No passengers are carried in flight; the hold is unoccupied, so occupant effects are none for every fuel failure condition.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss of the wing-imbalance annunciation is credible and, when it occurs, the imbalance can progress past the 3,000 kg structural limit before other cues prompt crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No usable roll control remains from other means (e.g. differential thrust across the four engines) after complete loss of ailerons and spoilers.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected erroneous or uncommanded roll develops into an unrecoverable roll departure before the crew can detect and arrest it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An aware erroneous or uncommanded roll is detectable from aircraft motion and displays and arrestable by crew corrective input, holding effects at a significant (not large) reduction in safety margins.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The mechanical reversion path provides pitch control only via stabiliser trim, so a complete loss of pitch control means every pitch means (elevators, stabiliser, and reversion) is unavailable together.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The flight crew can detect an erroneous or uncommanded pitch response and revert to a degraded control law or mechanical stabiliser trim in time to arrest divergence in the aware cases.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No independent FCS monitor reliably annunciates an erroneous pitch command in the undetected case, so no crew action is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Residual pitch authority in the within-MAC partial loss is sufficient to continue and land, while the outside-MAC partial loss cannot assure recovery.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight and the aircraft carries flight crew only, so occupant effects below hull loss are limited to the flight crew.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The outboard-engine-out case at the 28 m moment arm is the design-critical directional-control condition, so total loss of yaw prevents continued safe flight and landing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected uncommanded pitch excursion grows unchecked because crew alerting is absent, and the credited worst-phase outcome is Hazardous rather than unrecoverable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Erroneous and partial-authority yaw malfunctions are magnitude-limited (by FCS command monitoring and split-segment authority) so the worst credited outcome is a recoverable large-margin loss, not hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: No occupants other than flight crew are aboard in any flight phase, so the occupant axis never drives the class above the crew/aircraft axes.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold is unoccupied in flight, so occupant-injury effects reduce to crew fatalities on hull loss and there are no passengers to injure short of hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Uncommanded/erroneous yaw at the outboard 28 m moment arm can produce a large directional excursion that is arrestable by the crew when detected but unrecoverable when undetected.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A landing at the semi-prepared destination cannot be diverted to a longer commercial runway once committed, so degraded landing performance is assessed against the 1,800 m field length.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The asymmetry brakes at each high-lift section arrest an asymmetric deployment before the resulting rolling moment exceeds recoverable roll authority near the ground.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Without asymmetry annunciation the crew detect an asymmetric high-lift deployment only from aircraft response and therefore respond late during the takeoff/approach/landing phases.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Complete loss of ground load support occurs under weight at touchdown or on the ground roll and is not recoverable by crew action, producing hull loss.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The free-fall alternate extension is independent of the normal system-A hydraulic extension path and can be credited as a second means of getting the gear locked down.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial-gear landing on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip remains controllable without hull loss for the leg/bogie loss combinations of interest.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A credible uncommanded-retraction path exists with weight on wheels (no positive retraction inhibit stated), producing ground collapse.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An erroneous gear-position indication can, in the undetected case, defeat both dissimilar downlock sensing means so the crew reach touchdown unaware of the true configuration.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The Aeolus HL-1 hold is unoccupied in flight, so ground-deceleration failures expose only the two-to-four flight crew, not passengers.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The credited deceleration margin is the ~720 m difference between the 1,800 m landing-distance requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout on the design semi-prepared surface.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Directional control on the semi-prepared surface (nose-wheel steering, rudder, per-wheel-pair anti-skid) may not reliably arrest a braking-induced excursion, so an excursion is credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Rudder and differential/asymmetric braking provide adequate directional control on the ground roll after loss of nose-wheel steering on the 1,800 m semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The crew can detect and counter an uncommanded or erroneous steering deviation with rudder and differential braking before an unrecoverable runway excursion at take-off/landing ground-roll speed on the semi-prepared strip.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Ground steering is exercised on the ground roll phases only and has no in-flight effect (steering is a ground function).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The nose visor cannot be commanded to open or unlock in flight; operation is a ground-only function.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The pressure interlock (vents and confirms residual differential below 0.1 psi before the lock actuator will run) is not credited as removing the in-flight catastrophic class at AFHA stage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Loss of latching and locking that persists into flight leaves the closed door structurally unsecured, i.e. the latches/pins are a required in-flight structural securing means.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Dual dissimilar lock sensing and the take-off configuration check are assumed to detect an unlocked/unsecured visor before flight but are not credited as fully eliminating the undetected in-flight case at AFHA stage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial loss of latching/locking leaves enough of the twelve latches and eight pins engaged to retain the pressure boundary and is detected pre-flight by lock sensing and the take-off configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The pressure interlock and the no-in-flight-operation inhibit are independent of any cause that could inadvertently command unlock, so an inadvertent unlock cannot breach the boundary in flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected complete loss of latching and locking permits the visor to depart in flight and is not recoverable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A single surviving dissimilar sensing path is sufficient to confirm lock status and complete the take-off configuration check.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The take-off configuration monitor and flight deck rely on the SF-015 lock indication such that an erroneous or undetected-erroneous indication degrades assurance of nose-door lock/pressure-boundary state.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A complete or inadvertent full loss of restraint of the single 72.6 t blade in flight produces an uncontrollable CG/structural excursion not recoverable by crew action.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Partial loss of restraint stays bounded to a level the neighbouring strap load paths carry, and does not progress to loss of the blade before landing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An inadvertent release event affects enough straps/saddles to be equivalent to loss of restraint rather than a single bounded strap release.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A fully released 72.6 t blade shifts far enough to drive the CG outside the recoverable envelope before the crew can respond, and no in-flight means exists to arrest it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected single-station strap degradation is carried by neighbouring straps and does not progress to a multi-station loss or blade shift within one flight.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Erroneous restraint tension indication is itself detectable as misleading and does not silently mask a progressing restraint failure through to blade shift.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: An undetected slackening or masked strap on the single-loop restraint monitor cannot progress to a payload shift or CG excursion that reaches a hazardous structural or flight-safety limit before landing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: After total loss of air conditioning and distribution the flight-deck environment stays survivable long enough for the crew to descend and divert within the FL260 operating ceiling.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The erroneous air-conditioning mode manifests as a flight-deck environment degradation the crew can arrest by pack/bleed reconfiguration or manual mode, not as an uncorrectable environment excursion.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The flight-deck occupants are protected by four quick-donning crew oxygen masks adequate for an emergency descent from FL260.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The independent positive/negative pressure relief valves fully bound the maximum control-commanded over-pressure so structural rupture is not credited.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The cabin-altitude detection and alerting that would warn the crew of an under-pressure excursion is NOT fully independent of the erroneous ECS control channel.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The pressurisation architecture provides two controllers and two outflow valves with either valve sufficient, so a single-element partial loss leaves a redundant path.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The independent positive-pressure mechanical relief valves bound the over-pressure excursion below fuselage structural limits.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The hold pressurisation differential is the preliminary low value (~8,800 m equivalent) rather than a frozen higher value.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The crew can detect degraded/lost ice protection and exit the icing envelope before accretion or air-data loss becomes uncontrollable.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Redundant air data inertial reference units do not protect against common icing of the sensed probes feeding all references.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial loss of surface/inlet ice protection is a bounded, annunciated degradation (single zone or single-side bleed) leaving adequate protection.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: A partial or uncommanded probe/windshield protection failure leaves at least one valid, crew-detectable air-data path via the three dissimilar reference units and independent standby instrument.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The independent standby instrument's air data does not depend on probes rendered unusable by the same undetected probe-heat loss in icing.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: Ice protection remains fully available and manually selectable when automatic ice accretion detection is completely lost.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: The flight crew is the only occupant set; the hold is unoccupied in flight, so no passenger safety effects arise for any row.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm
