hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a single-station undetected strap loss is carried by neighbours without progressing to blade shift within one flight (SDD: 'loss of any one strap is carried by its neighbours'). If an undetected partial loss can propagate to a multi-station / blade-shift condition before the next inspection, the class rises toward Hazardous/Catastrophic — substantiate with restraint load-path and progression analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a fully released 72.6 t blade shifts far enough to drive the CG outside the recoverable envelope before any crew response, and that no in-flight means exists to arrest it (SDD: 'In flight the crew has indication only; there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint'). If blade travel is mechanically limited by saddle geometry to a recoverable excursion, the class may reduce — substantiate with blade-shift dynamics and CG-envelope analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed erroneous indication is annunciated/detectable as misleading (aware case) and does not itself precipitate an undetected restraint failure; a false-normal indication that masks a progressing restraint loss until blade shift occurs would couple into the SF-016-M2 Catastrophic outcome — the combination should be examined in CMA and the SFHA.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on whether an undetected slackening strap can progress to a payload shift or CG excursion that reaches a structural or flight-safety limit before landing; the SDD states single-loop monitoring and neighbour load-sharing but does not quantify how far degradation can go undetected. Assumed Major (latent monitoring loss, restraint still held by design). A restraint fault-tree / structural analysis showing an undetected strap loss cannot reach a hazardous shift would confirm Major; evidence it can would raise it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Same driving fact as SF-017-TL2: whether a masked slack strap can reach a hazardous payload shift or CG limit before landing. SDD gives single-loop monitoring with neighbour load-sharing but no undetected-degradation bound. Assumed Major; a structural/restraint analysis bounding the undetected shift would confirm or raise it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Class turns on whether the flight-deck environment after total conditioning loss stays survivable long enough for descent/diversion at FL260, and on the pressurisation coupling; the SDD confirms low differential, no hold occupants and a low ceiling but does not give a time-to-limit. Assumed Major (descent/diversion within capability). Environmental-endurance analysis or a coupled ECS/pressurisation showing a rapid cabin-altitude excursion could raise it toward Hazardous.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — The FCIM names a single lumped 'erroneous' mode without specifying whether it manifests as a benign temperature error (recoverable by pack reconfig) or a more severe environment excursion; the SDD gives manual mode and pack/bleed selection as available responses but no worst-case erroneous-conditioning limit. Assumed Major (crew-recoverable environment degradation). A benign, self-limited temperature error would drop to Minor; an environment excursion the crew cannot correct would raise it.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on the crew detecting depressurisation and donning oxygen in time; the SDD credits masks fed the ECS cabin-altitude signal and FL260 ceiling. If time-of-useful-consciousness margin at the actual hold/flight-deck altitude proves inadequate, or detection is delayed, this rises toward Hazardous — confirm crew-oxygen adequacy and alerting response time.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Depends on the under-pressure being detected and the crew acting in time; SDD credits the ECS cabin-altitude alert and crew oxygen at FL260. If detection is unreliable this converges with the undetected case (M3); confirm alerting coverage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the independent positive relief valve fully bounds over-pressure so structural rupture is not credited; SDD states relief "independently of the control system". If relief valve capacity is inadequate for the maximum erroneous demand this rises toward Hazardous/Catastrophic — confirm relief sizing against the worst-case control-commanded differential.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the cabin-altitude detection/alert that would warn the crew is independent of the erroneous ECS control channel. The SDD shows ECS supplies the cabin-altitude signal to the crew-oxygen logic, so a common ECS fault could defeat the cue — assumed here, giving Hazardous. If an independent cabin-altitude sensor annunciates regardless of the ECS control fault, this reduces to the detected M case (Major). Confirm the independence of cabin-altitude sensing/alerting from the pressurisation control channel.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on the hold pressurisation differential (preliminary, ~8,800 m equivalent) and on the relief valves capping the excursion below structural limits; if the relief valves do not bound the over-pressure to a non-hazardous level, or the residual differential is set higher when frozen, the class rises toward Hazardous. Confirm relief-valve setting margin against structural limits.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the crew can detect (detection function available) and exit the icing envelope before accretion becomes uncontrollable; the SDD gives no icing exposure time or degraded-handling data. If the envelope cannot be exited in time in a foreseeable operating condition, the accreted-ice handling loss could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm icing-envelope exposure and degraded handling analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the degradation is a bounded partial (single zone / single-side bleed) that is annunciated and leaves adequate protection for the encountered envelope; the SDD does not quantify the protected fraction retained. If a partial loss removes protection from a flight-critical surface in the envelope, the class rises. Confirm minimum protected configuration.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes probe/element loss is individually monitored so the crew are alerted and can exit the icing envelope, and that redundant ADIRUs do not protect against a common icing of the sensed probes. The SDD gives no icing exposure or unreliable-airspeed procedure data. If probe icing produces undetected misleading air data feeding all references, the condition could progress to Catastrophic. Confirm probe redundancy/heating monitoring and unreliable-airspeed handling.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes a partial loss leaves at least one valid air-data/vision path per the three ADIRUs and individual zone monitoring; if a partial loss can silently corrupt all primary airspeed sources this rises toward Major/Hazardous. Confirm which sensors a partial loss can affect together.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes erroneous protection produces degraded but crew-detectable air data with the independent standby instrument available for reversion; if it can drive undetected consistent misleading airspeed across the primaries this is Hazardous. Confirm sensor-to-air-data mapping and comparator coverage.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes uncommanded heating does not damage the sensing element or corrupt air data before deselection; if sustained inadvertent probe heating can bias the measured value this rises to Major. Confirm element thermal design margins and any air-data bias effect.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the undetected loss can affect enough probes to yield misleading primary air data in the icing envelope before the independent standby instrument (if unaffected) resolves it; if independent air-data integrity is assured despite the undetected loss this is Major. Confirm whether the standby path shares probe heating and whether comparator monitors detect the ice-induced degradation.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Applies the §5.4.2 loss-of-annunciation default (Major) because detection is advisory and manual protection selection remains; if the crew cannot otherwise recognise icing and unprotected accretion follows, the combined condition could be more severe. Confirm alternate icing cues and any auto-on logic dependency on the detectors.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the second identical detector plus manual-on capability keep icing recognition adequate after partial loss; the two detectors are the same type (recorded commonality item), so if the loss is a common-mode degradation affecting recognition confidence in both, severity would rise. Confirm detector independence and crew procedure for degraded detection.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes erroneous detection is recognisable and does not mask a genuine icing encounter that goes unprotected; a failure that reads 'no ice' when ice is present (misleading toward no-protection) could be more severe than one reading a false positive. Confirm which erroneous direction is credited and whether crew can independently confirm accretion.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the loss is truly unannunciated and that crew recognition of icing from other cues occurs late enough to allow meaningful unprotected accretion within the icing envelope; if a monitor annunciates the detection loss, or manual protection is habitually selected on entering known icing regardless of detector state, severity reduces toward Minor. Confirm detection-loss monitoring and icing-entry procedure.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on the crew detecting the erroneous display via independent flight information and reverting in time; the SDD provides an independent standby instrument sharing no supply/sensor/processing (§5.11.3), supporting detectability. If detection cannot be credited at aircraft level this migrates toward the undetected case (SF-023-M2). Confirm crediting of an independent cross-check at aircraft-function level.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether ANY independent source remains that could eventually reveal the error before an unrecoverable state; if no independent cross-check exists at all the class rises to Catastrophic. The three-ADIRU / independent standby architecture (§5.11) argues an independent source persists, holding this at Hazardous. Confirm no single common source drives all displays simultaneously with a plausible, non-detectable error.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on an independent standby means surviving the same event; the SDD states standby attitude/airspeed/altitude on the DC essential bus sharing no supply/sensor/processing with the primaries (§5.11.2–3), so total loss of the three reference units still leaves standby — holding this at Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If the standby shares a common failure path with the reference units the class rises. Confirm standby independence at aircraft level.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on how much of the function is lost in the partial case; classified for loss of one of the three reference units leaving two valid. If 'partial' were taken to mean loss of two of three (leaving one), the class would approach the total-loss/Hazardous end. Confirm the intended partial-loss depth for this row.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether the three-reference architecture detects/outvotes an erroneous source before it misleads the crew or the flight control law; a robust voting/comparison scheme holds this at Hazardous, while an undetected common erroneous source across sources approaches Catastrophic. The FCS consumes air data/inertial data via the avionics (§5.3.4), so erroneous reference has a flight-control path. Confirm the detection/voting credit at aircraft level.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether a comparator/annunciation reliably flags the undetected ADIRU disagreement to the crew in time; the SDD gives three reference units and an independent standby but does not state comparator/voting coverage that self-detects a single erroneous unit. If a validated cross-comparison alerts the crew, this could reduce toward Major; if two units can agree erroneously with no alert, Catastrophic is possible. Confirm with the AVI comparator design and crew-detection HF analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — How many standby parameters are lost is not specified; loss of a single parameter with primaries intact could be Minor. Assumed a degraded standby still constitutes a significant loss of the independent backup layer, hence Major; confirm the standby architecture (single integrated unit per §5.11.2 implies partial degradation is unlikely without total loss).
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the crew resolves the standby-vs-primary disagreement in favour of the primaries; that resolution is reasonable given the primaries carry three reference units against a single standby, but a validated HF/annunciation basis is not stated. If an erroneous standby could be trusted during a concurrent primary degradation, severity rises. Confirm with the AVI source-selection and alerting design.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Alerting is driven by two independent processing channels (§5.11.2), so complete loss requires both channels lost; whether residual dedicated warnings (e.g. fire handles, standby annunciators) remain to bound the effect is not fully stated. Assumed the consolidated alert list is the primary detection means whose total loss is Hazardous per §5.4.2 combination logic; confirm residual independent warning coverage and the un-annunciated combination objective.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed partial loss removes a bounded subset of alerts while the remaining list and direct indications stay available; if a partial loss can silence a catastrophic-linked alert whose detection has no independent means, the class rises. The alert catalogue and its coupling to failure conditions would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the erroneous alert is detectable by cross-check against independent system indications and the wrong procedure is not itself hazardous to execute. If an erroneous alert could drive a crew action that is catastrophic (e.g. false engine-fire prompting shutdown of a good engine near V1) with no independent cue, the class rises to Hazardous. The alert-to-procedure mapping would settle this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed a spurious alert does not by itself command any automatic aircraft response and remains crew-recognisable. If the alert catalogue includes a spurious alert whose associated procedure, if erroneously actioned, degrades a critical function (e.g. spurious fire alert leading to engine shutdown), the class rises. The alert catalogue and any auto-response linkage would confirm this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed the undetected subset can include alerts for conditions whose only credited detection is the alert list, so silence leaves the crew with no cue. If every function in the affected subset retains an independent direct indication the crew habitually monitor, the class falls to Major. The alerting architecture's dual-channel monitoring coverage (§5.11.2, two independent channels) and the alert-to-function map would settle this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumed an undetected erroneous alert can misdirect crew into or out of a safety-critical action but not directly command a catastrophic outcome without any subsequent cue. If the mapped procedure for a plausible erroneous alert is itself catastrophic to execute with no recovery cue, the class rises to Catastrophic. The alert-to-procedure map and the dual-channel comparison monitoring (§5.11.2) would confirm or overturn this.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether an actual fire coincident with total detection loss is credited within this single condition or handled as a combination. SDD gives dual-loop detection per zone and crew-commanded extinguishing but no probability data; if the coincident fire is credited the class moves to Catastrophic. Fault-tree/combination analysis (FHA+CMA) and the hold-suppression substantiation would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether erroneous detection can present as a false 'no-fire' during a real event (masking) versus only a false 'fire' warning. SDD states dual-loop AND logic for warning but does not describe cross-monitoring that would reject a stuck-clear loop; if masking is precluded by design the class reduces to Major. Detailed system FMEA of the detection logic would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Latent-plus-fire combination: if the coincident fire is credited within this condition the class is Catastrophic (undetected fire to hull loss); if the latent loss is treated in isolation with the fire handled as a separate combined event, Hazardous holds. Depends on whether the detection loss is self-monitored/annunciated — SDD does not state built-in monitoring of loop integrity. §25.4 significant-latent-failure treatment and CMA would confirm.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes erroneous delivery is detectable via status indication and worked around (crossover / per-mask regulators / mask-off breathing tolerable at FL260) before it incapacitates a crew member. If erroneous delivery can silently deliver a contaminated or oxygen-deficient supply to all masks during a depressurisation, undetected, the crew axis rises to fatalities or incapacitation and the class to Hazardous or Catastrophic — an FMEA of the delivery/manifold and a smoke/fume + depressurisation scenario would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed exceeds the aircraft's recoverable envelope (credited as hull loss). If FCS controllability analysis demonstrates the aircraft is controllable through a single inboard reverser-in-flight deployment across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. The multi-layer inhibit (WOW + radio-altimeter agreement + mechanical sleeve lock) bears on likelihood/architecture, not on the classified severity of the effect. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Same controllability assumption as SF-002-M: an uncommanded in-flight inboard reverser deployment at operating speed is credited as exceeding the recoverable envelope (hull loss). If FCS analysis shows the aircraft is controllable through this event across the envelope, this reduces to Hazardous. Confirm from FCS in-flight-reverser controllability analysis.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether any residual lateral control (e.g. differential thrust from the four engines, or rudder-induced roll) can be credited to make the flight recoverable; the SDD gives no roll authority from other means, so complete loss of both aileron and spoiler roll is assumed unrecoverable. Confirm whether differential thrust provides usable roll control in the FCS SFHA — if credited, the aircraft axis and class could be reduced.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes an inadvertent release affects enough of the restraint (multiple straps/saddles) to be equivalent to loss of restraint; if a single inadvertent release is bounded by the mechanical lock and neighbour load paths to a partial degradation, the class reduces toward the SF-016-PL Major level. The release-command architecture and how many independent releases are needed to unrestrain the blade would confirm or overturn.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes the independent standby instrument remains available on total loss of the primary display chain (it shares no supply/sensor/processing per §5.11.3) and provides a survivable but degraded means to fly and land, keeping the condition Hazardous rather than Catastrophic. If total display loss can occur concurrently with, or take out, the standby means, the condition becomes Catastrophic. Confirm the standby instrument's independence holds under the credited total-loss cause and quantify partial-panel approach/landing capability in IMC.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on whether a detected nacelle/APU fire, with extinguishing lost, is reliably controllable by engine shutdown + fuel isolation before propagation to structure. Assumed controllable-but-degraded (Hazardous). Firewall integrity substantiation and fire-propagation timing would confirm; evidence that shutdown does not arrest the fire would move this to Catastrophic.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes 'partial' leaves at least one usable discharge into the affected zone (cross-plumbed two-bottle-per-pair architecture). If the partial loss instead removes all agent from a single nacelle with no cross-feed to it, that nacelle's classification approaches the complete-loss (Hazardous) case; the specific partial state needs definition.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Assumes inadvertent discharge is of one bottle and does not itself create a hazard (agent release into an unmanned nacelle). If a spurious discharge is coincident with a real fire in the same pair, the residual capacity is reduced — that combination is a CMA/combination item, not this single-condition row.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm

hfaRows.text: JUDGEMENT CALL (limited information) — Turns on the combination: total oxygen loss is benign in isolation but Hazardous when coincident with depressurisation at FL260 or a smoke event. Cylinder pressure is a displayed dispatch item, so total loss is normally detected on the ground; an in-flight latent total loss coincident with a pressurisation event is the sizing case. If the combination is shown extremely improbable and detected, the isolated-condition classification is lower; DER disposition and CMA needed.
hfaRows.origin: AI-declared while drafting the AFHA (claude-opus-4-8) — confirm
